01Chapter 1 · Introduction to MLOps

Introduction to MLOps

Machine learning ka model notebook mein achha chal jaaye, ye kaafi nahi hai — asli kaam tab shuru hota hai jab model production mein jaata hai, wahan tikta hai, aur business ko fayda deta hai. Ye chapter isi baat se shuru hota hai ki ML engineering ki success kaise naapi jaaye, aur MLOps kyun zaroori ho gaya hai.

Success kaise naapein — model count ya business ROI?

Ek organisation mein ML initiative ki success naapne ke do tareeke hain. Pehla, kitne ML models production mein gaye. Dusra, un models ka business ROI par kya asar pada. In dono ke peeche ek aur cheez chhupi hai — model ki operational efficiency, matlab uski cost, uptime, aur use maintain karne ke liye kitne log chahiye. Agar model ban gaya lekin use chalana mehenga hai, baar-baar down hota hai, ya maintain karne mein poori team lag jaati hai, to wo project fail hone ki taraf ja raha hai.

Advanced technology organisations ye samajh gayi hain ki ML projects ke fail hone ka risk kam karne ke liye sahi methodologies aur tools chahiye. Isliye MLOps sirf ek buzzword nahi hai, ye ek zaroorat hai. Model banana ek kaam hai, aur model ko reliably chalana bilkul alag aur bada kaam hai.

ML aur cloud ka gehra rishta

Machine learning ka ek clear pattern hai — ye cloud computing se bahut gehre tareeke se juda hai. Kyunki ML ke raw ingredients hain massive compute, extensive data, aur specialized hardware. Ye teeno cheezein cloud par naturally milti hain. Isliye cloud platforms ne ML ko operationalize karne ke liye specialized platforms bhi banaye hain.

Tools aur platforms ki partial list ye hai: cloud native ML platforms jaise AWS SageMaker, Azure ML Studio, aur GCP AI Platform; containerized workflows jaise Docker format containers, Kubernetes, aur private aur public container registries; serverless technology jaise AWS Lambda, AWS Athena, Google Cloud Functions, Azure Functions; specialized hardware jaise GPUs, Google TPU, Apple A14, AWS Inferentia; elastic inference; aur big data platforms jaise Databricks, Hadoop/Spark, Snowflake, Amazon EMR, Google BigQuery. Matlab agar tum ML engineering kar rahe ho, to bahut likely tum ye cloud par hi kar rahe ho.

Rule of 25% — chaar cheezein barabar zaroori

Chapter ke end mein ek bahut achhi soch di gayi hai — Rule of 25%. Software engineering, data engineering, modeling, aur business problem — ye chaaro equally important hain, har ek 25%. Sirf model achha bana lena kaafi nahi hai. Agar software engineering kamzor hai to model deploy nahi hoga, agar data engineering kamzor hai to data hi nahi milega, aur agar business problem samjha hi nahi to model kis kaam ka?

Is rule ko follow karne wale products ke examples hain Tesla ki cars — semi-autonomous vehicles, constant software updates, aur naye data se model continuously train hota rehta hai — aur Amazon Alexa device. Dono mein chaaro hisse saath-saath kaam karte hain. MLOps ka multidisciplinary hona hi use tough banata hai, lekin yehi uski taakat bhi hai.

Bookshelf vs ped (tree) — MLOps ek living system hai

Ek aur sundar analogy chapter mein di gayi hai: bookshelf banana aur ped ugana alag cheezein hain. Bookshelf mein pehle design karo, phir ek baar build karo, kaam khatam. Lekin ML wala complex software system ped ki tarah hai — use grow karne ke liye multiple dynamic inputs chahiye: mitti, paani, hawa, aur dhoop. Matlab model ek baar deploy karke bhool nahi sakte; use data, monitoring, retraining aur feedback ki zaroorat hamesha rehti hai.

Yaad rakho: Model banana sirf 25% kaam hai. Software engineering, data engineering, modeling aur business problem — chaaro barabar zaroori hain. Production mein model ki cost, uptime aur maintenance hi uski asli success batate hain.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Introduction to MLOps

01.1Chapter 1 · Introduction to MLOps

Rise of the Machine Learning Engineer and MLOps

Machine learning engineer ek naya role kyun ban gaya? Kyunki model banana aur model ko production mein chalana, ye do alag skills hain — aur dono ke beech mein ek bada gap tha. Isi gap ko bharne ke liye ML engineer aur MLOps ubhre hain.

Model production mein kyun nahi pahunchte?

Ye chapter ka sabse important sawaal hai. Technology to hai — Covid ka rapid detection, mask vs non-mask computer vision solutions, faster drug discovery — ye sab possible hai, phir bhi ye solutions real world mein available kyun nahi hain? Jawab ye hai ki problem model banane mein nahi hai, problem uske aas-paas ki cheezon mein hai: data engineering, data processing, problem feasibility, aur business alignment.

Ek issue ye bhi hai ki bahut zyada focus code aur technical details par hota hai, business problem solve karne par nahi. Dusra issue hai automation ki kami, aur teesra hai HiPPO culture — Highest Paid Person's Opinions — matlab sabse bade aadmi ki rai se decisions lena, data se nahi. Aur bahut saara ML abhi bhi cloud native nahi hai; academic datasets aur academic software packages use hote hain jo large-scale problems par scale nahi karte.

Kaizen — chhote-chhote sudhaar, roz

Isi jagah Kaizen ka concept aata hai. Japanese mein Kaizen ka matlab hai improvement. Ye software management philosophy Japanese automobile industry mein World War II ke baad shuru hui thi. Iske neeche kai techniques aati hain: Kanban, root cause analysis aur five whys, aur Six Sigma. Kaizen practice karne ke liye duniya ki sahi aur realistic assessment zaroori hai, aur phir excellence ke liye roz chhote incremental improvements karte rehna hota hai.

Feedback loop jitna tez hoga, utna zyada time business problems par focus karne ko milega. Agar har chhoti cheez mein manual kaam laga rahega, to business problem par sochne ka time hi nahi bachega. Isliye MLOps ka pehla kaam hai feedback loop ko tez karna.

ML engineer kaun hota hai?

Jo log machine learning applications ko operationalize karte hain aur build karte hain, wo machine learning engineers aur data engineers hote hain. Ye role sirf model train karne wala nahi hai — ye wo hai jo model ko software system ki tarah treat karta hai, use deploy karta hai, monitor karta hai, aur improve karta hai. Aage chapter mein jo MLOps hierarchy of needs aayegi, usmein ye role har layer par kaam karta hai.

Ye rise achanak nahi hua. Jaise software industry ne DevOps ko apnaya tha apne similar issues solve karne ke liye, waise hi ab ML community MLOps ko apna rahi hai. Data science industry abhi immature hai production ke mamle mein — model notebook mein achha hai, lekin production mein le jaana ek alag discipline hai.

Yaad rakho: Model na pahunchne ki wajah modeling nahi, uske aas-paas ka kaam hai — data engineering, automation ki kami, HiPPO culture, aur business alignment. Kaizen matlab roz chhota sudhaar, aur tez feedback loop hi MLOps ki neev hai.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Introduction to MLOps

01.2Chapter 1 · Introduction to MLOps

What Is MLOps?

MLOps ka matlab hai machine learning ko DevOps methodologies use karke automate karna. Simple shabdon mein — ML system ke har hisse se manual kaam hatao, aur use ek repeatable, automated pipeline banao.

DevOps se lineage — agar automate nahi hai to toota hua hai

MLOps ki lineage DevOps se aati hai. DevOps philosophically automation maangta hai. Ek common expression hai — agar ye automated nahi hai, to ye toota hua hai. MLOps mein bhi system ka koi component aisa nahi hona chahiye jahan human hi machine ka lever ho. Automation ka history batata hai ki humans repetitive tasks karne mein sabse kam valuable hote hain, lekin technology ke architects aur practitioners ke roop mein sabse zyada valuable hote hain.

Isi tarah developers, models, aur operations ke beech coordination transparent teamwork aur healthy collaboration se honi chahiye. MLOps sirf tools ka naam nahi hai, ye ek tareeka hai kaam karne ka — automation aur collaboration dono.

DevOps kya hai?

DevOps best practices ka combination hai — microservices, continuous integration, aur continuous delivery — jo Operations aur Development ke beech ki deewar ko hata deta hai. Python ismein predominant language hai — scripting, DevOps, aur machine learning, teeno mein. Isliye ye book bhi Python par focus karti hai.

DevOps ke benefits hain speed, reliability, scale, aur security. Ye benefits best practices follow karne se milte hain, aur MLOps inhi practices ko ML systems par extend karta hai.

DevOps ki best practices — ek nazar mein

  • Continuous integration (CI): Software project ko continuously test karna aur test results se quality improve karna. Automated testing hoti hai open source aur SaaS build servers se jaise GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab, CircleCI, ya cloud native build systems jaise AWS CodeBuild.
  • Continuous delivery (CD): Code ko bina human intervention ke naye environment mein deliver karna. Code changes automatically test aur deploy hote hain, aksar IaC ke through.
  • Microservices: Ek software service jiska ek distinct function ho aur dependencies bahut kam hon. Flask ek popular Python-based microservice framework hai. ML prediction endpoint microservice ke liye perfect fit hai. Ye FaaS jaise AWS Lambda par bhi chal sakta hai, ya CaaS par jaise AWS Fargate, Google Cloud Run, ya Azure App Services par Dockerfile se Flask app deploy karke.
  • Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Infrastructure ko source code repository mein check karna aur deploy karke changes push karna. Isse idempotent behavior milta hai aur infrastructure banane ke liye humans ki zaroorat nahi padti. Examples hain AWS CloudFormation, AWS SAM, aur multicloud options Pulumi aur Terraform.
  • Monitoring aur instrumentation: Logging aur tools jaise New Relic, Datadog, ya Stackdriver se application ke behavior ka data collect karna, taaki performance aur reliability par decisions liye ja sakein. Yehi woh jagah hai jahan Kaizen kaam aata hai — data-driven organisation is instrumentation se roz ya har hafte cheezein behtar karti hai.
  • Effective technical communication: Repeatable aur efficient communication methods banana. Example — AutoML ko initial prototyping ke liye adopt karna. Ho sakta hai AutoML model aakhir mein rakha jaaye ya discard kar diya jaaye, lekin automation ek informational tool ki tarah kaam karta hai jo intractable problem par kaam karne se bachata hai.
  • Effective technical project management: Human aur technology solutions jaise ticket systems aur spreadsheets se project manage karna, aur problems ko chhote-chhote chunks mein todna taaki incremental progress ho. ML mein antipattern ye hai ki team ek production model par kaam kare jo problem ko perfectly solve kare. Iske bajaye roz ya har hafte chhoti wins deliver karna zyada scalable aur samajhdar tareeka hai.

MLOps mein kya extra hai?

MLOps mein sirf software engineering processes hi fully automate nahi hone chahiye, data aur modeling bhi automate hone chahiye. Model training aur deployment ek naya wrinkle hai jo traditional DevOps lifecycle mein add hota hai. Aur monitoring aur instrumentation mein nayi cheezein bhi account karni padti hain jo toot sakti hain — jaise data drift, matlab last training ke baad se data mein jo changes aaye hain, unka delta.

CI aur CD DevOps ke do sabse critical pillars hain. CI mein code source control repository mein merge hota hai jo automatically testing se code ki quality check karta hai. CD mein code changes automatically test aur deploy hote hain, staging ya production mein. Dono hi automation ke forms hain, Kaizen ya continuous improvement ki spirit mein.

CI/CD kiski zimmedari hai?

Achha sawaal hai — team mein CI/CD kaun implement kare? Ye waise hi hai jaise poochna ki democracy mein taxes kaun deta hai. Taxes se roads, bridges, law enforcement, emergency services, schools aur dusri infrastructure banti hai, isliye sabko contribute karna padta hai. Waise hi saare MLOps team members ko CI/CD system develop aur maintain karne mein madad karni chahiye. Ek well-maintained CI/CD system team aur company ke future mein investment hai.

Yaad rakho: MLOps matlab DevOps methodologies se ML ko automate karna. Agar automate nahi hai to toota hua hai. Aur data drift — training ke baad data ka badalna — ek aisi nayi cheez hai jo sirf ML systems mein monitor karni padti hai.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Introduction to MLOps

01.3Chapter 1 · Introduction to MLOps

An MLOps Hierarchy of Needs

Maslow ki hierarchy of needs suna hoga — pehle survival ki basic needs, phir uske upar human potential. ML systems par bhi wahi concept lagta hai. Neeche ki layers ke bina upar ki layers khadi nahi ho sakti.

Maslow se ML hierarchy tak

Maslow ke pyramid mein neeche ke levels survival ko reflect karte hain, aur asli human potential tab aata hai jab basic survival aur emotional needs poori ho jaati hain. Wahi baat ML par lagti hai. Ek ML system ek software system hai, aur software systems efficiently aur reliably tab kaam karte hain jab DevOps aur data engineering ki best practices jagah par hon. Agar DevOps ki basic foundation hi nahi hai, ya data engineering fully automated nahi hai, to ML ka asli potential organisation tak kaise pahunchega?

ML hierarchy of needs definitive guide nahi hai, lekin discussion shuru karne ke liye ek excellent jagah hai. Is hierarchy ko samajhna zaroori hai kyunki ML projects ko rokne wali sabse badi cheez yehi necessary foundation hai.

Hierarchy ki layers — neeche se upar

  • DevOps (foundation): Sabse neeche DevOps hai. Bina automated testing ke DevOps mein aage badhna possible nahi hai. Continuous integration iski neev hai.
  • Data automation (DataOps / data engineering): Iske upar data ka automated flow hai. Bina data automation ke organisation reliably MLOps nahi kar sakti.
  • Platform automation: Phir aati hai high-level platforms se ML solutions banana — jaise SageMaker, Azure ML Studio, Google AI Platform, ya Kubeflow.
  • ML automation (MLOps): Sabse upar true ML automation hai, yaani MLOps. Iska culmination hai ek ML system jo kaam karta hai.

Order ulta nahi ho sakta. Pehle DevOps foundation complete karo, phir data automation, phir platform automation, aur phir finally MLOps possible hota hai. Bahut si teams seedha model par kood jaati hain aur phir hairan hoti hain ki production mein kuch kaam kyun nahi karta — jawab aksar neeche ki layers mein hota hai.

DataOps — paani wale gaon wali kahani

Data automation ko samjhane ke liye book mein ek sundar analogy hai. Imagine karo ek gaon jahan ek hi kuan paani ka source hai. Roz paani laane ke liye trips arrange karni padti hain, aur jo cheezein hum granted lete hain — on-demand hot showers, on-demand dishwashing, automated irrigation — wo kaam nahi karengi. Waise hi ek organisation jiske paas data ka automated flow nahi hai, wo reliably MLOps nahi kar sakti.

DataOps ke commercial tools evolve ho rahe hain. Example hai Apache Airflow — pehle ek company ne apne data processing jobs schedule aur monitor karne ke liye banaya, phir open source kar diya. AWS tools mein AWS Data Pipeline aur AWS Glue hain. AWS Glue ek serverless ETL (Extract, Load, Transform) tool hai jo data source ka schema detect karta hai aur uska metadata store karta hai. AWS Athena aur AWS QuickSight se data query aur visualize kiya ja sakta hai.

Yahan consider karne wali cheezein hain data ka size, information kitni frequently change hoti hai, aur data kitna clean hai. Bahut si organisations ek centralized data lake ko hub banati hain. Data lake helpful isliye hai kyunki ye near-infinite scale deta hai I/O mein, high durability aur availability ke saath. Data lake aksar cloud-based object storage jaise Amazon S3 ka synonym hota hai. Ye data processing in place karne deta hai, data ko move kiye bina.

Platform automation — SageMaker example

Jab data ka automated flow hai, to agla sawaal hai ki organisation high-level platforms se ML solutions kaise banaye. Agar organisation pehle se Amazon S3 data lake mein data collect kar rahi hai, to natural hai ki ML workflows Amazon SageMaker se jode. Google use karne wali organisation Google AI Platform use kar sakti hai, Azure wali Azure Machine Learning Studio, aur Kubernetes use karne wali Kubeflow.

SageMaker ka example dikhata hai ki kaise wo ek real-world ML problem ke liye complex MLOps sequence orchestrate karta hai — virtual machines spin up karna, S3 se read aur write karna, aur production endpoints provision karna. Ye infrastructure steps bina automation ke production scenario mein karna bewakoofi hogi. ML platform repeatability, scale, aur operationalization ki real-world problems solve karta hai.

MLOps — ek behavior hai, sirf job title nahi

Jab saari layers complete hain — DevOps, Data Automation, aur Platform Automation — tab MLOps possible hai. MLOps ek behavior hai, jaise DevOps ek behavior hai. Kuch log DevOps engineers ke roop mein kaam karte hain, lekin zyada baar software engineer DevOps best practices use karke tasks perform karta hai. Waise hi machine learning engineer ko MLOps best practices use karke ML systems banana chahiye.

MLOps DevOps practices par build karta hai aur kuch items ko extend karta hai taaki wo directly ML systems ko target karein. Isse reproducible models bante hain, robust model packaging, validation, aur deployment ke saath, aur model performance ko explain aur observe karne ki ability badhti hai.

MLOps feedback loop — chaar hisse

  • Reusable ML pipelines se models create aur retrain karo: Model ek baar banana kaafi nahi hai. Data badal sakta hai, customers badal sakte hain, model banane wale log badal sakte hain. Solution hai versioned, reusable ML pipelines.
  • ML models ki continuous delivery: Jaise software ki CD hoti hai, waise hi ML models ki bhi. Jab saare steps automated hain, IaC ke saath infrastructure bhi, to model kisi bhi time deploy ho sakta hai, production samet.
  • MLOps pipeline ke liye audit trail: ML models ke liye auditing critical hai. Security, bias, aur accuracy jaise problems ki kami nahi hai. Isliye helpful audit trail invaluable hai, jaise production software engineering mein adequate logging critical hai. Audit trail feedback loop ka hissa hai jahan tum apna approach aur actual problem dono ko continuously improve karte ho.
  • Model data drift observe karo aur future models improve karo: ML ki unique baat ye hai ki data literally model ke neeche shift ho sakta hai. Do saal pehle customers ke liye jo model kaam karta tha, wo aaj waise kaam nahi karega. Data drift monitor karke — last training se changes ka delta — accuracy problems ko production issues banne se pehle roka ja sakta hai.

Kahan deploy karein? Build once, deploy many

MLOps ka ek key aspect hai cloud native platform model banana aur use kai different targets par deploy karna. Build once aur deploy many times — ye modern ML operations ki critical feature hai. Ek taraf elastically scale hone wala HTTP endpoint typical pattern hai, lekin ye eklauta tareeka nahi hai. Edge ML ka naya paradigm dedicated specialized processors jaise ASICs use karta hai — examples hain Google ka TPU aur Apple ka A14. AutoML bhi yahi karta hai — jaise Google AutoML Vision TensorFlow ko TF Lite, TensorFlow.js, Core ML, Container, ya Coral par deploy kar deta hai.

Yaad rakho: Hierarchy ka order hai — DevOps, phir Data Automation, phir Platform Automation, phir MLOps. Neeche ki layer ke bina upar wali khadi nahi hoti. Aur MLOps ka feedback loop hai: reusable pipelines, continuous delivery, audit trail, aur data drift observation.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Introduction to MLOps

01.4Chapter 1 · Introduction to MLOps

Implementing DevOps — CI with GitHub Actions

DevOps ki foundation hai continuous integration. Bina automated testing ke aage badhne ka koi tareeka nahi hai. Achhi khabar ye hai ki Python project ke liye CI relatively painless hai — bas ek scaffolding chahiye, aur phir use GitHub Actions se connect kar do.

Python project scaffolding — chaar files

ML project ka runtime almost guaranteed Linux operating system par hota hai, isliye project structure straightforward hai. Sirf chaar files chahiye CI journey shuru karne ke liye — Makefile, requirements.txt, hello.py, aur test_hello.py — plus ek Python virtual environment.

Virtual environment banane ke liye:

python3 -m venv ~/.your-repo-name
source ~/.your-repo-name/bin/activate

Virtual environment kyun? Kyunki Python ek interpreted language hai, wo libraries ko operating system mein kahin se bhi grab kar sakta hai. Virtual environment third-party packages ko ek specific directory mein isolate kar deta hai. Isi problem ke aur solutions bhi hain, lekin sab effectively yehi karte hain — Python library aur interpreter ko ek particular project ke liye isolate karna.

Makefile — teen recipes

Makefile Unix-based operating systems ke saath aane wale make system se recipes chalata hai. Ye CI ke steps simplify karne ke liye ideal choice hai:

install:
    pip install --upgrade pip && pip install -r requirements.txt
lint:
    pylint --disable=R,C hello.py
test:
    python -m pytest -vv --cov=hello test_hello.py

Makefile kyun chahiye? Beginner ka common reaction hota hai — ye extra kaam kyun? Asliyat mein ye kam kaam hai, kyunki ye complicated build steps ko yaad rakhta hai jo type karna mushkil aur error-prone hai. Lint step ka example lo — Makefile se sirf make lint type karna hai, aur wahi command CI server ke andar bhi chal sakti hai. Alternative hai har baar poora directive type karna, jaise pylint --disable=R,C *.py — ye tedious hai aur galti hone ke chances zyada hain. Makefile commands shell auto-completion se bhi pehchane jaate hain, to tab-complete se steps aasan ho jaate hain.

Ek common mistake ye hai ki newcomer Makefile ko virtual environment se confuse kar le. Makefile sirf commands chalata hai — isliye agar project virtual environment use karta hai, to pehle use source karo. Aur agar editor jaise VS Code use kar rahe ho, to use apne Python virtual environment ke baare mein batana hoga taaki syntax highlighting aur linting sahi mile.

Source code aur tests

hello.py mein ek simple add function hai:

def add(x, y):
    # This is an add function
    return x + y

print(add(1, 1))

Aur test_hello.py mein pytest se test hai, jo hello.py ke same folder mein hona chahiye taaki from hello import add kaam kare:

from hello import add

def test_add():
    assert 2 == add(1, 1)

requirements.txt pip installation tool ki convention hai — project mein ek ya zyada aisi files ho sakti hain agar different environments ke liye different packages chahiye.

Local CI — teen commands

Locally teen steps chalao:

  • make install — project ki libraries install karo.
  • make lint — pylint chalao; example output mein code rated 10.00/10 aaya tha.
  • make test — pytest chalao; example mein test_hello.py::test_add PASSED aur coverage 100% aayi thi.

Jab ye locally kaam karne lage, to isi process ko remote SaaS build server se integrate karna straightforward hai. Options hain GitHub Actions, cloud native build server jaise AWS CodeBuild, GCP CloudBuild, Azure DevOps Pipelines, ya open source self-hosted build server jaise Jenkins.

GitHub Actions se CI configure karna

GitHub Actions se CI implement karne ka sabse straightforward tareeka hai. GitHub UI mein Actions select karke naya banao, ya is directory mein file banao: .github/workflows/<yourfilename>.yml. Example YAML ye hai:

name: Azure Python 3.5
on: [push]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v2
    - name: Set up Python 3.5.10
      uses: actions/setup-python@v1
      with:
        python-version: 3.5.10
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        make install
    - name: Lint
      run: |
        make lint
    - name: Test
      run: |
        make test

Dekho kitna simple hai — kyunki Makefile ne pehle se hard work kar liya tha, CI steps trivial ho gaye. Har push par ye workflow chalta hai: code checkout hota hai, Python set up hota hai, dependencies install hote hain, lint chalta hai, test chalta hai. Python ka exact version wahi set karo jo project ko chahiye.

CI ke baad kya? Continuous delivery

Ye step CI setup ka final portion complete karta hai. Agla logical step hai continuous deployment — matlab ML project ko automatically production mein push karna. Ismein code ko ek specific location par deploy karna hota hai, continuous delivery process aur IaC (Infrastructure as Code) use karke. CI bina CD adhura hai, aur CD bina CI dangerous hai — pehle test karo, phir deploy karo.

Yaad rakho: Makefile CI ki jaan hai — make install, make lint, make test. Ye teen commands locally chalao, phir wahi teen GitHub Actions YAML mein daal do. Har push par automatic check, bina manual kaam ke.

02Chapter 2 · MLOps Foundations

MLOps Foundations

Chapter 1 mein humne MLOps ka big picture dekha — ab neev bharne ka time hai. Ye chapter un foundational skills par hai jin ke bina production mein ML karna mushkil hai: Bash aur Linux command line, cloud computing, Python, math, aur phir sab kuch jod kar ek end-to-end MLOps pipeline banana.

Foundation kyun zaroori hai?

Book kehta hai ki jab naye students data science aur ML mein aate hain, to unmein inhi foundational cheezon ko lekar kai misconceptions hoti hain. Is chapter ka aim hai ek strong foundation banana taaki aage ki methodologies samajh mein aayein. MLOps multidisciplinary field hai — ek hi aadmi ko terminal bhi chalana hai, cloud bhi samajhna hai, Python bhi likhna hai, aur math ki intuition bhi honi chahiye.

Approach ye hai: chhota shuru karo, sabse basic solution ko working karo, phir us par iterate karo. Koi bhi complex cheez ekdum se nahi banti. Pehle hello world, phir Flask app, phir pipeline — aise hi aage badhte hain.

Chapter mein kya-kya hai — ek map

  • Bash aur Linux command line: Terminal advanced settings hai — cloud, ML aur programming ke liye zaroori skill.
  • Cloud computing foundations: Near-infinite resources, AutoML, aur multicloud development environment.
  • Python crash course: Statements aur functions — bas itna seekh kar zero se one tak pahuncha ja sakta hai.
  • Math for programmers: Descriptive statistics, normal distributions, optimization, greedy algorithms, aur gradient descent ki intuition.
  • ML key concepts: Supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement learning, aur data science ka formulaic structure — Ingest, EDA, Modeling, Conclusion.
  • MLOps pipeline from zero: Flask ML app ko Azure App Services par deploy karna, Azure Pipelines ke saath.

Chhota shuru karo, phir iterate karo

Chapter ke conclusion mein ek bahut practical salah hai: jab kuch inherently complex ho, to good approach hai small start karna aur sabse basic solution ko working karna, phir iterate karna. Ek organisation ke liye bhi yehi hai — team ko cloud computing ki basics aani chahiye, Linux terminal navigate karna aana chahiye, aur DevOps matlab CI/CD set up karna aur use karna aana chahiye. Ye sab final exercise mein ek minimalist MLOps-style project mein judta hai.

Agle chapter mein containers aur edge devices aayenge — jo SageMaker ya Azure ML Studio jaise most MLOps platforms ke essential components hain, aur isi chapter ke knowledge par build karte hain.

Yaad rakho: Foundation mein paanch cheezein hain — terminal, cloud, Python, math, aur ML concepts. Inmein se koi ek bhi kamzor ho to pipeline kahin na kahin atak jayega. Chhota shuru karo, basic solution working karo, phir iterate karo.

← Previous01.4 · Implementing DevOps — CI with GitHub Actions→ Next02.1 · Bash and the Linux Command Line
02.1Chapter 2 · MLOps Foundations

Bash and the Linux Command Line

Zyaada tar ML cloud mein hota hai, aur zyaada tar cloud platforms expect karte hain ki tum terminal se kuch na kuch interact karoge. Isliye Linux command line ki basics MLOps ke liye critical hain. Terminal se darne ki zaroorat nahi hai — ye environment ki advanced settings hai.

Terminal kya hai — advanced settings

Jab pehli baar terminal dikhaya jaata hai to students ko shock aur horror jaisa lagta hai, kyunki aajkal GUI interfaces jaise macOS ya Windows bahut powerful hain. Lekin terminal ko environment ki advanced settings ki tarah socho — cloud, ML, ya programming mein agar advanced tasks karne hain, to yehi tareeka hai. Linux terminal mein competence kisi bhi skill set ko enormously enhance kar deti hai.

Zyaada tar servers Linux par chalte hain, aur kai naye deployment options containers use karte hain jo bhi Linux chalate hain. macOS ka terminal Linux ke kaafi kareeb hai — zyaada tar commands similar hain, khaas taur par agar Homebrew jaise third-party tools install kar lo. Seekhne wali minimal cheezein hain: cloud-based shell environment, Bash shell aur commands, files aur navigation, input/output, configuration, aur script likhna.

Cloud shell development environments

Personal workstation se web-based cloud shell development environment par shift karna worth hai. Analogy hai surfer ki — wo roz 50 miles drive karke beach ja sakta hai, lekin ye inconvenient, inefficient aur expensive hai. Behtar hai beach ke paas rehna. Waise hi cloud development environment kai problems solve karta hai: ye zyada secure hai kyunki developer keys idhar-udhar pass karne ki zaroorat nahi, bahut si problems local machine se solve nahi hoti kyunki extensive data cloud se wapas nahi laa sakte, aur tools ki deep integration kaam ko efficient banati hai. Aur beach ke paas rehne ke opposite, cloud development environment free hai — saare major clouds apne cloud development environments free tiers par dete hain.

AWS par do options hain. Pehla hai AWS CloudShell — ek Bash shell jismein unique AWS command completion built-in hai. Agar tum regularly CloudShell use karte ho, to ~/.bashrc edit karke apna experience customize karna achha idea hai, built-in vim editor se. Dusra hai AWS Cloud9 — ek zyada comprehensive development environment jismein shell ke saath GUI editor bhi hai, Python, Go aur Node samet kai languages ke liye syntax highlighting ke saath. ML microservices develop karne ke liye Cloud9 ideal hai kyunki console se deployed services ko web requests bhej sakte ho aur AWS Lambda ke saath deep integration hai. Azure ya GCP par bhi wahi concepts apply hote hain.

Bash shell aur commands — list, locate, count

Shell ek interactive environment hai jismein prompt hota hai aur commands run karne ki ability hoti hai. Aajkal zyaada tar shells Bash ya ZSH chalate hain. Ek immediately useful kaam hai ZSH aur vim configurations install karna — vim ke liye awesome vim, aur ZSH ke liye ohmyzsh recommended hain.

Files list karne ke liye ls command hai, -l flag additional listing information deta hai:

bash-3.2$ ls -l
bash-3.2$ which ls
/bin/ls
bash-3.2$ ls -l /bin/ | wc -l
37

which command batata hai ki shell executables kahan hain — ls /bin directory mein hai. Aur pipe operator | ek command ka output dusre command ko deta hai, jaise yahan /bin mein executables count karne ke liye wc -l use hua.

Files aur navigation, input aur output

GUI mein folder ya file kholte ho; shell mein commands se wahi kaam hota hai. pwd full path dikhata hai jahan tum ho, cd naye directory mein change karta hai:

bash-3.2$ pwd
bash-3.2$ cd /tmp

Input/output ka example dekho — pehle words ek file mein redirect hote hain, phir cat se print hote hain, phir wc se count hote hain:

bash-3.2$ echo "foo bar baz" > out.txt
bash-3.2$ cat out.txt | wc -c
12
bash-3.2$ cat out.txt | wc -w
3

Ek aur powerful example hai shuf command — ye file ko shuffle karta hai aur specified rows tak limit karta hai. Ek almost 1 GB file se pehle 100,000 rows lekar nayi file banana sirf 2.7 seconds mein ho gaya. Aise shell technique se din bach sakta hai jab CSV file laptop par data science libraries se process karne ke liye bahut badi ho:

bash-3.2$ time shuf -n 100000 en.openfoodfacts.org.products.tsv > 10k.sample.en.openfoodfacts.org.products.tsv

Configuration — .bashrc aur .zshrc

ZSH aur Bash shell configuration files mein settings store hoti hain jo har baar terminal khulne par invoke hoti hain. ZSH ke liye .zshrc aur Bash ke liye .bashrc starting point hai. Example mein ek alias hai jo ek command se directory mein cd karta hai aur Python virtual environment source karta hai, aur dusre section mein AWS CLI variables export hote hain:

alias flask-azure-ml="cd /path/to/project && source ~/.flask-ml-azure/bin/activate"
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="<key>"
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="<key>"
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="us-east-1"

Apni shell configuration file customize karna chhota investment hai jo automation se bade dividends deta hai.

Apni pehli script likhna

Shell script likhna daunting lag sakta hai kyunki syntax Python se scary hai, weird characters ke saath. Lekin kai tareekon se ye start karna aasan hai — command ko ek file mein daalo, phir use run karo. Pehli line shebang line kehlati hai aur script ko Bash use karne ko kehti hai, dusri line echo command hai:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "hello world"
bash-3.2$ chmod +x hello.sh
bash-3.2$ ./hello.sh
Hello World

Bash script ki achhi baat ye hai ki tum koi bhi commands paste kar sakte ho — isse chhote tasks automate karna straightforward ho jaata hai, bina programming ki zyada knowledge ke.

Yaad rakho: Terminal advanced settings hai, darne ki cheez nahi. ls, pwd, cd, pipe |, redirect >, aur chmod +x — bas itne se tum cloud shell mein kaam shuru kar sakte ho. Aur apni .bashrc ya .zshrc customize karna mat bhoolo.
Book ka poora code — official repo se (code cells/files only, outputs nahi):
add.py — chapter2/add.py
#!/usr/bin/env python
from random import choices

def add(x,y):
    print(f"inside a function and adding {x}, {y}")
    return x+y

#Send random numbers from 1-10, ten times to the add function
numbers = range(1,10)
for num in numbers:
    xx = choices(numbers)[0]
    yy = choices(numbers)[0]
    print(add(xx,yy))
hello.sh — chapter2/hello.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash

echo "Hello World"

← Previous02 · MLOps Foundations→ Next02.2 · Cloud Computing Foundations and Cloud Shell
02.2Chapter 2 · MLOps Foundations

Cloud Computing Foundations and Cloud Shell

Almost saare forms of ML ko kisi na kisi form mein cloud computing chahiye. Cloud ka key concept hai near-infinite resources — bina cloud ke kai ML models karna hi feasible nahi hai. Aur cloud ki killer feature hai compute aur storage ko data ke paas le jaana, data ko move kiye bina.

Near-infinite resources — calculus wali analogy

Cloud computing ke baare mein ek paper hai — Above the Clouds: A Berkeley View of Cloud Computing — jo near-infinite resources ke idea ko describe karta hai. Bina cloud ke kai ML models feasible hi nahi hain. Book mein ek sundar comparison hai: calculus ne infinity ko sahi tareeke se use karke universe ke secrets unlock kiye — centuries tak circle ka shape jaise problems impossible the bina calculus ke. Waise hi cloud computing ke bina ML mein operationalizing jaise issues feasible nahi hain. Cloud near-infinite compute aur storage deta hai aur data par bina use move kiye kaam karta hai.

Ye ability — data ko move kiye bina us par computing power harness karna, ML platforms jaise AWS SageMaker ya Azure ML Studio ke through — cloud ki killer feature hai jo bina cloud ke replicate nahi ho sakti.

Automator's law — automation eventually hoti hai

Iske saath ek concept hai jise book Automator's law kehti hai: jab general public kisi vertical ki automation ke baare mein baat karna shuru kar deti hai — self-driving cars, IT, factories, machine learning — to wo eventually hoti hai. Iska matlab ye nahi ki koi magic unicorn aata hai aur projects aasan ho jaate hain; matlab ye hai ki humans collective group ke roop mein trends spot karne mein achhe hain.

Examples bahut hain. Television industry mein pehle linear editing hoti thi — black screen par dissolve karne ke liye teen tapes chahiye the: source tape, edit master tape, aur black footage wali teesri tape. Log baat karte the ki ye workflow automate ho jaaye to kitna achha ho, aur baad mein nonlinear editing se ye fully automated ho gaya. Early 1990s mein ye systems hundreds of thousands of dollars ke the; aaj ek thousand-dollar laptop par usse zyada complicated editing hoti hai.

Cloud computing ke saath bhi wahi hua. Early 2000s mein companies ke apne data centers the, teams of people maintain karte the. Log kehte the ki future mein companies poora data center laptop se control karengi. Expert data center technicians is idea par haste the, lekin Automator's law phir se strike hui — 2020 aur uske baad majority companies ke paas kisi na kisi form mein cloud computing hai. Chess mein bhi wahi hua — chess software ne humans ko hara diya, lekin expert humans aur chess software mil kar chess software alone se jeete. ML aur data science ke saath bhi aisa hi ho sakta hai — automation simple ML tasks replace karegi aur domain expert humans ko orders of magnitude zyada effective bana degi.

AutoML kya hai?

AutoML modeling aspect ki automation hai. Crude aur straightforward example hai Excel spreadsheet jo linear regression karti hai — tum Excel ko batate ho kaunsa column target hai predict karne ke liye aur kaunsa column feature hai. Zyada sophisticated AutoML systems waise hi kaam karte hain: tum select karte ho kya predict karna hai — image classification, numerical trend, categorical text classification, ya clustering — phir AutoML software wahi techniques karta hai jo data scientist karta — hyperparameter tuning, algorithm selection, aur model explainability.

Saare major cloud platforms ke paas MLOps platforms mein embedded AutoML tools hain. Isliye AutoML saare cloud-based ML projects ke liye ek option hai aur productivity enhancement ban raha hai.

Multicloud development environment se shuruaat

Cloud computing se shuru karne ka recommended approach hai ek multicloud development environment set up karna. Basic structure ye dikhata hai ki cloud shell wo cheez hai jo in teeno clouds mein common hai — AWS, Azure, aur GCP, teeno ke paas cloud-based development environments hain cloud shell ke through. GitHub jaise source control repository central location hai jahan teeno cloud environments initially communicate karte hain.

Chapter 1 wala Python scaffolding yahan bhi kaam aata hai — repeatable aur testable structure. GitHub Actions ke through CI/CD process ensure karta hai ki Python code working hai aur high quality ka hai. Testing aur linting Python code ek aisa process hai jo software project ki quality validate karta hai. Developer locally testing aur linting chalata hai taaki software quality high rahe. Ye robotic vacuum machine (robovac) jaisa hai — jab room saaf karna ho to on kar do, aur wo room ko known good state mein rakhta hai. Waise hi lints aur tests code ko known good state mein rakhte hain.

CI/CD pipeline ye quality-control checks ek external environment mein chalata hai taaki application release se pehle working ho. Isse software deployment repeatable aur reliable banta hai — ye modern software engineering best practice hai, aur iska dusra naam hai DevOps. Teeno major clouds use karna cloud computing se familiar hone ka great tareeka hai, kyunki names alag hain lekin concepts identical hain. Agar terminology mein help chahiye to Appendix A dekho.

Yaad rakho: Cloud ki killer feature hai data ko move kiye bina us par near-infinite compute chalana. Automator's law kehti hai — jis vertical ki automation ki baat shuru ho jaaye, wo eventually hoti hai. AutoML modeling ko automate karta hai, aur teeno clouds ke concepts same hain, sirf naam alag hain.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — MLOps Foundations
← Previous02.1 · Bash and the Linux Command Line→ Next02.3 · Python Crash Course
02.3Chapter 2 · MLOps Foundations

Python Crash Course

Python DevOps, cloud computing, data science, aur ML ki de facto language kyun hai? Kyunki ye language computer ke liye nahi, developer ke liye optimize hai. Kam code, jaldi kaam — aur cloud aur containers ne uski performance wali kamzori ko cover kar diya hai.

Python ki taakat aur kamzori

C ya C++ jaise languages ki performance excellent hai kyunki wo lower-level hain — developer ko zyada mehnat karni padti hai: memory allocate karna, types declare karna, program compile karna. Python programmer kuch commands daalta hai aur run karta hai, aur aksar Python mein code significantly kam hota hai. Is convenience ke liye Python ki performance C, C#, Java aur Go se bahut slow hai. Python ki limitations bhi hain — true threads ki kami, JIT (Just in Time) compiler ki kami, aur C# ya F# jaisi type inference ki kami.

Lekin cloud computing ke saath language performance kai problems ko bind nahi karti. Fair kehna hoga ki Python accidentally lucky ho gaya do cheezon ki wajah se: cloud computing aur containers. Cloud ke saath design fully distributed hai — AWS Lambda aur AWS SQS jaise technologies par build hota hai. Containerized technology jaise Kubernetes distributed systems banane ka heavy lifting karti hai, to Python threads achanak irrelevant ho jaate hain.

Cloud ek operating system hai

Cloud ko ek operating system ki tarah socho. Mid-1980s mein Sun Computer ka marketing phrase tha — The Network is the Computer. 1980 mein ye premature ho sakta tha, lekin 2021 mein ye bahut accurate hai. Single machine par threads spawn karne ke bajaye tum cloud mein AWS Lambda functions spawn kar sakte ho, jo infinitely scalable resources wale operating system ki tarah behave karta hai.

AWS Lambda ek function as a service (FaaS) technology hai jo AWS platform par chalti hai. Iska naam FaaS isliye hai kyunki ek Lambda function sirf kuch lines ka code ho sakta hai — literally ek function. Ye functions events se attach ho sakte hain jaise cloud queuing system Amazon SQS, ya Amazon S3 object storage par upload hui image.

Performance ka ek shocking number bhi book mein hai: Python equivalent matrix operations mein C se 64,000 times slower hai. Aur ek research paper, Energy Efficiency across programming languages, dikhata hai ki kai operations mein Python C se 50 times zyada energy leta hai. Python popularity mein badh raha hai, to ye concern hai ki kya ye coal powerplant jaisa hai green energy solar system ke bajaye. Ek solution ho sakta hai ki koi major cloud vendor Python ke liye naya runtime banaye jo JIT compiler jaise modern computer science techniques use kare.

Consumer bano, creator nahi — pehle functions seekho

Newcomers ke saath ek technical hurdle ye hai ki wo traditional computer science approach se code seekhte hain. Cloud computing aur ML conventional software engineering projects jaise GUI applications develop karne se bahut alag hain. Cloud aur ML world mein zyada tar chhote functions likhne hote hain. Aksar Python ke dusre parts — object-oriented code — ki zaroorat nahi hoti, aur newcomer ko discourage karte hain.

Concurrency, object-oriented programming, metaprogramming, aur algorithm theory jaise computer science topics platform, library aur tool creators ke liye valuable hain. Lekin agar tum libraries aur frameworks create nahi kar rahe, use kar rahe ho, to tum in advanced topics ko safely ignore kar sakte ho aur functions par stick kar sakte ho. Ye crash course consumer ke liye hai — data scientist ya MLOps practitioner, jahan zyaada tar log apna career spend karte hain. In topics ke baad, agar curious ho, to complex computer science topics par jaane ke liye solid foundation mil jayegi. Ye advanced topics immediately productive hone ke liye necessary nahi hain.

Minimal Python — statements aur functions

Shuru karne ke liye sabse kam Python kya chahiye? Do sabse essential components hain — statements aur functions. Python statement computer ko instruction hai; jaise kisi insaan ko hello kehna, waise hi computer ko print hello keh sakte ho:

>>> print("Hello World")
Hello World

Python mein do statements ko semicolon se chain bhi kar sakte ho. Example mein os module import karke os.listdir call kiya gaya hai jo current directory ke contents list karta hai:

>>> import os; os.listdir(".")
['chapter11', 'README.md', 'chapter2', '.git', 'chapter3']

Ye pattern data science notebooks mein pervasive hai, aur shuru karne ke liye bas itna hi chahiye. Python ya IPython ya Jupyter REPL mein try karna Python se familiar hone ka pehla tareeka hai.

Dusri cheez hai functions likhna aur use karna. Function ek unit of work hai — jaise kitchen mein toaster unit of work hai: bread input lo, warm karo, toast return karo. Waise hi add function ek baar likhne ke baad kitni bhi baar naye inputs ke saath use kar sakte ho:

>>> def add(x, y):
...     return x + y
...
>>> add(1, 1)
2
>>> add(3, 4)
7

Poori script banana

Ab knowledge ko assemble karke ek Python script banao. Shuruaat mein shebang line hoti hai, jaise Bash mein. Phir choices library import hoti hai, jo baad mein loop mein add function ko random numbers bhejti hai:

#!/usr/bin/env python
from random import choices

def add(x, y):
    print(f"inside a function and adding {x}, {y}")
    return x + y

numbers = range(1, 10)
for num in numbers:
    xx = choices(numbers)[0]
    yy = choices(numbers)[0]
    print(add(xx, yy))

Script ko Bash script ki tarah chmod +x add.py se executable banao, phir ./add.py se chalao — har baar random numbers add hokar print honge. Aise examples se toy karke zero se one tak pahunchna sabse tez tareeka hai.

Yaad rakho: Python developer ke liye optimize hai, computer ke liye nahi. Cloud aur containers ne uski slowness ko cover kar diya. MLOps mein pehle functions seekho — statements aur functions hi kaafi hain shuru karne ke liye; OOP aur advanced CS topics baad mein aayenge.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — MLOps Foundations
← Previous02.2 · Cloud Computing Foundations and Cloud Shell→ Next02.4 · Math for Programmers Crash Course
02.4Chapter 2 · MLOps Foundations

Math for Programmers Crash Course

Math daunting aur irritating lag sakta hai, lekin ML ke saath kaam karne ke liye basics samajhna essential hai. Ye section kuch useful aur essential ideas ko minimal tareeke se cover karta hai — statistics, optimization, aur deep learning ki intuition.

Descriptive statistics aur normal distributions

Duniya mein kai cheezein normally distributed hoti hain. Achha example hai height aur weight. Agar duniya ke har insaan ki height plot karo, to bell-shaped distribution milegi. Intuitive hai — zyaada tar log average height ke hote hain, aur seven-foot-tall basketball player dekhna unusual hai.

Book mein ek Jupyter notebook ka example hai jismein 19 saal ke bachchon ki heights aur weights ke 25,000 records hain. Pandas se CSV read karo, phir seaborn se lmplot banao — height aur weight ke beech linear relationship dikhega: jitne lambe ho, utna zyada weight hota hai. Data ko visualize karne ka ye step Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) kehlata hai — math aur visualization ke combination se aas-paas dekhna.

import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("height-weight-25k.csv")
import seaborn as sns
sns.lmplot("Height-Inches", "Weight-Pounds", data=df)

Phir df.describe() se descriptive statistics milte hain. Inhe aise samjho jaise numerically wo dekhna jo aankh visually dekhti hai. 50th percentile ya median exact middle height batata hai — lagbhag 68 inches. Max statistic is dataset mein 75 inches hai — sabse extreme observation, sabse lamba insaan. Normally distributed dataset mein max observation rare hota hai, jaise minimum bhi. Kernel Density plot se dono — weight aur height — bell distribution dikhate hain: extreme values rare hain, zyaada tar values beech mein hain.

ML heavily normal distribution ke idea par build karta hai, aur ye intuition models build aur maintain karne mein bahut kaam aati hai. Lekin note karo ki normal distribution ke beyond bhi distributions hain jo duniya ko model karna zyada mushkil banati hain — jaise fat tails, matlab hard-to-predict aur rare events jo duniya par significantly affect karte hain. Modeling mein over-confident hone ka danger bhi hai — weather forecasts sirf do hafte tak accurate ho sakte hain, uske aage predict karna fantasy hai.

Optimization — gradient descent ki intuition

ML mein ek fundamental problem hai optimization — kisi problem ka best ya good enough solution dhoondhna. Gradient descent ek optimization algorithm hai jo deep learning ke heart mein hai. Iska goal hai global minimum tak pahunchna, matlab optimal solution, local minimum mein atakne ke bajaye. Intuition straightforward hai agar imagine karo ki andhere mein pahad se neeche chal rahe ho. Global minimum matlab tum zinda pahad ke neeche pahunch gaye. Local minimum matlab tum galti se pahad ke side mein ek lake mein chal gaye, neeche se 1,000 feet door.

Notation bhi samajhna zaroori hai — spreadsheet, algebra, aur Python mein same cheez likhne ke tareeke alag hain, lekin kaam wahi hai. Whiteboard par, Excel mein, ya thode code se — same kaam kar sakte ho.

Greedy algorithms — change banana

Greedy algorithms hamesha pehle best option lete hain. Ye achhe kaam karte hain agar perfect solution ki parwah nahi hai, ya perfect solution dhoondhna impossible hai, lekin good enough solution se kaam chal jaata hai. Change banane ka example lo — sabse bade value ke coins pehle lo, phir next highest, aur aise hi aage:

python change.py --full 1.34
Quarters 5: , Remainder: 9
Dimes 0: , Remainder: 0
Nickles 1: , Remainder: 4
Pennies 4:

Core code mein ek recursive function har iteration solve karta hai — bade coins khatm hote hain, phir medium coins, phir sabse chhote coins. Tests bhi hain is algorithm ke liye — unittest se check karte hain ki quarter, dime, nickel, penny ke cases sahi hain, aur chhote aur bade numbers par bhi. Optimization wale solution ko test karna hamesha achha idea hai.

Traveling Salesman Problem — good enough hi kaafi hai

Optimization mein sabse zyada studied problems mein se ek hai Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) — cities ki list par travel karo aur distance minimize karo. Ye ek perfect solution na hone ka excellent example hai, lekin good enough solution hai. Greedy algorithm har choice par sahi solution pick karega. Is example mein har baar ek random city starting point ke roop mein chuni jaati hai, phir simulations se lowest distance pick ki jaati hai.

Routes Bay Area ki companies ke beech distances hain — jaise AAPL se INTC 8, AAPL se CSCO 14. Script ko iterations ki sankhya input mein do, jaise python greedy_random_start.py 20 se 20 baar chalao. 25 simulations chalane par good solution 129 mili, jabki sirf ek baar chalane par worse distance 143 mili. Jitni zyada simulations, utna behtar chance ki global minimum ke kareeb pahuncho — agar dataset enormous ho aur jaldi ho to kuch simulations, aur agar poora din hai to 1,000 baar chala kar subah tak best answer pa lo. Geographic coordinates dataset mein kai local minima ho sakte hain — solutions jo optimal solution tak nahi pahunchte.

Deep learning intuition — learning rate

MLOps ke liye convergence ek essential operational issue hai — matlab model aisa solution dhoondhe jo aur data add karne se improve na ho. Kya GPU-based training cluster faster convergence dega? Kya CPU-based training cluster lower costs dega? Operating costs real world mein company ya project ko tod sakte hain, isliye optimization ki intuition hona aur use practice mein test karna essential hai.

Gradient descent ki intuition badhane ke liye ek valuable tool hai TensorFlow Playground. Learning rate ke saath experiment karo — bahut high rate oscillation ki taraf le jaata hai, test loss 0.984 par atak jaata hai kyunki gradient descent effectively use nahi ho pa raha. Bahut low rate global minimum tak nahi pahunchega ya converge karne mein bahut time lega. Optimal learning rate global minimum par converge karta hai, bahut high thrashing karta hai, aur bahut low local minimum mein atak sakta hai.

ML key concepts — teen categories

ML matlab computers ka bina explicit programming ke tasks karna — data se seekh kar. Teen categories hain: supervised, unsupervised, aur reinforcement learning. Supervised ML mein labels known hote hain aur model historical data se seekhta hai — height-weight example mein height aur weight labels hain aur 25,000 observations historical data hain. Saara ML data ko numerical form mein aur scaling ke saath chahiye — magnitude ka reason hai scaling: agar koi kahe 50 run kiya, to 50 miles ya 50 feet?

Unsupervised ML labels discover karta hai. Example hai NBA season 2015-2016 — computer ne players ko group karna seekha, chaar attributes compare karke: points, rebounds, blocks, aur assists. Multidimensional space mein ek dusre se lowest total distance wale players group hue. Domain expert phir labels select karta hai — ek group ko best kaha gaya. K-means clustering mein ek common dilemma hai sahi number of clusters select karna — iska perfect answer nahi hai, art aur science dono hai. Ek solution hai Yellowbrick jaise framework se elbow plots banana, ya MLOps platform jaise SageMaker se automated hyperparameter tuning se K-means cluster assignment karwana.

Reinforcement learning mein ek agent environment explore karke tasks karna seekhta hai. Example hai AWS DeepRacer — model car ko track par drive karna sikhaya jaata hai. Agent car hai, environment track hai. Reward function decide karta hai agent har run mein kaise interact kare. Ek reward function centerline follow karne par reward deta hai — center ke kareeb ho to reward 1.0, thoda door ho to 0.5, aur door ho to 0.1, aur off track ho to 1e-3. Dusra reward function saare wheels track par rehne par reward deta hai. Dono similar hain, lekin dramatically different results de sakte hain — randomness ka bahut bada role hai.

Data science ka formula — Ingest, EDA, Modeling, Conclusion

Data science karne ka ek formulaic structure hai jo notebook mein banana chahiye: Ingest, EDA, aur Modeling and Conclusion. Isse team ka koi bhi member project ke sections mein quickly toggle karke feel le sakta hai. Production mein deploy hue model ke saath ek notebook checked in hona chahiye jo project ke peeche ki thinking ka README ho.

Ingest section mein data sources web request se load hote hain, seedha Pandas mein. EDA section mein ideas explore karte hain — data mein kya ho raha hai. Modeling section mein model rehta hai — jaise serialized sklearn model, Boston Housing Pickle notebook mein. Conclusion section business leader ke liye summary hona chahiye jo decision le raha hai. Aakhir mein project ko GitHub mein check karo taaki MLOps portfolio bane.

Yaad rakho: Normal distribution mein extreme values rare hote hain, zyaada tar values beech mein. Gradient descent mein learning rate na bahut high ho na bahut low. Aur greedy algorithm perfect nahi, good enough solution deta hai — ML mein aksar good enough hi kaafi hota hai.

← Previous02.3 · Python Crash Course→ Next02.5 · Build an MLOps Pipeline from Zero
02.5Chapter 2 · MLOps Foundations

Build an MLOps Pipeline from Zero

Ab tak sab alag-alag seekha — terminal, cloud, Python, math. Ab sab kuch jod kar ek MLOps pipeline from zero banate hain: ek Flask ML application ko Azure App Services par deploy karna, Azure Pipelines ke saath. GitHub events build trigger karte hain, aur build deploy karta hai serverless platform par.

Architecture — GitHub se Azure tak

Pipeline ka overview ye hai: GitHub events Azure Pipelines build process ko trigger karte hain, jo changes ko serverless platform par deploy karta hai. Naam dusre cloud platforms par alag hain, lekin conceptually AWS aur GCP mein bhi cheezein bahut similar hain. Yehi pattern hai jo aage ke chapters mein containers aur cloud pipelines mein phir se aayega.

Locally chalana — chaar steps

Locally run karne ke steps ye hain:

python3 -m venv ~/.flask-ml-azure
source ~/.flask-ml-azure/bin/activate
make install
python app.py

Phir alag shell mein ./make_prediction.sh chalao. Ye wahi scaffolding hai jo Chapter 1 mein seekhi thi — virtual environment, make install, phir app chalao. Locally kaam karna pehla milestone hai; jab tak locally nahi chal raha, cloud par deploy karne ka koi matlab nahi hai.

Azure Pipelines mein chalana — step by step

Azure mein run karne ke steps ye hain. Pehle Azure Shell launch karo. Phir Azure Pipelines enabled ke saath ek GitHub repo banao — ye existing repo ka fork bhi ho sakta hai. Phir repo ko Azure Cloud Shell mein clone karo. SSH keys set up karne ke liye alag guide hai, lekin concept wahi hai — shell se repo access karo.

Phir virtual environment banao aur source karo, make install chalao, aur app service create karke initially Cloud Shell mein deploy karo:

python3 -m venv ~/.flask-ml-azure
source ~/.flask-ml-azure/bin/activate
make install
az webapp up -n <your-appservice>

Deployed application ko verify karo — deployed URL par browse karo: https://<your-appservice>.azurewebsites.net/. Phir ML predictions verify karo — make_predict_azure_app.sh mein line change karo taaki POST request deployed prediction URL par jaaye, jaise -X POST https://<yourappname>.azurewebsites.net:$PORT/predict.

Azure DevOps project aur pipeline YAML

Phir Azure DevOps project banao aur Azure se connect karo. Azure Resource Manager se connect karo, phir connection ko pehle se deployed resource group se configure karo. Phir GitHub integration ke saath ek naya Python pipeline banao. Is process se ek YAML file create hoti hai jo machine-generated hoti hai — uska pehla hissa kuch is tarah dikhta hai:

trigger:
- master
variables:
  azureServiceConnectionId: 'df9170e4-12ed-498f-93e9-79c1e9b9bd59'
  webAppName: 'flask-ml-service'
  vmImageName: 'ubuntu-latest'
  environmentName: 'flask-ml-service'
  pythonVersion: '3.7'
stages:
- stage: Build
  displayName: Build stage
  jobs:
  - job: BuildJob
    pool:
      vmImage: $(vmImageName)
    steps:
    - task: UsePythonVersion@0
      inputs:
        versionSpec: '$(pythonVersion)'
    - script: |
        python -m venv antenv
        source antenv/bin/activate
        python -m pip install --upgrade pip
        pip install -r requirements.txt

Ye YAML trigger, variables, stages, jobs aur steps define karti hai — build stage mein Python version set hoti hai, virtual environment banta hai, aur requirements install hote hain. Official Azure Pipeline YAML documentation se iske baare mein aur detail mein padh sakte ho.

Lint step add karna aur CD verify karna

Aakhir mein continuous delivery verify karo — app.py mein change karo aur dekho ki pipeline automatically deploy karti hai ya nahi. Aur ek lint step add karo, jo code ko syntax failure ke against gate karta hai:

- script: |
    python -m venv antenv
    source antenv/bin/activate
    make install
    make lint
  workingDirectory: $(projectRoot)
  displayName: 'Run lint tests'

Lint step ka matlab hai ki agar code mein syntax error hai, to pipeline aage nahi badhegi. Ye wahi robovac wali soch hai — code ko known good state mein rakhna, har push par automatically.

Yaad rakho: Pipeline ka flow hai — pehle locally chalao (venv, make install, python app.py), phir az webapp up se deploy karo, phir Azure Pipelines YAML se automate karo, aur lint step se gate karo. Local pehle, cloud baad mein.
