← Previous02.4 · Math for Programmers Crash Course→ Next03 · MLOps for Containers and Edge Devices
03Chapter 3 · MLOps for Containers and Edge Devices

MLOps for Containers and Edge Devices

Jab technology mein shuruaat hui to virtual machines har jagah the — hosting providers se lekar bade servers wale IT rooms tak. Lekin ab do technologies model deployments ke liye increasingly important hain: containers aur edge devices. VM cellphone par nahi chalegi, aur reproducible files ke saath jaldi iterate karne ke liye bhi VM sahi nahi hai.

Virtual machines ki problem — move karna mushkil

VMs ke saath ek problem thi unhe move karna. Agar host server A par naya operating system install karna ho, to system administrator ko VMs ko host server B par move karna padta tha. VM utni hi badi hoti thi jitna data initially configure kiya gaya tha — 50 GB virtual drive ka matlab 50 gigabytes ki file. 50 gigabytes ek server se dusre par move karne mein time lagta tha, aur agar critical service chal rahi ho to downtime minimize karna mushkil tha.

Snapshots, recovery, backups jaise strategies se ye issues minimize hue, aur cloud providers ne practically inhe eliminate kar diya. Aaj bhi VMs ki cloud offerings mein important jagah hai — Google Cloud unhe Compute Engine kehta hai, aur dusre providers ke paas similar reference hai. Bahut si VMs enhanced GPUs deti hain taaki ML operations ke liye better performance mile. Lekin VMs yahan rehne ke liye hain, phir bhi containers aur edge devices ko samajhna zaroori hai.

Containers kyun viral hue — Docker aur registry

Docker ko PyCon 2013 mein announce kiya gaya tha, aur demo incredible laga. Lean virtualization Linux ke liye naya nahi tha — LXC (Linux containers) pehle se wahi functionality deta tha. Lekin LXC ki tooling dismal thi, aur Docker ne ek key factor laaya: easy collaboration aur sharing through a registry. Registries kisi bhi developer ko apne changes central location par push karne deti hain, jahan se dusre unhe pull karke locally run kar sakte hain. Registry support, wahi tooling ke saath jo containers deal karti hai, ne technology ko incredible pace par aage badhaya.

Red Hat ki description ke mutabik, containers application ke baare mein hain — sirf wo jo application hai, jaise source code aur supporting files — versus wo jo use run karne ke liye chahiye, jaise databases. Traditional tareeke mein engineers virtual machines ko all-in-one service ki tarah use karte the jahan database, web server aur saari system services ek hi machine par installed, configured aur run hoti thi. Ye applications monolithic hoti thi, tied interdependencies ke saath. Microservice, iske opposite, ek application hai jo system requirements jaise databases se fully decoupled hai aur independently run kar sakti hai. VMs ko microservices ki tarah use kar sakte ho, lekin containers is concept mein better fit hote hain.

Edge devices — compute user ke kareeb

Edge ka matlab hai compute devices jo data center ke andar thousands of servers ke saath nahi hain. Mobile phones, Raspberry Pi, aur smart home devices edge devices ke examples hain. Bade telecommunication companies edge computing ki taraf push kar rahi hain — users ko faster feedback dena, expensive compute requests ko remote data center tak route karne ke bajaye.

General idea hai ki computational resources user ke jitne kareeb honge, user experience utna fast hoga. Specialized chips chhote, fast aur zyada effective ho rahe hain, to future mein zyada ML edge par hoga. Edge inferencing ki problems — offline, remote, aur fast access — transformational ho sakti hain, khaas taur par remote regions ke liye jahan reliable power aur network nahi hai.

Chapter mein kya-kya hai

  • Containers: Runtime, Dockerfile se create karna, run karna, aur best practices — linting aur vulnerability scanning.
  • Serving a trained model over HTTP: Flask se Boston Housing model ko container mein serve karna.
  • Edge devices: Coral USB Accelerator, Azure Percept, TFHub, aur non-TPU models ko compiler se port karna.
  • Managed ML systems aur monetizing: SageMaker jaise systems containers par build hote hain, aur containers hi models aur algorithms bechne ka package hain.

Chapter ke end mein Build Once, Run Many workflow aata hai — ek container predictions serve kar sakta hai, training kar sakta hai, ya Coral TPU ya iPhone jaise edge device par deploy ho sakta hai. Containers aur MLOps complementary hain: containers business value deliver karne mein madad karte hain, aur MLOps methodologies uske upar productivity streamline karti hain.

Yaad rakho: VM all-in-one aur badi hoti hai, container sirf application aur uski zarooratein hoti hai. Registry ne containers ko viral banaya — push karo, koi bhi pull karke chala le. Aur edge matlab compute user ke kareeb, data center se door.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — MLOps for Containers and Edge Devices
← Previous02.5 · Build an MLOps Pipeline from Zero→ Next03.1 · Containers — Runtime, Creating, Running
03.1Chapter 3 · MLOps for Containers and Edge Devices

Containers — Runtime, Creating, Running

Container, Docker, aur container runtime — ye terms aksar interchangeably use hote hain aur confuse karte hain. Pehle inhe clear karo, phir Dockerfile se container banao, tag karo, registry mein push karo, aur run karo.

Container runtime kya hai?

Docker company ne initially containers create, manage aur run karne ki tooling develop ki thi, isliye Docker container kehna common ho gaya. Runtime — matlab system mein container run karne ke liye required software — bhi Docker ne banaya tha. Kuch saal baad Red Hat ne containers run karne ka ek alag tareeka contribute kiya, ek naye alternative runtime environment ke saath. Is naye environment ke saath containers operate karne ke liye naye tools bhi aaye, jo Docker ke tools ke saath kuch compatibility rakhte hain.

In naye tools aur runtime ke benefits hain — ab superuser account ki zaroorat nahi hai extensive privileges ke saath, jo kai use cases ke liye samajh mein aata hai. Lekin ye tools non-Linux operating systems par chalana abhi bhi somewhat complicated hai. Dusri taraf Docker kaam ko seamless banata hai chahe Windows, macOS ya Linux use kar rahe ho. Examples ke liye Docker use karna aasan hai — pehle ensure karo ki docker command help output dikhaye, taaki successful install verify ho.

Dockerfile — FROM aur RUN

Dockerfile container create karne ke heart mein hai. Jab bhi container create kar rahe ho, Dockerfile current directory mein present hona chahiye. Is special file mein kai sections aur commands ho sakte hain jo container image banate hain. Ek nayi file banao, naam Dockerfile rakho, aur ye contents daalo:

FROM centos:8
RUN dnf install -y python38

File mein do sections hain; har ek ko ek unique keyword delimit karta hai, jo instructions kehlate hain. FROM instruction batati hai container ka base kya hai — yahan CentOS distribution version 8 hai. Version, is case mein, ek tag hai. Tags containers mein ek point in time define karte hain. Jab koi tag define nahi hota, to default latest tag hota hai.

RUN instruction ek system command chalati hai — yahan Python 3 install hoti hai, jo base CentOS 8 image mein included nahi hai. dnf command mein -y flag hai jo installer se confirmation ka prompt rokta hai, jo build ke time trigger hota. Kisi bhi prompt se bachna crucial hai kyunki wo build ko halt kar dega.

Layers — ek baar download, baar-baar reuse

Containers ki ek bahut useful aspect hai ki wo kai layers se compose ho sakte hain, aur ye layers dusre containers mein use ya reuse ho sakti hain. Is layering workflow se 10 megabytes ki base layer har container ke liye baar-baar download nahi hoti — ek baar download karo aur kai baar reuse karo. Ye VMs se bahut alag hai, jahan saare VMs mein same files hon to bhi unhe poora download karna padta hai.

Container build karo usi directory se jahan Dockerfile hai:

$ docker build .
[+] Building 11.2s (6/6) FINISHED
=> CACHED [1/2] FROM docker.io/library/centos:8
=> [2/2] RUN dnf install -y python38

Output batata hai ki CentOS 8 ki initial layer pehle se hai, to dobara pull karne ki zaroorat nahi. Phir Python 3.8 install hokar image creation complete hoti hai.

Tagging — bina tag ke image pehchan na mushkil

Aise build karne mein problems hain. Pehli, image ko baad mein identify karna mushkil hai — sirf sha256 digest hai reference ke liye, aur kuch nahi. docker images mein repository aur tag dono none dikhenge, image ID sirf 12 characters tak reduce ho jaata hai. Isliye build karte time tag karna good practice hai:

$ docker build -t localbuild:removeme .
$ docker images localbuild
REPOSITORY   TAG        IMAGE ID       SIZE
localbuild   removeme   3ca470de8dbd   294MB

Image change nahi hui, to build speedy tha aur build system ne internally already built image ko tag kar diya. Naming aur tagging images ko registry mein push karte time madad karta hai.

Push aur pull — registry se sharing

Push karne ke liye tumhe repository own karna hoga — warna push denied hoga. Re-tag karo apne registry account aur destination se, phir push karo:

$ docker tag localbuild:removeme [username]/removeme
$ docker push [username]/removeme
958488a3c11e: Pushed
latest: digest: sha256:a022eea71ca955cafb4d38b12c28b9de59dbb3d9fcb54b size: 741

Registry — is case mein Docker Hub — par ab recently pushed image available hai. Agar account open hai aur registry access restrict nahi kar rahi, to koi bhi docker pull [username]/removeme se image pull kar sakta hai. Ye revolutionary feel hona chahiye — How do I install your software? ka jawab ab ban gaya hai just pull the container, almost kisi bhi cheez ke liye.

Container run karna — SSH nahi, docker exec

VMs chalate time SSH daemon enable karke port expose karna common practice thi. Containers mein SSH access ki zaroorat nahi hai — enable kar sakte ho aur kaam bhi karega, lekin running container access karne ka ye tareeka nahi hai.

$ docker run -ti -d --name centos-test --rm centos:8 /bin/bash
$ docker ps

Flags samjho: -ti TTY allocate karta hai aur stdin attach karta hai taaki baad mein terminal mein interact kar sako. -d container ko background mein chalata hai taaki current terminal control na le. --name naam deta hai, aur --rm container ko stop hone ke baad remove kar deta hai. Command ke baad digest return hota hai jo batata hai container start ho gaya hai.

Kuch containers ENTRYPOINT (aur optionally CMD) instruction ke saath create hote hain — ye instructions container ko kisi specific task ke liye up aur running karne ke liye hoti hain. CentOS example mein /bin/bash specify karna pada kyunki warna container running nahi rehta. Dockerfile mein ENTRYPOINT add karo:

FROM centos:8
RUN dnf install -y python38
ENTRYPOINT ["/bin/bash"]

Ab background mein bina /bin/bash specify kiye run kar sakte ho. Running container mein access ke liye docker exec use karo:

$ docker exec -it 023c8e67d91f bash
[root@023c8e67d91f /]# whoami
root
$ docker exec 023c8e67d91f tail /var/log/dnf.log

Sirf command run karni ho to -it flag omit kar sakte ho. Ek common aspect hai container ka size jitna ho sake chhota rakhna — isliye CentOS container mein newly installed CentOS VM se bahut kam packages honge. Isse surprising experiences hote hain jab tum expect karte ho ki koi package present hoga, jaise text editor Vim, aur wo nahi hota.

Best practices — linting, pinning, aur vulnerability scanning

Nayi language ya tool try karte time pehla kaam hai ek linter dhoondhna. Dockerfile ke liye linters mein se ek hai hadolint, jo conveniently ek container ke roop mein packaged hai:

$ docker run --rm -i hadolint/hadolint < Dockerfile
DL3013 Pin versions in pip.
Instead of `pip install <package>` use `pip install <package>==<version>`

Pinning packages hamesha great idea hai kyunki dependency ke update se tumhara code incompatible hone se safe rehta hai. Lekin pinned dependencies ko kabhi update na karna bhi great idea nahi hai — wapas aakar check karo ki update karna useful hoga ya nahi. Linting ko automate karne ka mauka dhoondho — manual step hatao, aur essential pieces par concentrate karo.

Har RUN instruction par ek nayi layer create hoti hai. Containers individual layers se bane hote hain, to layers jitni kam, container ka size utna chhota. Isliye alag-alag RUN ke bajaye ek hi line mein kai dependencies install karna preferable hai, && se chain karke:

RUN apk add --no-cache python3 && python3 -m ensurepip && pip3 install pytest

Aur ek critical piece hai vulnerabilities check karna. Container preinstalled libraries ke saath aata hai — ye ek full operating system hai jo build time par extra dependencies pull karega. Flask jaise framework se trained model serve kar rahe ho to uske ya uski dependencies ke Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) ho sakte hain. Flask version 1.1.2 ki dependencies hain click, itsdangerous, Jinja2, MarkupSafe, aur Werkzeug. CVE kisi bhi time report ho sakta hai — aaj version vulnerable nahi hai, kal subah naya CVE discover ho sakta hai.

Ek fast aur easy solution hai Anchore ka grype command line tool. Mac par brew tap anchore/grype aur brew install grype se install karo, Linux par curl se install script chalao. Phir container ke against run karo:

$ grype python:3.8
$ grype python:3.8 | grep High
$ grype --fail-on=high centos:8

Example mein python:3.8 image mein 1540 vulnerabilities mili, aur High severity filter karne par CVE-2020-8492 mila jo Python 2.7 se related tha — application Python 3.8 use karta hai, to ye container vulnerable nahi hai, lekin ab tumhe pata hai kya vulnerable hai aur production deployment ka executive decision le sakte ho. --fail-on=high se specific vulnerability level par fail karna ek aur check hai jo linting ke saath automate kar sakte ho.

Yaad rakho: Container mein SSH nahi, docker exec use karo. Har image ko tag karo, versions pin karo, RUN instructions ko && se ek layer mein chain karo, aur grype se vulnerabilities scan karo. Bina tag ke image sirf ek digest hai, use pehchan na mushkil hai.
Book ka poora code — official repo se (code cells/files only, outputs nahi):
Dockerfile — chapter3/Dockerfile
FROM debian:stable

RUN apt-get update && apt install -yq curl build-essential gnupg

RUN curl https://packages.cloud.google.com/apt/doc/apt-key.gpg |  apt-key add -

RUN echo "deb https://packages.cloud.google.com/apt coral-edgetpu-stable main" |  tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/coral-edgetpu.list

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -yq edgetpu-compiler

CMD ["/bin/bash"]
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — MLOps for Containers and Edge Devices
← Previous03 · MLOps for Containers and Edge Devices→ Next03.2 · Serving a Trained Model Over HTTP
03.2Chapter 3 · MLOps for Containers and Edge Devices

Serving a Trained Model Over HTTP

Ab containers ke core concepts clear hain, to ek container banao jo Flask web framework se trained model ko HTTP API par serve kare. Model hai Boston Housing prediction, aur poora project sirf kuch files ka hai — Dockerfile, requirements.txt, aur webapp directory.

Dockerfile — version label ke saath

Har cheez Dockerfile se shuru hoti hai. Assume karo ki requirements.txt current working directory mein present hai:

FROM python:3.7
ARG VERSION
LABEL org.label-schema.version=$VERSION
COPY ./requirements.txt /webapp/requirements.txt
WORKDIR /webapp
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
COPY webapp/* /webapp
ENTRYPOINT [ "python" ]
CMD [ "app.py" ]

Is file mein kuch nayi cheezein hain. Pehle, VERSION naam ka argument define hota hai jo LABEL ke liye variable ki tarah use hota hai. Label schema convention labels ke naam normalize karne ke liye useful hai. Version add karna container ke baare mein informational metadata dene ka helpful tareeka hai — baad mein trained model ka version identify karne ke liye use hoga. Imagine karo container expected accuracy nahi de raha — label se problematic model ka version identify karne mein madad milti hai. Ek label yahan use hua hai, lekin zyada descriptive labels aur bhi behtar honge.

Image Python 3.7 use karti hai kyunki likhne ke time kuch dependencies Python 3.8 ke saath kaam nahi karti thi. Tum 3.7 ko 3.8 se swap karke check kar sakte ho ki ab kaam karta hai ya nahi.

requirements.txt aur app.py

requirements.txt mein ye dependencies hain:

Flask==1.1.2
pandas==0.24.2
scikit-learn==0.20.3

Ab webapp naam ki nayi directory banao taaki web files ek jagah hon, aur app.py add karo:

from flask import Flask, request, jsonify
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.externals import joblib
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

app = Flask(__name__)

def scale(payload):
    scaler = StandardScaler().fit(payload)
    return scaler.transform(payload)

@app.route("/")
def home():
    return "<h3>Sklearn Prediction Container</h3>"

@app.route("/predict", methods=['POST'])
def predict():
    clf = joblib.load("boston_housing_prediction.joblib")
    inference_payload = pd.DataFrame(request.json)
    scaled_payload = scale(inference_payload)
    prediction = list(clf.predict(scaled_payload))
    return jsonify({'prediction': prediction})

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=5000, debug=True)

predict route ka input sample JSON hai — CHAS, RM, TAX, PTRATIO, B, LSTAT jaise Boston Housing features — aur output sample hai { "prediction": [ 20.35373177134412 ] }. Flow ye hai: joblib se trained model load karo, request JSON ko Pandas DataFrame mein daalo, StandardScaler se scale karo, predict karo, aur jsonify se prediction return karo.

Trained model aur project structure

Aakhri file hai trained model. Boston Housing prediction dataset train kar rahe ho to use webapp directory mein app.py ke saath rakho aur naam do boston_housing_prediction.joblib. Trained version book ke GitHub repository mein bhi mil sakta hai. Final structure ye honi chahiye:

.
├── Dockerfile
└── webapp
    ├── app.py
    └── boston_housing_prediction.joblib
1 directory, 3 files

Build aur run karna

Container build karo. Example mein Azure se mila run ID version ke roop mein use hua hai taaki identify karna aasan ho ki model kahan se aaya — tum alag version use kar sakte ho, ya koi version nahi bhi:

$ docker build --build-arg VERSION=AutoML_287f444c -t flask-predict .
$ docker images flask-predict
REPOSITORY     TAG      IMAGE ID       SIZE
flask-predict  latest   5487a63442aa   1.15GB

Ab container ko background mein run karo, port 5000 expose karke, aur verify karo ki chal raha hai:

$ docker run -p 5000:5000 -d --name flask-predict flask-predict
$ docker ps
CONTAINER ID  IMAGE          STATUS       PORTS
d95ab6581429  flask-predict  Up 2 seconds 0.0.0.0:5000->5000/tcp

Browser mein http://localhost:5000 kholo — home() function ka HTML Sklearn Prediction application se welcome karega. curl se bhi verify kar sakte ho: curl 192.168.0.200:5000 se wahi h3 milega.

Prediction test karna — requests se POST

Koi bhi tool jo HTTP par information bhej sakta hai aur response process kar sakta hai, use kar sakte ho. Ye example Python mein requests library se kuch lines mein POST request bhejta hai sample JSON data ke saath:

import requests
import json

url = "http://localhost:5000/predict"
data = {
    "CHAS": {"0": 0},
    "RM": {"0": 6.575},
    "TAX": {"0": 296.0},
    "PTRATIO": {"0": 15.3},
    "B": {"0": 396.9},
    "LSTAT": {"0": 4.98},
}
input_data = json.dumps(data)
headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
resp = requests.post(url, input_data, headers=headers)
print(resp.text)

Python code ko predict.py naam ki file mein likho aur execute karo:

$ python predict.py
{
  "prediction": [
    20.35373177134412
  ]
}

Containerizing deployments ek excellent tareeka hai portable data banane ka jo dusre try kar sakte hain. Container share karke environment set up karne ka friction greatly reduce ho jaata hai, aur interact karne ke liye repeatable system ensure hota hai. Ab tum containers create, run, debug aur deploy kar sakte ho ML ke liye — isse noncontainerized environments ko automate karke production deployments fast aur robust banaye ja sakte hain.

Yaad rakho: Flask app mein do routes hain — / home ke liye aur /predict POST ke liye. Model joblib file se load hota hai, input StandardScaler se scale hota hai, aur output JSON prediction hota hai. Version label se pata chalta hai kaunsa model container ke andar hai.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — MLOps for Containers and Edge Devices
← Previous03.1 · Containers — Runtime, Creating, Running→ Next03.3 · Edge Devices — Coral, Azure Percept, TFHub
03.3Chapter 3 · MLOps for Containers and Edge Devices

Edge Devices — Coral, Azure Percept, TFHub

Fast inferencing ki computational cost kuch saal pehle astronomical thi. Aaj costs kam ho gayi hain aur zyada powerful chips ban rahe hain — kuch chips explicitly ML tasks ke liye tailored hain. Isi se edge devices possible hue hain: fast, small, aur ML ke liye bane hue.

Edge kya hai — aur kyun zaroori hai?

Deploying to the edge ka matlab hai compute devices jo data center ke andar thousands of servers ke saath nahi hain. Mobile phones, Raspberry Pi, aur smart home devices edge devices ke examples hain. General idea hai ki computational resources user ke jitne kareeb honge, user experience utna fast hoga. Specialized chips chhote, fast aur effective ho rahe hain, to future mein zyada ML edge par hoga.

Distance ka asar samjho: Peru ke paas South America se connect karne wale submarine cables hain lekin US se direct connectivity nahi hai. Agar Peru se US data center mein hosted service par picture upload kar rahe ho, to Panama jaise desh se exponentially zyada time lagega jiske paas North America jaane wale multiple cables hain. Ye trivial picture upload ka example hai — ML predictions jaise computational operations par to aur bhi bura hota hai. Aur imagine karo jab connectivity hi na ho ya bahut limited ho, jaise remote farm. Wahan fast inferencing chahiye to options limited hain, aur edge deployment ka data center par advantage hai. Users ko spoon ki parwah nahi hai — unhe soup try karne ka seamless tareeka chahiye.

Coral — USB Accelerator aur Edge TPU

Coral Project ek platform hai jo local on-device inferencing banane mein madad karta hai — edge deployments ka essence: fast, user ke kareeb, aur offline. Is section mein USB Accelerator cover hota hai, ek edge device jo saare major operating systems support karta hai aur TensorFlow Lite models ke saath achha kaam karta hai. Zyaada tar TensorFlow Lite models ko compile karke is edge TPU (Tensor Processing Unit) par chalaya ja sakta hai.

ML operationalize karte time device support, installation methods, aur compatibility ke baare mein aware rehna padta hai — Coral Edge TPU ke baare mein ye teeno sach hain: ye zyaada tar operating systems par kaam karta hai, TensorFlow Lite models ke saath jab tak wo TPU par chalne ke liye compile ho sakein.

Runtime install karne ke liye file download karke unzip karo aur installer script chalao:

$ curl -O https://dl.google.com/coral/edgetpu_api/edgetpu_runtime_20201204.zip
$ unzip edgetpu_runtime_20201204.zip
$ cd edgetpu_runtime
$ sudo bash install.sh

Ye setup examples Macintosh computer use karte hain, to dusre operating systems par installation methods aur dependencies vary karenge — getting started guide check karo.

Coral se image classification karna

Coral team ka useful repository hai jismein Python3 code hai jo ek command se image classification chalata hai. Directory banao aur repository clone karo — --depth 1 flag se shallow clone hota hai, jo desirable hai jab repository ki poori history nahi chahiye:

$ mkdir google-coral && cd google-coral
$ git clone https://github.com/google-coral/tflite --depth 1
$ cd tflite/python/examples/classification

install_requirements.sh script pehle mat chalao. Pehle Python3 se naya virtual environment banao, activate karo, aur ensure karo ki Python interpreter virtual environment ki taraf point kare, system Python ki taraf nahi:

$ python3 -m venv venv
$ source venv/bin/activate
$ which python
$ pip install numpy Pillow
$ pip install https://github.com/google-coral/pycoral/releases/download/release-frogfish/tflite_runtime-2.5.0-cp38-cp38-macosx_10_15_x86_64.whl

Ye long link crucial hai aur tumhare platform aur architecture se match karna chahiye — bina is library ke Coral device se interact karna possible nahi hai. TensorFlow Lite ke liye Python installation guide se double-check karo ki tumhare platform ke liye kaunsa link chahiye.

Ab classify_image.py script chalakar help menu lao — ye verify karne ka excellent tareeka hai ki saari dependencies install hui hain aur script kaam karti hai. Bina flags ke chalane par error aayega ki -m/--model aur -i/--input required hain. Coral AI site ke models section se iNat insects wala model dhoondho jo 1000 se zyada types ke insects recognize karta hai. tflite model aur labels dono download karo. Sample image ke liye ek common fly ki image lo. Directories banao — models, labels, aur images — aur files ko respectively unmein rakho:

.
├── classify_image.py
├── images
│   └── macro-1802322_640.jpg
├── labels
│   └── inat_insect_labels.txt
└── models
    └── mobilenet_v2_1.0_224_inat_insect_quant_edgetpu.tflite

Ab classification chalao — device USB cable se plugged in hona chahiye, warna long traceback aayega jo clearly explain nahi karta ki problem kya hai — Failed to load delegate from libedgetpu.1.dylib ka matlab hai device unplugged hai:

$ python3 classify_image.py   --model models/mobilenet_v2_1.0_224_inat_insect_quant_edgetpu.tflite   --labels labels/inat_insect_labels.txt   --input images/macro-1802322_640.jpg
----INFERENCE TIME---
11.9ms
2.6ms
2.5ms
-------RESULTS-------
Lucilia sericata (Common Green Bottle Fly): 0.43359

Image correctly classify hui — common fly detect hui! Note karo ki Edge TPU par pehli inference slow hoti hai kyunki model ko Edge TPU memory mein load karna included hai, uske baad inference 2.5ms ke aas-paas ho jaati hai. Dusri insect pictures lekar command dobara chalakar check karo ki model different inputs par kaisa perform karta hai.

Azure Percept — poora platform, sirf hardware nahi

Jab book likhi ja rahi thi, Microsoft ne Azure Percept naam ka platform aur hardware announce kiya tha. Hands-on practical examples ke liye time nahi mila, lekin iski functionality mention karne layak hai. Coral device aur edge ke general concepts wahi apply hote hain: ye seamless ML operations edge par allow karte hain.

Emphasize karna important hai ki Percept products zyada tar hardware ke roop mein advertise hote hain, lekin Azure Percept edge computing ke liye ek poora platform hai — devices se lekar deployment, training aur management tak Azure mein. Major AI platforms jaise ONNX aur TensorFlow ka support bhi hai, jisse prebuilt models try karna aasan hota hai. Ek downside hai ki Coral devices ke comparison mein Azure Percept hardware bahut zyada expensive hai, jisse ek bundle khareed kar nayi technology try karna mushkil ho jaata hai. Microsoft ne documenting aur context aur examples add karne mein stellar job kiya hai, jo explore karne layak hain.

TFHub — pretrained models ka repository

TensorFlow models dhoondhne ke liye ek great resource hai TensorFlow Hub. Hub thousands of pretrained models ka repository hai jo use karne ke liye ready hain. Coral Edge TPU ke liye saare models kaam nahi karenge — TPU ke alag instructions hain, to model ko explicitly uske liye compile karna padta hai.

Hub par Coral model format available hai — us par click karo to TPU ke liye ready models milenge. MobileNet Quantized V2 model select karo download ke liye — ye images se 1000 se zyada objects detect kar sakta hai. Coral examples mein labels aur model dono chahiye, to dono download karna ensure karo. TFHub website par models present karte time multiple formats available hote hain — double-check karo ki kaunsa model format le rahe ho aur wo Coral device ke saath compatible hai.

Non-TPU models ko port karna — container se compiler

Kuch situations mein tumhe jo model chahiye wo available hai lekin TPU device ke liye compiled nahi hai. Coral Edge TPU ka compiler available hai, lekin wo har platform par installable nahi hai — compiler documentation mein Debian ya Ubuntu Linux distribution chahiye. Agar tum Apple computer par kaam kar rahe ho aur dusra Linux computer nahi hai, to container runtime ka use karo — yehi perfect use case hai.

Ek naya Dockerfile banao jo Debian-based container banaye compiler ke liye sab kuch installed ke saath:

FROM debian:stable
RUN apt-get update && apt install -yq curl build-essential gnupg
RUN curl https://packages.cloud.google.com/apt/doc/apt-key.gpg | apt-key add
RUN echo "deb https://packages.cloud.google.com/apt coral-edgetpu-stable main" | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/coral-edgetpu.list
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -yq edgetpu-compiler
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

Image banao: docker build -t tpu-compiler .. Sirf wahi models compiler ke saath kaam karenge jo precompiled hain TensorFlow Lite ke liye aur quantized hain — download karne se pehle ensure karo ki model dono hai, tflite aur quantized. Model download karo:

$ wget -O mobilenet_v1_50_160_quantized.tflite https://tfhub.dev/tensorflow/lite-model/mobilenet_v1_0.50_160_quantized/1/default/1?lite-format=tflite

Downloaded model ko container mein le jaane aur files wapas copy karne ke liye Docker ka bind mount use karo — ye tumhari machine ka path container mein link karta hai, effectively jo kuch hai use share karta hai. Container mein banayi files automatically local environment mein dikhengi:

$ docker run -it -v ${PWD}:/models tpu-compiler
root@5125dcd1da4b:/# cd models
root@5125dcd1da4b:/models# ls
mobilenet_v1_50_160_quantized.tflite
$ edgetpu_compiler --help
$ edgetpu_compiler mobilenet_v1_50_160_quantized.tflite
Edge TPU Compiler version 15.0.340273435
Model compiled successfully in 787 ms.
Input size: 1.30MiB
Output model: mobilenet_v1_50_160_quantized_edgetpu.tflite
Output size: 1.54MiB
Number of Edge TPU subgraphs: 1
Total number of operations: 31

Operation ek second se bhi kam mein chali aur newly compiled model banaya jo ab edge device ke saath use kar sakte ho. Container se exit karo aur local machine par list karo — original model, log file, aur _edgetpu.tflite model teenon dikhenge. Ye ek handy workaround hai kisi tool ke liye operating system require karne ka — ab is container ko aur automate kiya ja sakta hai, kuch lines ki script se models port karke. Nonquantized model try karne par compiler error dega: Invalid model, Model not quantized.

Containers for managed ML systems aur monetizing

Advanced next-generation MLOps workflows ke heart mein managed ML systems hain jaise AWS SageMaker, Azure ML Studio, aur Google Vertex AI. Ye saare systems containers par build hote hain — containers MLOps ka secret ingredient hain. Bina containerization ke SageMaker jaise technologies develop aur use karna bahut zyada challenging hota. SageMaker mein EC2 Container Registry woh location hai jahan inference code image aur training code rehte hain. Is process se DevOps best practices images banane mein bake ho jaati hain — sabse important, continuous integration aur continuous delivery. Containers poori ML architecture ki quality badhate hain kyunki images already baked hoti hain — intellectual horsepower dusri problems par shift ho sakti hai jaise data drift, feature store, ya evaluate karna ki naya model customer needs solve karta hai ya nahi.

Monetizing MLOps mein bhi containers role play karte hain. SageMaker mein AWS Marketplace mein becha jaane wala algorithm ya model hi delivery ka mode hai. Container ko product ki tarah bechna aisa hai jaise physical store mein peanut butter, flour ya milk bechna — company ko sirf high-quality peanut butter banane par focus karna hai, use bechne ke liye stores ka network banane par nahi. Waise hi ML monetize karne wali companies ke liye container models aur algorithms deliver karne ka ideal package hai.

Yaad rakho: Edge par inference fast, offline aur user ke kareeb hoti hai. Coral ke liye model TensorFlow Lite aur quantized hona chahiye, aur pehli inference slow hoti hai kyunki model memory mein load hota hai. Compiler Debian/Ubuntu mangta hai — Mac par ho to container se kaam chalao.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — MLOps for Containers and Edge Devices
← Previous03.2 · Serving a Trained Model Over HTTP→ Next04 · Continuous Delivery for Machine Learning Models
04Chapter 4 · Continuous Delivery for Machine Learning Models

Continuous Delivery for Machine Learning Models

Continuous ka matlab hai persistence ya recurrence of a process — ek process ka baar-baar hona. CI/CD aksar saath mein mention hote hain jab system ki baat hoti hai jo artifacts ko build, verify aur deploy karta hai. Ye chapter batata hai ki ek robust process kaisa dikhta hai aur models ko production mein ship karne ke liye pipeline implement ya improve kaise karein.

Constant evaluation — injury wali kahani

Chapter ek athlete ki kahani se shuru hota hai. High-performance athlete season ke beech mein days off afford nahi kar sakta. Agar plan saat din workout ka hai, to saaton din se guzarna critical hai — ek din miss karne se ab tak ke workouts diminish ho sakte hain ya poori tarah wipe out ho sakte hain. Workouts wheelbarrow ko uphill push karne jaise hain — ek workout miss karna matlab side mein hatna aur wheelbarrow ko downhill jaane dena, phir wapas jaakar use uthakar phir se push karna padega.

Injury ho to jaldi se full shape mein wapas aana priority hai, aur alternative workouts dhoondhna bhi — hamstring hurt kar rahi hai aur run nahi kar sakte to pool mein cardio continue karo, hill repeats nahi kar sakte kyunki toe toot gaya to bike par wahi hills tackle karo. Injuries ko war strategy chahiye; haar manna option nahi hai, retreat karna ho to least possible retreat karo. Recovery ke liye constant evaluation chahiye: har din pehle assess karo ki injury same hai, worse hai, ya better hai. Worse hai to previous workouts change karo, same hai to last week ya month se compare karo, better hai to current strategy continue karo. Pain foe nahi hai — ye indicator hai jo decide karne mein madad karta hai ki jo kar rahe ho wo continue karo ya roko aur rethink karo.

Constant evaluation, feedback par changes aur adaptation, aur success achieve karne ke liye nayi strategies apply karna — yehi exactly continuous integration (CI) aur continuous delivery (CD) hain. Aaj bhi, jab robust deployment strategies ki information easily available hai, businesses bina tests ke ya poor testing strategy ke saath milte hain, ya releases jo weeks aur months lete hain. Ek bade open source project ka naya release cut karne mein kabhi-kabhi ek hafta lag jaata tha, aur QA lead har team lead ko email bhejta tha poochne ke liye ki kya wo release ke liye ready feel karte hain. Emails bhejna aur alag-alag replies ka wait karna software release karne ka straightforward tareeka nahi hai — ye error-prone aur highly inconsistent hai. CI/CD platforms aur steps ka feedback loop invaluable hai. Agar problem mile to use automate karke hata do taaki agle release mein wo problem hi na rahe.

Is chapter mein kya seekhoge

  • Packaging for ML models: ONNX model ko container mein package karna aur Flask app se sentiment prediction serve karna.
  • Infrastructure as Code aur cloud pipelines: GitHub Actions se model ko Azure se pull karna, container build karna, aur registry mein publish karna — bina manual steps ke.
  • Controlled rollout: Blue-green aur canary deployments se naye model ko dheere-dheere production mein laana, aur rollback karna.
  • Testing techniques: Automated checks, linting, aur shift left — jitni jaldi error detect karo, utna sasta fix hoga.

Shipping models into production number one objective hai, lekin bahut high confidence ke saath, resilient steps mein karna — yehi tumhe strive karna chahiye. Tumhara task processes jagah par aane ke baad khatm nahi hota. Tumhe hamesha tareeke dhoondhte rehna hai jinse tum khud ko baad mein thank karo — ye pooch kar: aaj main kya add kar sakta hoon jo meri life aasan bana de agar ye process fail ho jaaye? Aur workflows aise banao jinmein aur checks aur verifications add karna aasan ho. Agar add karna mushkil hai, to koi use touch nahi karna chahega, aur robust pipeline ka purpose hi defeat ho jayega.

Yaad rakho: Continuous matlab baar-baar, persistence. Injury ki tarah model deployment mein bhi constant evaluation chahiye — same, worse, ya better? Problem mile to use automate karke hata do, taaki agle release mein wo dobara na aaye.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 4 — Continuous Delivery for Machine Learning Models
← Previous03.3 · Edge Devices — Coral, Azure Percept, TFHub→ Next04.1 · Packaging for ML Models
04.1Chapter 4 · Continuous Delivery for Machine Learning Models

Packaging for ML Models

Packaging ML models ka matlab koi special OS package jaise RPM ya DEB file nahi hai. Iska matlab hai model ko container mein daalna taaki containerized processes ka fayda mile — sharing, distributing, aur easy deployment. Container runtime installed ho to kisi bhi operating system par model ko quickly try karna ek dream scenario hai.

Packaging ki teen characteristics

  • Locally run karna effortless hai: Jab tak container runtime installed hai, container ko locally chalana effortless hai.
  • Cloud mein deploy karne ke plenty options hain: Zaroorat ke hisab se scale up ya down karne ki ability ke saath.
  • Dusre easily try kar sakte hain: Dusre log container ke saath quickly try kar sakte hain aur interact kar sakte hain.

In characteristics ke benefits ye hain ki maintainability less complicated ho jaati hai, aur nonperformant model ko locally ya cloud offering mein debug karna terminal mein kuch commands jitna simple ho sakta hai. Deployment strategy jitni complicated hogi, potential issues troubleshoot aur investigate karna utna difficult hoga.

Example — RoBERTa ONNX model se sentiment analysis

Is section mein ek ONNX model use hota hai jo Flask app serve karne wale container ke andar package hota hai aur prediction karta hai. Model hai RoBERTaSequenceClassification ONNX model, jo bahut well documented hai. Naya Git repository banane ke baad pehla step hai dependencies figure out karna. requirements.txt file ye hai:

simpletransformers==0.4.0
tensorboardX==1.9
transformers==2.1.0
flask==1.1.2
torch==1.7.1
onnxruntime==1.6.0

Phir Dockerfile banao jo container mein sab kuch install kare:

FROM python:3.8
COPY ./requirements.txt /webapp/requirements.txt
WORKDIR /webapp
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
COPY webapp/* /webapp
ENTRYPOINT [ "python" ]
CMD [ "app.py" ]

Dockerfile requirements file copy karta hai, webapp directory banata hai, aur application code ko ek app.py file mein copy karta hai.

app.py — tokenizer aur ONNX session

webapp/app.py banao jo sentiment analysis kare. Shuruaat mein imports aur ONNX runtime session banane ke liye jo chahiye wo add karo:

from flask import Flask, request, jsonify
import torch
import numpy as np
from transformers import RobertaTokenizer
import onnxruntime

app = Flask(__name__)
tokenizer = RobertaTokenizer.from_pretrained("roberta-base")
session = onnxruntime.InferenceSession("roberta-sequence-classification-9.onnx")

Ye pehla hissa Flask application banata hai, model ke saath use karne ke liye tokenizer define karta hai, aur finally ONNX runtime session initialize karta hai jiske liye model ka path pass karna hota hai. Phir Flask route add karo jo live inferencing enable kare:

@app.route("/predict", methods=["POST"])
def predict():
    input_ids = torch.tensor(
        tokenizer.encode(request.json[0], add_special_tokens=True)
    ).unsqueeze(0)
    if input_ids.requires_grad:
        numpy_func = input_ids.detach().cpu().numpy()
    else:
        numpy_func = input_ids.cpu().numpy()
    inputs = {session.get_inputs()[0].name: numpy_func(input_ids)}
    out = session.run(None, inputs)
    result = np.argmax(out)
    return jsonify({"positive": bool(result)})

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(host="0.0.0.0", port=5000, debug=True)

predict() function ek Flask route hai jo /predict URL enable karta hai jab application chal rahi ho. Ye function sirf POST HTTP methods allow karta hai. Input ek JSON-formatted request hai — ek array jismein ek string hai — aur response ek JSON object hai jismein positive key hai jo sentence ka sentiment indicate karti hai.

Model download aur project structure

Ek critical part abhi missing hai — ONNX model exist nahi karta. RoBERTaSequenceClassification ONNX model locally download karo aur project ke root par rakho. Final project structure ye honi chahiye:

.
├── Dockerfile
├── requirements.txt
├── roberta-sequence-classification-9.onnx
└── webapp
    └── app.py
1 directory, 4 files

Ek aakhri cheez missing hai build se pehle — Dockerfile mein model ko container mein copy karne ki instruction nahi hai. app.py ko model roberta-sequence-classification-9.onnx /webapp directory mein chahiye. Dockerfile update karo:

COPY roberta-sequence-classification-9.onnx /webapp

Locally verify karo, phir container banao

Container build karne se pehle double-check karo ki sab kaam karta hai. Naya virtual environment banao, activate karo, aur dependencies install karo:

$ python3 -m venv venv
$ source venv/bin/activate
$ pip install -r requirements.txt

ONNX model project ke root par hai, lekin application use /webapp directory mein chahti hai, to use us directory ke andar move karo taaki Flask app complain na kare — ye extra step container chalte time needed nahi hai:

$ mv roberta-sequence-classification-9.onnx webapp/
$ cd webapp
$ python app.py
* Serving Flask app "app" (lazy loading)
* Running on http://0.0.0.0:5000/ (Press CTRL+C to quit)

Ab application HTTP requests consume karne ke liye ready hai. curl se sample payload bhejkar sentiment detect karo:

$ curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/JSON" --data '["Containers are more or less interesting"]' http://0.0.0.0:5000/predict
{
  "positive": false
}
$ curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data '["MLOps is critical for robustness"]' http://0.0.0.0:5000/predict
{
  "positive": true
}

Ab container locally banao aur meaningful tag do, phir run karo aur same tareeke se interact karo:

$ docker build -t [username]/roberta .
$ docker run -it -p 5000:5000 --rm [username]/roberta
$ curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data '["espresso is too strong"]' http://0.0.0.0:5000/predict
{
  "positive": false
}

Ye saare steps overwhelming lag sakte hain, lekin challenging processes automate karne aur continuous delivery patterns leverage karne ka perfect opportunity hain. Agle section mein ye sab automate hoga — container ko container registry mein publish karna jo koi bhi consume kar sake.

Yaad rakho: Packaging matlab model ko container mein daalna, RPM/DEB nahi. Pehle locally verify karo (venv, pip install, python app.py, curl test), phir docker build aur docker run karo. Model ko Dockerfile mein COPY karna mat bhoolo, warna app use dhoondh nahi payegi.
Book ka poora code — official repo se (code cells/files only, outputs nahi):
app.py — Flask webapp — chapter4/packaging-containers/webapp/app.py
from flask import Flask, request, jsonify
import torch
import numpy as np
from transformers import RobertaTokenizer
import onnxruntime


app = Flask(__name__)
tokenizer = RobertaTokenizer.from_pretrained("roberta-base")
session = onnxruntime.InferenceSession("roberta-sequence-classification-9.onnx")


def to_numpy(tensor):
    return (
        tensor.detach().cpu().numpy() if tensor.requires_grad else tensor.cpu().numpy()
    )


@app.route("/")
def home():
    return "<h3>RoBERTa Sentiment Analysis Prediction Container</h3>"


@app.route("/predict", methods=["POST"])
def predict():
    """
    Input sample:

        [ "Containers are good" ]

    Output sample:

        {"postive": True}
    """
    input_ids = torch.tensor(
        tokenizer.encode(request.json[0], add_special_tokens=True)
    ).unsqueeze(
        0
    )

    if input_ids.requires_grad:
        numpy_func = input_ids.detach().cpu().numpy()
    else:
        numpy_func = input_ids.cpu().numpy()

    inputs = {session.get_inputs()[0].name: numpy_func}
    out = session.run(None, inputs)

    result = np.argmax(out)

    return jsonify({"positive": bool(result)})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(host="0.0.0.0", port=5000, debug=True)
minimal.py — chapter4/packaging-containers/webapp/minimal.py
from flask import Flask, request, jsonify
import torch
import numpy as np
#from transformers import RobertaTokenizer
import onnxruntime


app = Flask(__name__)
tokenizer = RobertaTokenizer.from_pretrained("roberta-base")
session = onnxruntime.InferenceSession(
    "roberta-sequence-classification-9.onnx"
)


@app.route("/predict", methods=["POST"])
def predict():
    input_ids = torch.tensor(
        tokenizer.encode(request.json[0], add_special_tokens=True)
    ).unsqueeze(0)

    if input_ids.requires_grad:
        numpy_func = input_ids.detach().cpu().numpy()
    else:
        numpy_func = input_ids.cpu().numpy()

    inputs = {session.get_inputs()[0].name: numpy_func(input_ids)}
    out = session.run(None, inputs)

    result = np.argmax(out)

    return jsonify({"positive": bool(result)})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(host="0.0.0.0", port=5000, debug=True)

← Previous04 · Continuous Delivery for Machine Learning Models→ Next04.2 · Infrastructure as Code and Cloud Pipelines
04.2Chapter 4 · Continuous Delivery for Machine Learning Models

Infrastructure as Code and Cloud Pipelines

Ek baar ek public repository mein kuch test container images thi jo test infrastructure widely use karta tha. Ek library ko update karna tha, lekin images banane wali files kahin nahi mili — kisi engineer ne locally build karke images registry mein upload kar di thi. Yehi problem ML mein bhi hoti hai: manual aur complex cheezon ko automate karne ka hamesha opportunity hai. Is section mein GitHub Actions aur cloud pipelines se wo automation banate hain.

Lost Dockerfile wali kahani — automation kyun?

Images ko container registry jaise Docker Hub mein host karna repeatable builds aur reliable tests ke liye pehle se hi ek great step hai. Lekin jab files lost ho jaayein, to simple change bhi nahi kar sakte kyunki image banane ke liye needed files hi nahi hain. Experienced container developers zyada tar files rebuild karne ka tareeka dhoondh sakte hain, lekin point ye nahi hai. Aage badhne ka step hai automation banana jo known source files, Dockerfile samet, se containers automatically build kar sake. Container ko update karke registry mein dobara upload karna aisa hai jaise blackout mein candles aur flashlights dhoondhna, jabki generator hona chahiye jo power jaate hi automatically start ho jaaye.

Jab aisi situation ho, to blame karne ke bajaye analytical bano aur process enhance karne ka opportunity use karo. ML mein bhi hum manual aur complex cheezon ke aadi ho jaate hain, lekin hamesha automate karne ka opportunity hai.

Problem scenario — model Azure mein, files GitHub mein

Assume karo kisi ne Docker Hub mein ek model wala container banaya hai. Koi nahi jaanta trained model container mein kaise aaya, koi docs nahi hain, aur updates chahiye. Thodi complexity add karo: model kisi repository mein nahi hai, lekin Azure mein registered model ke roop mein rehta hai. Automation se is problem ko solve karte hain.

Models ko GitHub repository mein add karna tempting ho sakta hai. Ye certainly possible hai, lekin GitHub ki hard file limit hai 100 MB — agar model is size ke kareeb hai, to use repository mein add nahi kar paoge. Aur Git version control system binary files version karne ke liye meant nahi hai aur iska side-effect hai huge repositories banana. Isliye model ko repo mein daalne ke bajaye Azure se pull karna behtar hai.

Model Azure ML platform par available hai aur pehle se registered hai — Azure ML Studio mein Models section mein Register model par click karke register karo, form bharo, aur Upload file field se locally downloaded model upload karo. Phir Packaging section wala hi project reuse karo. Saara heavy lifting local live inferencing ke liye ho chuka hai, to naya GitHub repository banao aur ONNX model ke alawa project contents add karo. .gitignore file banao taaki model galti se add na ho:

*onnx

GitHub Actions workflow — main.yml

Contents push karne ke baad automation shuru karne ke liye ready ho. GitHub Actions use karo, jo ek continuous delivery workflow YAML file mein banane deta hai jo configurable conditions meet hone par trigger hota hai. Idea ye hai ki jab bhi repository ki main branch mein change ho, platform Azure se registered model pull kare, container create kare, aur aakhir mein use container registry mein push kare. Project ke root par .github/workflows/ directory banao aur main.yml add karo:

name: Build and package RoBERTa-sequencing to Dockerhub
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  workflow_dispatch:

Ab build job define karo jo sab kuch jodta hai:

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v2
    - name: Authenticate with Azure
      uses: azure/login@v1
      with:
        creds: ${{secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS}}
    - name: set auto-install of extensions
      run: az config set extension.use_dynamic_install=yes_without_prompt
    - name: attach workspace
      run: az ml folder attach -w "ml-ws" -g "practical-mlops"
    - name: retrieve the model
      run: az ml model download -t "." --model-id "roberta-sequence:1"
    - name: build flask-app container
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v2
      with:
        context: ./
        file: ./Dockerfile
        push: false
        tags: [username]/flask-roberta:latest

Build job mein kai steps hain, har step ka ek distinct task hai — ye failure domains separate karne ka excellent tareeka hai. Agar sab kuch ek hi script mein hota, to potential issues grasp karna zyada difficult hota. Pehla step repository checkout karta hai jab action trigger hoti hai. Phir Azure action se authenticate karna hota hai kyunki ONNX model locally exist nahi karta — authentication ke baad az tool available ho jaata hai, folder ko workspace aur group se attach karna hota hai, aur finally job model ko uski ID se retrieve kar sakti hai. uses directive batata hai kaunsa external action aur kis version par hai — jaise checkout v2 tag hai.

Workflow file mein AZURE_CREDENTIALS use ho raha hai — ye special syntax se repository ke liye configured secrets retrieve karta hai. Ye credentials service principal information hain. Service principal ko workspace aur group ke resources access karne ki configuration chahiye. Secret add karo GitHub repository mein Settings, phir Secrets, phir New repository secret link par click karke.

Steps ko chhota rakho — greedy steps se bacho

Changes commit aur push karo, phir Actions tab par jao — naya run immediately schedule hota hai aur kuch seconds mein start ho jaata hai. Kuch minutes mein sab complete ho jaana chahiye — example mein close to four minutes lage. Packing ke steps ye hain: current branch checkout karo, Azure Cloud authenticate karo, Azure CLI extensions ka auto-install configure karo, workspace se interact karne ke liye folder attach karo, ONNX model download karo, aur current repo ke liye container build karo.

Naye steps ya pipelines design karte time ek good idea hai steps enumerate karna aur greedy steps identify karna — wo steps jo bahut zyada karne ki koshish karte hain aur bahut responsibility rakhte hain. Pehli nazar mein koi problematic step identify karna mushkil hai. CI/CD job maintain karne ke process mein steps ki responsibilities refine karna aur accordingly adapt karna included hai. Steps ko chhote steps mein todne se har part ki responsibility tez samajh aati hai — tez samajh ka matlab hai easier debugging, aur ye habit tumhe fayda degi.

Publish karna — Docker Hub aur GitHub Container Registry

Ek final item abhi missing hai — container build hone ke baad publish karna. Different container registries ko different options chahiye honge, lekin zyaada tar GitHub Actions support karte hain. Docker Hub straightforward hai — ek token banao aur use GitHub project secret ke roop mein save karo, Docker Hub username ke saath. Phir workflow file adapt karo taaki build se pehle authentication step include ho:

- name: Authenticate to Docker hub
  uses: docker/login-action@v1
  with:
    username: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_HUB_USERNAME }}
    password: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_HUB_ACCESS_TOKEN }}

Aakhir mein build step ko update karo taaki push: true ho. GitHub ne ek container registry offering bhi release ki hai, aur uska GitHub Actions ke saath integration straightforward hai. Wahi Docker steps minor changes ke saath use kar sakte ho aur ek PAT (Personal Access Token) bana kar. PAT banao GitHub account settings mein Developer Settings, phir Personal access tokens par jaakar, Generate new token par click karke. Note section mein meaningful description do, aur ensure karo ki token ke paas write packages ki permissions hon. Ye eklauta time hai jab token plain text mein dikhega, to abhi copy kar lo. Phir repository mein naya repository secret banao, naam GH_REGISTRY rakho, aur PAT paste karo:

- name: Login to GitHub Container Registry
  uses: docker/login-action@v1
  with:
    registry: ghcr.io
    username: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
    password: ${{ secrets.GH_REGISTRY }}
- name: build flask-app and push to registry
  uses: docker/build-push-action@v2
  with:
    context: ./
    tags: ghcr.io/[username]/flask-roberta:latest
    push: true

Changes ko main branch par push karne ke baad (ya merge karne ke baad agar pull request banayi thi), job trigger hogi. Model Azure se pull hoga, container mein package hoga, aur finally GitHub Package ke roop mein uski container registry offering mein publish hoga. Is tareeke se shuruaat wali problematic scenario solve ho gayi — model ko container mein package karna hai, lekin container files available nahi hain. Ab process clarity deta hai, chhote steps mein segmented hai, aur container mein koi bhi updates karne deta hai.

Cloud pipelines — steps ka set

Pipelines ke baare mein pehli baar sunne par laga tha ki ye typical scripting pattern se zyada advanced hain, lekin pipelines advanced concepts nahi hain. Agar tumne kisi continuous integration platform mein shell scripts deal kiye hain, to pipeline straightforward lagegi. Pipeline steps ya instructions ka ek set hai jo ek specific objective achieve kar sakta hai, jaise model ko production environment mein publish karna. Example ke liye, model train karne ke liye teen steps wali pipeline — data retrieve karo, validate karo, train karo.

Wahi pipeline ek shell script ke roop mein bhi represent ki ja sakti hai jo teeno kaam ek saath kare. Pipeline ke multiple benefits hain jo concerns separate karte hain. Jab har step ki ek specific responsibility hoti hai, to use grasp karna aasan hota hai. Agar single-step pipeline data retrieve kare, validate kare, aur model train kare aur fail ho jaaye, to immediately clear nahi hota ki kyun fail hua. Logs mein dive kar sakte ho aur actual error check kar sakte ho. Agar pipeline ko teen steps mein separate karo aur train model step fail ho, to failure ka scope narrow kar sakte ho aur possible resolution tak tez pahunch sakte ho.

Ek general recommendation hai: kisi bhi operation ko future failure situation ke liye zyada straightforward banane par consider karo. Pipeline ko single step mein deploy karke fast jaane ki temptation se bacho kyunki ye aasan hai. Time lo aur reason karo ki kya cheez tumhare aur dusron ke liye ML infrastructure build karna aasan banayegi. Jab failure ho aur problematic aspects identify karo, to implementation par wapas jao aur use improve karo. CI/CD ke concepts ko improvement par apply karo: processes ki continuous evaluation aur improvement robust environments ke liye sound strategy hai.

Cloud pipelines kisi bhi continuous integration platform se alag nahi hain, bas ye cloud provider ke dwara hosted ya managed hote hain. RedHat ki pipelines ki explanation mein paanch common elements bataye gaye hain: build, test, release, deploy, aur validate. Ye elements mostly mix-and-match ke liye hain, strictly include karne ke liye nahi. Agar tumhara model deploy karne ki zaroorat nahi hai, to deploy step pursue karne ki zaroorat nahi hai. Agar workflow mein data extract aur preprocess karna hai, to use ek aur step ke roop mein implement karo.

SageMaker pipelines — specialized ML platform

AWS SageMaker involved pipelines craft karne ke liye ready-to-use examples dene mein outstanding job karta hai, jismein kai steps hote hain. SageMaker ek specialized ML platform hai jo sirf pipeline mein steps offer karne se aage jaata hai — tumhe features milte hain jo models ko production mein laane ke liye particularly important hain. Wo features dusre common platforms jaise GitHub Actions mein nahi hain, ya agar hain to utne well thought out nahi hain kyunki GitHub Actions ya Jenkins ka primary goal ML models train karna nahi hai, balki jitna generic hona hai taaki zyaada tar common use cases accommodate ho sakein.

Ek aur crucial problem hai ki specialized machines training ke liye — jaise GPU-intensive tasks — generic pipeline offering mein available hi nahi hain ya configure karna mushkil hai. SageMaker Studio kholo aur left sidebar mein Components and Registries section mein Projects select karo — kai SageMaker project templates dikhenge. Examples tumhe start karne ke liye hain, aur Jupyter Notebooks provide kiye gaye hain, lekin ye steps involved aur unhe apni specific needs ke liye change aur adapt karne ke baare mein seekhne ke liye great hain. Pipeline instance create karne, training karne, aur finally model register karne ke baad pipeline ke parameters browse kar sakte ho. Pipeline ke saare steps bhi available hain — data prepare karna, training, evaluating, aur model register karna. Main objective hai model register karna taaki use baad mein live inferencing ke liye deploy kiya ja sake packaging ke baad. Saare steps ek hi pipeline mein capture karne ki zaroorat nahi hai — dusri pipelines craft kar sakte ho jo jab bhi newly registered model available ho tab chalein. Is tareeke se pipeline kisi particular model se tied nahi hai, balki use kisi bhi dusre model ke liye reuse kar sakte ho jo successfully train aur register hua ho. Components aur automation ki reusability DevOps ka ek aur critical component hai jo MLOps par achha kaam karta hai.

Controlled rollout — blue-green aur canary

Web service deployments ke kuch concepts models ko production mein deploy karne ki strategies mein nicely map hote hain — jaise live inferencing application ke kai instances scalability ke liye banana aur progressively purane model se naye model par switch karna. Do strategies detail mein discuss hoti hain:

  • Blue-green deployment: Naya version staging environment mein laaya jaata hai jo production ke identical hota hai. Kabhi-kabhi ye staging environment production jaisa hi hota hai, lekin traffic alag tareeke se route hota hai. Kubernetes is type ki deployment ke liye perfect hai kyunki same cluster mein do versions rakh sakte ho, naye blue version ko alag address par traffic route kar sakte ho jabki production traffic abhi bhi purane green version par ja raha hai. Is separation ka reason hai ki naya model expected tareeke se kaam kar raha hai, iski further testing aur assurance ho sake. Jab verification complete ho aur certain conditions satisfactory hon, to configuration modify karke traffic current model se naye model par switch kar do. Issue ye hai ki production environments replicate karna complicated ho sakta hai — phir se Kubernetes perfect fit hai kyunki cluster same application ko different versions ke saath ease se accommodate kar sakta hai.
  • Canary deployment: Ye thoda zyada involved aur somewhat riskier hai. Traffic progressively naye model ko route hota hai, jabki previous model bhi simultaneously predictions serve kar raha hai — dono versions live hain aur requests process kar rahe hain, lekin different ratios mein. Percentage-based rollout ka reason hai ki metrics aur dusre checks enable karke problems ko real time mein capture kar sakte ho, aur conditions unfavorable hon to immediately roll back kar sakte ho. Example — naya model better accuracy aur no noted drift ke saath production mein jaane ke liye ready hai. Naye version ke kai instances available hone ke baad configuration change karke 10% traffic naye version ko bhejo. Traffic route hote time responses se dismal amount of errors notice karo — HTTP 500 errors indicate karte hain ki application mein internal error hai. Investigation se pata chalta hai ki inferencing karne wali Python dependencies mein se ek ek module import karne ki koshish kar rahi hai jo move ho gaya hai, jisse exception aata hai. Agar application ko 100 requests per minute milte hain, to sirf 10 ne error condition experience ki hogi. Errors notice karne ke baad configuration quickly change karke saara traffic purane version ko bhej do — is operation ko rollback kehte hain.

Zyaada tar cloud providers ke paas in strategies ke liye models ka controlled rollout karne ki ability hai. Azure Python SDK se naye version ke liye traffic ka percentage define kar sakte ho:

from azureml.core.webservice import AksEndpoint
endpoint.create_version(version_name="2",
    inference_config=inference_config,
    models=[model],
    traffic_percentile=10)
endpoint.wait_for_deployment(True)

Tricky part ye hai ki canary deployment ka objective hai progressively increase karna jab tak traffic_percentile 100% na ho jaaye. Increase application healthiness aur minimal ya zero error rates ke constraints meet karne ke saath hona chahiye. Production models ki monitoring, logging, aur detailed metrics robust deployment strategy ke liye absolutely critical hain — ye deployment ke liye crucial hain aur Chapter 6 mein cover hone wale robust DevOps practices ka core pillar hain.

Testing techniques — automated checks, linting, shift left

Ab tak container great kaam karta hai aur exactly jo chahiye wo karta hai — carefully crafted JSON body wale HTTP requests se JSON response sentiment predict karta hai. Ek seasoned ML engineer ne accuracy aur drift detection model packaging stage se pehle jagah par rakhi hogi. Assume karo wo already hai, aur dusre helpful tests par concentrate karo jo model deploy karne se pehle perform kar sakte ho.

Jab container ko HTTP request bhejkar prediction lete ho, to start se end tak kai software layers se guzarna padta hai: client HTTP request bhejta hai JSON body ke saath, ek array jismein ek string hai; specific HTTP PORT (5000) aur endpoint (predict) exist karne chahiye aur route hone chahiye; Python Flask application ko JSON payload receive karke native Python mein load karna hai; ONNX runtime ko string consume karke prediction produce karni hai; aur JSON response HTTP 200 ke saath prediction ka boolean value contain karni chahiye. In high-level steps mein se har ek ko test kiya ja sakta hai aur karna chahiye.

Automated checks ki zaroorat ek real problem se samajh aati hai: onnxruntime Python module ki documentation version pin nahi karti thi, jisse latest version install hui jo input ke roop mein different arguments chahti thi. Model ki accuracy achhi thi aur significant drift detect nahi hua, phir bhi model deploy kiya to requests consume hote hi fully broken mila. Time ke saath applications better aur zyada resilient banti hain. Koi dusra engineer error handling add kar sakta hai taaki invalid inputs detect hone par error message ke saath respond kare, aur appropriate HTTP error code ke saath nice error message jo client samajh sake. In additions aur behaviors ko model ko production mein ship karne se pehle test karna zaroori hai.

Kabhi-kabhi koi HTTP error condition nahi hogi aur koi Python tracebacks bhi nahi honge. Imagine karo JSON response mein ye change ho jaaye: { "positive": "false" } — boolean false ke bajaye string false. Ye change unnoticed chala jayega. Canary deployment strategy 100% tak bina kisi error detect kiye pahunch jayegi. ML engineer high accuracy aur no drift se khush hoga. Aur phir bhi is change ne model ki effectiveness ko completely tod diya hai. Isliye ye checks kabhi manual nahi hone chahiye; manual verification minimum rakho. Automation high priority honi chahiye, aur ye suggestions pipeline ka hissa ban sakte hain. Ye checks dusre models ke liye generalize karke reuse kiye ja sakte hain, aur high level par parallel mein run ho sakte hain.

Linting bhi ek check hai — code ke kareeb, functional checks se zyada simple implement karne ke liye, jaise Python ke liye Flake8 recommend kiya jaata hai. Saare checks automate karo taaki production release ke time trouble mein na pado. Flask application banate time linter se errors mile jaise hi code ko HTTP requests ke saath kaam karne ke liye adapt kiya gaya:

$ flake8 webapp/app.py
webapp/app.py:9:13: F821 undefined name 'RobertaTokenizer'

Undefined names applications tod dete hain — is case mein transformers module se RobertaTokenizer import karna bhool gaye the. Jaise hi realize hua, import add karke fix kar diya — kuch seconds se zyada nahi lage. Error ko jitni jaldi detect kar sako, utna behtar hai. Software security mein software supply chain ki baat hoti hai — chain wo saare steps hain development se lekar shipping code tak production mein. Is chain mein constant push hai shift left karne ka. Agar steps ko ek badi chain ki tarah dekho, to leftmost link hai developer jo software create aur update karta hai, aur chain ka end hai released product jahan end-consumer interact kar sakta hai. Error detection ko jitna jaldi left shift kar sako, utna behtar hai — kyunki ye production mein pahunchne ke baad rollback karne se sasta aur tez hai.

Continuous improvement ki ek kahani ye batati hai: ek bade open source software ke release manager ko release karne mein do din se lekar poora hafta lag jaata tha. Ek baar release nikaalte time ek core developer ne ek last change daalne ko kaha — sirf ek line ka change, function mein ek documentation comment. Change daala gaya, release cut hui, aur agle din subah users aur customers complain kar rahe the ki latest release completely broken hai — install hoti thi, lekin run hi nahi hoti thi. Culprit wahi one-line change tha — comment ke andar ek unexpected syntax thi jo dusre code se parse hoti thi, aur application start hone se rokti thi. Isse release process restart karna pada, ek change ki testing mein ek extra din laga, aur released packages retire karke repositories redo karne pade taaki naye users ko previous version mile. Ye beyond costly tha. Lesson ye tha ki ye dobara allow nahi hona chahiye — chahe one-line change hi kyun na ho. Error jitni jaldi detect karo, utna kam impact hoga aur utna sasta fix hoga.

Yaad rakho: GitHub mein 100 MB file limit hai aur Git binary files ke liye nahi hai — model ko Azure se pull karo, repo mein mat daalo. Steps ko chhota rakho, greedy steps se bacho. Canary mein 10% traffic se shuru karo aur errors dekh kar rollback karo. Aur boolean false aur string "false" ka farq automated check se pakdo, manual se nahi.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 4 — Continuous Delivery for Machine Learning Models
← Previous04.1 · Packaging for ML Models→ Next05 · AutoML and KaizenML
05Chapter 5 · AutoML and KaizenML

AutoML and KaizenML

Ye chapter ek bahut bade sawaal se shuru hota hai — agar machine learning ka kaam automate ho sakta hai, to hum use haath se kyun karein? AutoML ka matlab hai model training se judi tasks ko automate karna, aur KaizenML ka matlab hai poori ML system ko lagatar improve karte hue automate karna. Dono ko samajhna MLOps ki neev hai.

AutoML kya hai, aur ye itna important kyun hai

AutoML, matlab Automated Machine Learning, wo technique hai jo clean data par model train karne se judi tasks ko automate kar deti hai — jaise algorithm chunna, hyperparameters tune karna, aur model ko evaluate karna. Lekin ye poori kahani nahi hai. Asli duniya me problems itne simple nahi hote — data ganda hota hai, features banane padte hain, model ko deploy karna padta hai, aur production me uski monitoring karni padti hai. Isi gap ko KaizenML bharta hai.

Book me ek bahut achha example diya gaya hai — khane ka. Aap ghar par aata khareed kar khud pizza bana sakte ho, ya ready-made garam pizza order kar sakte ho. Dono hi khana hain. Mushkil hona ya aasan hona, kisi cheez ko asli ya nakli nahi banata. Bilkul waise hi, AutoML se bana model bhi asli model hota hai. Jo kaam machine behtar kar sakti hai, use haath se karne ki zidd karna samajhdari nahi hai.

Self-handicapping — khud apne pair par kulhadi

Chapter me ek interesting concept hai — self-handicapping. Matlab, jab data science project fail hota hai, to log bahane banate hain: problem bahut mushkil thi, ya tools achhe nahi the. Lekin ek tareeka ye bhi hai ki hum jaan-boojh kar best tools use hi na karein — jaise AutoML use na karna jab wo madad kar sakta ho. Ye project ki kamyabi me khud hi rukawat dalna hai.

Software engineering ka ek golden rule hai — kaam ke liye best tools use karo, kyunki wo complexity kam karte hain. GitHub Actions testing automate karke aur Visual Studio Code code completion aur linting dekar developer ki productivity badhate hain. Data science me bhi yehi mantra chahiye — best tools ko apnana, unse ladna nahi.

Urgency wali soch — sirf zaroori kaam par focus

Book me ek bahut powerful sawal uthaya gaya hai — agar aapko sirf chaar ghante me ek model train karke production me dalna ho, to aap kya karoge? Jawab simple hai — jitna kam code likhna pade, utna kam likhoge, aur ready-made automation tools use karoge, jaise Azure AutoML, Apple Create ML, Google AutoML, H2O, ya Ludwig. Phir sawal ye banta hai — aam projects me bhi hum itna code kyun likhte hain?

Duniya ko production me high-quality ML models ki zaroorat hai — cancer ka cure dhundhna ho, clean energy optimize karni ho, drug discovery tez karni ho, ya transport safe banana ho. Ye sab tabhi hoga jab hum jo automate ho sakta hai use abhi automate karein, aur jo aaj automate nahi ho sakta use automate karne ke tareeke dhundhein.

Is chapter me aage kya hai

Aage ke sections me hum dekhenge ki AutoML MLOps industrial revolution ka sirf ek chhota hissa kyun hai, Kaizen aur KaizenML me kya farq hai, Feature Stores kaise kaam karte hain, Apple, Google, Azure aur AWS ke Cloud AutoML solutions kaise use karte hain, aur Ludwig, FLAML, ELI5 aur SHAP jaise open source tools se explainability kaise milti hai.

Yaad rakho: AutoML sirf model training automate karta hai — ye poora MLOps nahi hai. Asli jeet tab milti hai jab data se lekar deployment aur monitoring tak har step automate aur lagatar improve ho — yehi KaizenML hai.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 5 — AutoML and KaizenML
← Previous04.2 · Infrastructure as Code and Cloud Pipelines→ Next05.1 · AutoML — MLOps Industrial Revolution
05.1Chapter 5 · AutoML and KaizenML

AutoML — MLOps Industrial Revolution

AutoML ko lekar data scientists ke beech bahut debate hoti hai — kuch ko lagta hai ye unki naukri kha jayega. Lekin book ka point bilkul saaf hai — AutoML sirf 5% hai. Asli picture bahut badi hai: poora MLOps, yaani KaizenML, jisme automation aur continuous improvement hi sab kuch hai.

Data science ek behavior hai, AutoML ek technique

Pehli baat jo samajhni hai — data science aur AutoML aapas me compete hi nahi karte. Data science ek behavior hai, jaise statistics ek behavior hai — ye kisi problem ka solution nahi, problem solve karne ka tareeka hai. AutoML ek technique hai, bilkul continuous integration (CI) ki tarah — ye chhote-mote tedious tasks automate karta hai.

Book me ek bahut achha example hai — cruise control car driver se compete nahi karta. Driver ko abhi bhi gaadi control karni hoti hai aur bade faisle lene hote hain. Bilkul waise hi, AutoML ke baad bhi insaan ko hi bade executive decisions lene hote hain — kaunsa problem solve karna hai, kaunsa data use karna hai, aur model production me sahi chal raha hai ya nahi.

Industrial Revolution se comparison

1760 se 1840 ke beech pehli industrial revolution me steam aur coal machines ne insaani kaam automate kiya, aur isse population, GDP aur quality of life teeno badhe. 1870 ke aas-paas dusri industrial revolution me mass production aur electrical grid aaye. Book kehta hai ki ML me bhi ab yehi ho raha hai — MLOps industrial revolution.

Tesla ki factory ka example dekho — robots gaadi ke parts screw karte hain, bolt lagate hain, welding karte hain. Insaan ab robots ko wo kaam feed karte hain jo robots khud abhi poori tarah automate nahi kar sakte. Bilkul waise hi, traditional data science workflow me insaan hyperparameters ko haath se "bolt" karta rehta hai — jaise purani Ford assembly line. Aakhir me manual kaam automate ho hi jata hai, aur sabse pehle wo kaam automate hota hai jo automate karna sabse aasan hai.

80% manual training replace ho sakta hai

Book ek bold prediction karta hai — jald hi kam se kam 80% manual data science model training commoditized open source AutoML tools ya downloaded pre-built models se replace ho jayega. Jaise Linux kernel free aur har jagah hai, waise hi model training ka software bhi free aur ubiquitous ho sakta hai, khaas taur par jab Ludwig ya Apple CreateML jaise tools aur sophisticated hote jayenge.

Iska matlab ye hoga ki data science bimodal ho sakta hai — ya to aap bahut senior, bahut zyada paid expert ho, ya entry-level. Beech ka competitive advantage traditional software engineering best practices me chala jayega — data aur users, automation, execution, aur solid product management aur business practices. Data scientist ek job title se zyada ek standard skill ban sakta hai — jaise accounting, writing, ya critical thinking.

Kaggle feedback loop

Ek aur interesting angle hai — Kaggle ko ek feedback loop ki tarah dekho jisse Google apne AutoML tools ko behtar banata hai. Data science 1.0 me insaan manually "buttons click" karte hain, bilkul purane zamane ke switchboard operators ki tarah. Data science 2.0 me, jo kai mamlo me aa chuka hai, automated tools unhi models ko train karte hain jo pehle insaan train karte the.

To aise badlav ke time me kis skill me invest karein? Book ka jawab hai — automation aur execution me world-class bano, technical aur business dono taraf se, aur uske saath solid domain expertise jodo. Ideas se innovation nahi hoti — ideas ko execution ke saath jodne se hoti hai. Sawal ye hai — kya ye kaam karta hai, aur kya koi iske liye paise dega?

Yaad rakho: AutoML aapki naukri nahi khata — ye aapke tedious kaam khata hai. Jo log automation aur execution me best honge, aur domain ko gehrai se samjhenge, wahi is revolution me aage rahenge.

05.2Chapter 5 · AutoML and KaizenML

Kaizen Versus KaizenML

Kaizen ek Japanese shabd hai jiska matlab hai continuous improvement — lagatar sudhar. KaizenML isi idea ko machine learning par lagata hai — ML system ka har hissa, feature engineering se lekar AutoML tak, lagatar improve hota rahe. Ye section Kaizen, KaizenML aur MLOps ke beech ka farq saaf karta hai.

Teeno cheezein alag hain — confuse mat karo

Log aksar data science, AutoML aur MLOps (KaizenML) ko ek hi samajh lete hain, aur yehi confusion problem hai. Data science ek behavior hai. AutoML sirf ek technique hai. Aur KaizenML ya MLOps ek systems methodology hai jiska outcome hai — production me chalte hue models jo customer ki problem solve karte hain.

Isi liye sirf AutoML versus data science ki baat karna poori picture ko chhota kar deta hai. Asli mudda ye hai ki sirf hyperparameter tuning jaise tedious hisse hi nahi, har cheez automate honi chahiye. Automation aur continuous improvement se data scientists, ML engineers aur poori organization apna dhyaan us par laga sakti hai jo asli me matter karta hai — execution.

Kaizen ki kahani — Japan ki automobile industry

Second World War ke baad Japan ne apni automobile industry ko Kaizen ke concept par khada kiya. Matlab simple tha — agar kuch toota hua ya unoptimized mile, to use fix karo. Ruko mat, agle quarter ka wait mat karo, abhi sudharo. Bilkul waise hi KaizenML me ML ke har aspect ko improve kiya jata hai — data se lekar features tak, training se lekar deployment tak.

Book ek simple formula bhi deta hai — DevOps + KaizenML = MLOps. DevOps software ki testing aur deployment automate karta hai. KaizenML usme data aur ML models ki quality ko lagatar improve karna jodta hai. Dono milkar poora MLOps bante hain.

Data ek competitive advantage hai

Jaise-jaise AutoML technology aage badhegi, aaj data scientists jo bahut sa kaam karte hain, wo gayab ho sakta hai. Aaj kal manual transmission wali ya cruise control ke bina gaadi milna rare hai. Waise hi future me hyperparameters ko haath se adjust karna rare ho sakta hai. Tab current data scientists ML engineers ya domain experts ban jayenge jo apne kaam ke hisse ke roop me "data science karte" hain.

Is future me data aur data ko effectively handle karne ki expertise hi competitive advantage ban jayegi, kyunki data ek scarce resource hai. Models to sab download kar lenge ya AutoML se bana lenge — farq is baat se padega ki kiske paas behtar data hai aur kaun use behtar tareeke se use karta hai.

Har insaan ko data science aana chahiye

Book ek strong baat kehta hai — har insaan ko data science aur programming karni chahiye, kyunki ye critical thinking ke forms hain. Pandemic ek wake-up call tha — bahut se log isliye nuksan me rahe kyunki unhone data ko sahi se samjha nahi. Data science ke tools kisi elite priesthood ke haath me nahi rehne chahiye — ye human rights ki tarah hain, sabko milne chahiye.

Automation data science aur programming ko itna aasan bana dega ki har insaan ye kar sakega — aur kai mamlo me abhi available automation se bhi kar sakta hai. KaizenML ya MLOps ka focus narrow hai — machine learning aur software engineering (DevOps se influenced) se problems solve karna, jisse business value mile ya insaani halat sudhre, jaise cancer ka cure.

Yaad rakho: Kaizen ka matlab hai — kuch toota mile to use fix karo, abhi. KaizenML me ye rule ML pipeline ke har step par lagta hai. Ye ek baar ka project nahi, ek culture hai jiska koi end date nahi hota.
