← Previous05.1 · AutoML — MLOps Industrial Revolution→ Next05.3 · Feature Stores
05.3Chapter 5 · AutoML and KaizenML

Feature Stores

Feature Store KaizenML ka ek bahut important hissa hai — ye high-quality machine learning inputs ki registry hai, jisme features ko store, share aur serve kiya jata hai. Agar aapne kabhi ek hi feature ko alag-alag projects me baar-baar banaya hai, to aapko Feature Store ki zaroorat samajh me aa jayegi.

Problem kya hai — manual data science me sab bespoke hai

Manual data science me har cheez bespoke hoti hai — har project me data ko scratch se clean karna, features haath se banana, aur phir mushkil se model ko production tak pahunchana. Isse data ki quality low rehti hai aur working model ko production me le jana bahut mushkil ho jata hai.

Jaise-jaise zyada cheezein automate hoti hain — data se features tak, Feature Store ke through, aur phir model ko production me serve karne tak — outcome behtar hota jata hai. Feature Store isi automation chain ki ek kadi hai.

Uber ka example — Feature Store kya karta hai

Uber Engineering blog ke hisab se Feature Store do kaam karta hai. Pehla — users apne banaye hue features ko shared Feature Store me add kar sakte hain. Dusra — ek baar features Feature Store me aa jayein, to unhe training aur prediction dono me use karna bahut aasan ho jata hai.

Uber ne apne Feature Store me 10,000 features use karke machine learning projects ko accelerate kiya aur uske upar AutoML solutions banaye. Matlab, features ek baar achhe se ban gaye to unhe baar-baar reuse karke naye models jaldi banaye ja sakte hain.

Databricks aur data warehouse se farq

Databricks jaise platforms me Feature Store unke big data system ke andar built-in hota hai. Raw data input hota hai, transform hota hai, aur ek refined, specialized feature registry banti hai jo batch aur online dono problems solve kar sakti hai.

Traditional data warehouse aur MLOps Feature Store me similarity bhi hai aur farq bhi. Data warehouse business intelligence systems ko feed karta hai, jabki Feature Store ML system ko inputs deta hai. ML data processing repetitive hoti hai — data normalize karna, clean karna, aur wo features dhundhna jo model ko improve karein. Feature Store banakar aap ideation se lekar production tak poore ML process ke automation ko ek aur kadam aage le jate ho.

Feature Store poori system ka hissa hai

Ek baat dhyaan me rakhni hai — AutoML poori problem ka sirf 5% ho sakta hai. Data ko ETL job management se automation chahiye. Feature Store ko ML inputs improve karne ke liye automation chahiye. Deployment ko automated deployment (CD) aur cloud elasticity (autoscaling) se automation chahiye. Complex software systems me har cheez ko automation chahiye, aur Feature Stores KaizenML ke kai components me se sirf ek hain.

  • Shared registry: features ek baar banao, poori team reuse kare.
  • Training aur prediction consistency: training me jo feature use hua, wahi prediction me mile — train-serve skew kam hota hai.
  • Batch aur online: ek hi feature registry dono tarah ke use cases serve kar sakti hai.
  • Drift monitoring: KaizenML ke hisse ke roop me Feature Store data drift monitor karne aur models ko register aur serve karne me madad karta hai.
Yaad rakho: Feature Store sirf ek database nahi hai — ye ML inputs ki quality aur reusability ka system hai. Achha Feature Store matlab kam dobara kaam, zyada consistent models, aur tez experimentation.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 5 — AutoML and KaizenML
← Previous05.2 · Kaizen Versus KaizenML→ Next05.4 · Cloud AutoML — Apple, Google, Azure, AWS
05.4Chapter 5 · AutoML and KaizenML

Cloud AutoML — Apple, Google, Azure, AWS

Har bada cloud provider apna AutoML solution deta hai, aur har ek ka approach thoda alag hai. Apple on-device ML aur no-code GUI par focus karta hai, Google Vertex AI aur edge devices par, Azure ML Studio aur explainability par, aur AWS SageMaker Autopilot par. Is section me chaaro ka practical workflow dekhenge.

Apple — Create ML aur Core ML

Apple pehle to ML tools me unlikely candidate lag sakta hai, lekin uska mobile ecosystem bahut rich hai aur App Store se uski badi revenue aati hai — 2019 me 55.5 billion dollars se badhkar 2020 me 72.3 billion dollars. Apple chahta hai aap uske App Store ke liye apps banao, isliye wo developer tools ko behtar banata hai. Uske paas on-device ML ke liye dedicated hardware bhi hai — A12 se A14 chips aur M1 architecture, jisme CPU, GPU aur dedicated neural network hardware hota hai.

Apple Create ML ek intuitive GUI deta hai jisme aap bina code ke Core ML models bana sakte ho, model performance preview kar sakte ho, Mac par train kar sakte ho (M1 chip ka fayda lekar), training ko pause, save aur resume kar sakte ho, aur eGPU use kar sakte ho. Ye image, video, motion, sound, text aur tabular — kai domains cover karta hai.

Create ML ka workflow simple hai — Xcode download karo, Create ML launch karo, Image Classifier template chuno, cats-dogs-small dataset drag-and-drop karo, test data dalo, aur train button dabao. Augmentations jaise Noise, Blur, Crop, Expose, Flip aur Rotate se model zyada robust banta hai. Phir internet se cat-dog ki photos preview me drag karke test karo, aur model ko download karke iOS app me use karo — poora kaam zero code me.

Apple Core ML Tools — pretrained models ko convert karo

Dusra powerful workflow hai pretrained model download karke use Core ML format me convert karna, coremltools Python library se. Jaise MobileNetV2 ko TensorFlow Hub se lekar convert karna:

!pip install coremltools
import coremltools as ct
keras_model = tf.keras.applications.MobileNetV2(weights="imagenet", input_shape=(224, 224, 3,), classes=1000)
image_input = ct.ImageType(shape=(1, 224, 224, 3,), bias=[-1,-1,-1], scale=1/127)
model = ct.convert(keras_model, inputs=[image_input], classifier_config=ct.ClassifierConfig(class_labels))
model.save("MobileNetV2.mlmodel")

Book ka takeaway hai — kai baar experts ke banaye hue pretrained model ko download karna khud train karne se bhi aasan hota hai. Core ML dono use cases support karta hai — bespoke AutoML aur pretrained models.

Google — AutoML Vision aur Vertex AI

Google ka approach vertically integrated hai — framework, operating system, aur specialized hardware jaise TPU (TensorFlow Processing Unit) aur Coral.AI edge chip. Computer vision ke liye GCP par difficulty ke order me chaar options hain — khud ML code likhkar train karna, Google AutoML Vision use karna, TensorFlow Hub se pretrained model download karna, ya Vision AI API use karna.

AutoML Vision ka workflow hai — Cloud Console kholo, AutoML Vision API enable karo aur IAM permission do, training data aur labels CSV ke through Google Cloud Storage me upload karo, console me data ko visually inspect karo aur labels fix karo, button click karke train karo, built-in tools se evaluate karo, aur phir online endpoint banao ya model download karke iOS, Android, JavaScript, Coral hardware ya container par chalao. Ye sab ab Google Vertex AI me integrated hai — Notebooks se lekar Batch Predictions tak ek hi left panel me.

gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT_ID --member="user:$USERNAME" --role="roles/automl.admin"
gsutil -m cp -r gs://spls/gsp223/images/* gs://${BUCKET}
gsutil cp gs://spls/gsp223/data.csv .

Azure AutoML — console aur Python SDK

Azure AutoML tak pahunchne ke do tareeke hain — Azure ML Studio console aur AutoML Python SDK. Console me aap Automated ML option chunte ho, dataset upload karte ho ya open dataset use karte ho, phir classification job banate ho — jaise NBA players ke dataset se predict karna ki player kis position par khel sakta hai. Regression aur time-series forecasting bhi available hain.

Azure ki khaas baat hai explainability — job complete hone ke baad aap Azure ML Studio se pooch sakte ho ki model ne apni predictions kaise banayi. Ye ML Studio me deep integration ke saath aata hai. Python SDK se wahi kaam is tarah hota hai:

from azureml.train.automl import AutoMLConfig
automl_config = AutoMLConfig(task='regression', debug_log='automated_ml_errors.log', training_data=x_train, label_column_name="totalAmount", **automl_settings)

AWS — SageMaker Autopilot

AWS ka recommended AutoML solution SageMaker Autopilot hai. Workflow hai — SageMaker Autopilot kholo, naya task banao, NBA Players Data ko Amazon S3 me upload karo, experiment banao aur target chuno — jaise draft position predict karna. Phir Autopilot preprocessing se lekar Model Tuning tak ka pipeline chalata hai, resources use karta hai, aur end me models ki list unki accuracy ke saath dikhata hai. Book ke example me accuracy .999945 tak pahunchi.

Job complete hone par aap model ko production me deploy kar sakte ho ya trail details me jaakar explainability aur metrics ya charts inspect kar sakte ho. Agar aapki organization pehle se AWS use kar rahi hai, to Autopilot ko existing workflows me integrate karna straightforward hai, khaas taur par bade datasets aur reproducibility-critical problems ke liye.

Yaad rakho: Chaaro clouds ka AutoML ek hi idea ko alag tareeke se implement karta hai — kam code, zyada automation. Apna cloud chunne se pehle dekho ki aapko kya chahiye — on-device inference, edge deploy, explainability, ya enterprise scale.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 5 — AutoML and KaizenML

05.5Chapter 5 · AutoML and KaizenML

Open Source AutoML — Ludwig, FLAML, Explainability

Cloud AutoML ke saath-saath open source AutoML bhi tezi se aage badh raha hai. Book ka point hai — jaise Linux free hone ki wajah se Unix ko peeche chhod gaya, waise hi open source AutoML bhi commoditization ki taraf badh raha hai. Is section me Ludwig, FLAML aur explainability tools ELI5 aur SHAP dekhenge.

Ludwig — config se model training

Ludwig ek promising open source AutoML framework hai, jo ab Linux Foundation ke under hai aur version 4 me remote filesystems, Dask aur Ray jaise distributed out-of-memory tools, aur MLflow ke saath deep integration deta hai. Iska sabse bada fayda — ye open source hai, kisi ek corporation ke control me nahi hai.

Text classification ka Ludwig workflow Colab me sirf kuch commands ka hai — install karo, config aur dataset download karo, aur ek command se experiment chalao:

!pip install -q ludwig
!wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paiml/practical-mlops-book/main/chap05/config.yaml
!wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paiml/practical-mlops-book/main/chap05/reuters-allcats.csv
!ludwig experiment --dataset reuters-allcats.csv --config_file config.yaml

Run ke output me wo metrics dikhte hain jinse model ki strength evaluate ki ja sakti hai. Ludwig ki documentation me aur bhi bahut se excellent examples milte hain.

FLAML — teen lines me AutoML

FLAML Microsoft Research ka framework hai, jo cost-effective hyperparameter optimization ke liye design kiya gaya hai. Iska sabse famous use case hai — poora modeling process sirf teen lines me automate kar dena:

from flaml import AutoML
automl = AutoML()
automl.fit(X_train, y_train, task="classification")

Ek comprehensive example me time budget aur metric set karke training chalayi jati hai, aur kai iterations ke baad FLAML optimized hyperparameters ke saath ek best model chunta hai — jaise XGBClassifier:

!pip install -q flaml
from flaml import AutoML
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
automl = AutoML()
automl_settings = {"time_budget": 10, "metric": 'accuracy', "task": 'classification'}
X_train, y_train = load_iris(return_X_y=True)
automl.fit(X_train=X_train, y_train=y_train, **automl_settings)
print(automl.predict_proba(X_train))
print(automl.model)

Inke alawa aur bhi open source AutoML frameworks hain jinhe dekhna chahiye — H2O AutoML, Auto-sklearn, TPOT, PyCaret aur AutoKeras.

Explainability — model ne aisa kyun predict kiya

Automation ka ek important hissa hai model explainability ko automate karna. Jaise subah kaam par aakar team CPU aur memory usage dekhti hai, waise hi use raat ko train hue model ki explainability report bhi dekhni chahiye. AWS SageMaker, Azure ML Studio aur Google Vertex AI me explainability built-in hai, lekin aap open source se bhi implement kar sakte ho.

Do popular open source frameworks hain — ELI5 aur SHAP. ELI5 ka matlab hai "explain like I am five" — ye models ko visualize aur debug karta hai aur sklearn jaise kai frameworks support karta hai. SHAP ek game-theoretic approach hai jo model ke output ko explain karta hai, aur iske visualizations bahut achhe hote hain.

SHAP aur ELI5 ka practical walkthrough

Book me NBA players ke 2016-2017 season ke data se ek walkthrough hai — AGE, POINTS, SALARY_MILLIONS, PAGEVIEWS, TWITTER_FAVORITE_COUNT aur TOV features se winning_season predict karna, matlab player winning team me hoga ya nahi. Data clean karke, train-test split karke logistic regression train kiya jata hai, phir SHAP ke liye XGBoost model train kiya jata hai:

!pip install -q shap
import xgboost
import shap
model_xgboost = xgboost.train({"learning_rate": 0.01}, xgboost.DMatrix(x_train, label=y_train), 100)
shap.initjs()
explainer = shap.TreeExplainer(model_xgboost)
shap_values = explainer.shap_values(features)
shap.force_plot(explainer.expected_value, shap_values[0,:], features.iloc[0,:])
shap.summary_plot(shap_values, features, plot_type="bar")

SHAP force plot me laal rang wale features prediction ko upar dhakelte hain aur neele rang wale neeche. Summary plot dikhata hai ki "off the court" metrics jaise Twitter aur Salary bhi wins predict karne me important hote hain. ELI5 me permutation importance se pata chalta hai ki feature hatane par accuracy kitni girti hai — aur wahan player ki age ka wins se negative correlation dikhta hai:

!pip install -q eli5
import eli5
from eli5.sklearn import PermutationImportance
perm = PermutationImportance(model, random_state=1).fit(x_train, y_train)
eli5.show_weights(perm, feature_names = features.columns.tolist())
Yaad rakho: Explainability koi luxury nahi hai — ye MLOps ka dashboard hai. Agar aap nahi bata sakte ki model ne aisa predict kyun kiya, to stakeholders ka bharosa aur business ke healthy outcomes dono mushkil hain.

06Chapter 6 · Monitoring and Logging

Monitoring and Logging

Logging aur monitoring DevOps ke core pillars hain, aur robust ML practices ke liye ye bilkul zaroori hain. Model ko production me dalna hi kaafi nahi hai — ye jaanna bhi zaroori hai ki wo sahi chal raha hai ya nahi, uski accuracy gir to nahi rahi, aur data badal to nahi gaya. Ye chapter isi ko "data science for operations" kehta hai.

Logging aur monitoring mushkil kyun hain

Zyadatar software engineers code likhna pasand karte hain, aur testing, documentation, logging aur monitoring ko peeche chhod dete hain. Lekin useful logging aur monitoring ko sahi karna mushkil hai. Cloud services heavy lifting kar sakti hain, lekin strategy aapko hi banani padti hai — kya information produce karni hai taaki wo usable ho.

Book me ek real example hai — ek software ka log line thi jo kisi ko samajh hi nahi aayi, aur jab ek knowledgeable engineer ne use translate kiya to matlab nikla — "the machine you are on is unable to contact the monitor." Do saal kaam karne ke baad bhi log line ka matlab samajh nahi aaya tha. Isi liye log messages aise hone chahiye jo kahani suna sakein, na ki cryptic codes hon.

Metrics se kahani — subscribe button wala example

Ek bade Python-based CMS par kaam karte hue, management ko metrics add karne ka proposal diya gaya. Unka jawab tha — humare paas pehle se metrics hain, disk usage aur memory alerts hain. Jawab me ek sawal poocha gaya — website ka sabse important button hai subscribe button, jo paying users banata hai. Agar naye deploy me JavaScript issue se wo button kaam karna band kar de, to kaunsa metric ya alert ye batayega?

Disk usage wahi rahega, memory usage bhi shayad na badle, lekin sabse important button bina notice ke unusable ho jayega. Iske liye metrics chahiye — har ghante, din aur hafte me us button ka click-through rate. Metrics se ye kahani banti hai ki aaj website pichhle saal ke isi mahine se zyada ya kam revenue generate kar rahi hai. Server ke disk aur memory par nazar rakhna useful hai, lekin ye ultimate goal nahi hai.

Measure, compare, improve

Book me ek athlete journaling ki kahani hai — har din workout ke baad journal me likhna: planned workout kya tha, actual results kya rahe, kaisa feel hua, aur koi aur relevant baat jaise beemari ya injury. Saalon baad jab agle season ki planning hui, to wahi journals sabse powerful tool bane. Coach ne kaha — "If we can measure, then we can compare. And if we can compare, only then can we improve."

ML operations me bhi yehi hai — jab model ka naya version production me jata hai, to pata hona chahiye ki wo behtar hai ya bura. Aur ye information accessible aur straightforward tareeke se produce honi chahiye. Automation silly processes ko hata deta hai aur information availability ko effortless bana deta hai.

Is chapter me aage kya hai

Aage hum cloud observability dekhenge — AWS CloudWatch, Google Cloud operations suite aur Azure Monitor kaise kaam karte hain. Phir Python me logging ki gehrai me jayenge — log levels, formatting, traceback aur alag-alag loggers. Aur aakhir me drift monitoring dekhenge — SageMaker aur Azure ML se kaise pata chalta hai ki data ya model badal gaya hai.

Yaad rakho: Production me model dalna hi kaafi nahi hai — agar aap measure nahi kar sakte, to aap compare nahi kar sakte, aur agar compare nahi kar sakte, to improve bhi nahi kar sakte. Logging aur monitoring foundation hain, luxury nahi.

06.1Chapter 6 · Monitoring and Logging

Observability for Cloud MLOps

Aaj zyadatar machine learning cloud environment me ho raha hai, aur har cloud provider ke paas observability ke liye special services hain — AWS par Amazon CloudWatch, GCP par Google Cloud operations suite, aur Azure par Azure Monitor. Ye section batata hai ki ye services ML systems ke liye kyun nonoptional hain.

CloudWatch kaise kaam karta hai

Amazon CloudWatch ek achha example hai ki ye monitoring services kaise kaam karti hain. High level par, cloud system ka har component CloudWatch ko metrics aur logs bhejta hai — servers, application logs, ML jobs ki training metadata, aur production ML endpoints ke results.

Phir ye information dashboards se lekar auto-scaling tak kai tools ka hissa ban jati hai. Jaise AWS SageMaker me, agar production ML service ke endpoints 75% se zyada CPU ya memory use karne lagein, to service automatically scale ho jayegi. Ye observability insaano aur machines dono ko ye samajhne aur us par action lene deti hai ki production ML system me kya ho raha hai.

MLOps me observability kyun alag hai

Experienced cloud software engineer janta hai ki cloud observability tools kisi bhi cloud deployment ke nonoptional components hain. Lekin MLOps me ek nayi baat hai — naye components ko bhi granular monitoring chahiye. ML model deployment me poori nayi series ki actions hoti hain, aur CloudWatch in naye metrics ko bhi collect karta hai.

High level par CloudWatch data collect karta hai, alerts route karta hai, aur cloud computing ke dynamic components jaise elastic scaling ke saath engage karta hai. Yehi master system hai jiske upar logging aur monitoring ki finer-grained details banti hain.

Metrics ke teen common types

Monitoring ki basics samajhne ke liye metric types ko samajhna zaroori hai. Book teen types batata hai jo zyadatar metric-capturing systems me milte hain:

  • Counter: kisi bhi cheez ko ginne ke liye — jaise har column me empty values ki ginti. Items par iterate karte hue counting ke liye useful hai.
  • Timer: kisi action me kitna time laga, ye measure karne ke liye. Hosted HTTP APIs ke monitoring graphs me time spent aam dikhta hai — jaise hosted model ko HTTP par prediction dene me kitna time laga.
  • Value: jab counter aur timer fit na hon, to value use hoti hai. Jaise JSON files process karke database me save karne ke baad resulting database ka size gigabytes me — ek aisa number jise capture karke persist karna hai, chahe uska matlab abhi poori tarah samajh na aaye.

Target dataset aur baseline — drift monitoring ki neev

ML ke liye cloud providers ko do cheezein monitor karni hoti hain. Pehli hai target dataset — ye wahi dataset ho sakta hai jisse model train kiya gaya tha, lekin khaas dhyaan rakhna hota hai ki features ki sankhya aur order na badle. Dusri hai baseline — ye decide karti hai ki kaunse differences acceptable hain jab model train hota hai. Baseline ko acceptable thresholds ki tarah socho jo ye batate hain ki model production ke liye kitna fit hai.

Book me ek real example hai — system vulnerability data process karte hue code me change ke baad database kai gigabytes se sirf 100 megabytes ka ho gaya. Code change ka maksad size kam karna tha hi nahi, isliye turant pata chal gaya ki galti hui hai. Aise situations hi batate hain ki kaunse metrics capture karne hain aur kab.

Yaad rakho: Disk aur memory alerts hi kaafi nahi hain — ML system me model ki performance, data ki quality aur prediction latency jaise ML-specific metrics bhi monitor karne hote hain. Observability ka matlab hai poori system ki kahani dekh pana, sirf servers ki health nahi.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 6 — Monitoring and Logging
← Previous06 · Monitoring and Logging→ Next06.2 · Logging in Python
06.2Chapter 6 · Monitoring and Logging

Logging in Python

Logging ka matlab hai program ke chalte hue uski state ke baare me meaningful information produce karna — taaki baad me samajh aaye ki kya hua, kab hua, aur kyun hua. Ye section Python ke logging module ko ek chhoti si CSV script ke example se step by step samjhata hai.

Logging ki basics — Nginx ka example

Zyadatar logging facilities me common aspects hote hain — log levels define hote hain, aur user chun sakta hai ki kis level ke statements dikhne chahiye. Nginx web server ka default configuration access logs ko /var/log/nginx/access.log me aur error logs ko /var/log/nginx/error.log me save karta hai.

Access log ki line me server ka IP address, time, request ka type aur user-agent information hoti hai — jaise kaunsa browser kis machine se request bhej raha hai. Error log me level saaf dikhta hai — jaise file unreadable hone par "Permission denied" error. Level se consumer turant identify kar sakta hai ki information kitni serious hai.

print() kyun kaafi nahi hai

Debug karne ke liye log aksar print() statements use karte hain, lekin isme problems hain. Pehli — problem solve hone ke baad saare print() hatane padte hain, aur agli baar phir se add karne padte hain. Dusri — print() se application break ho sakti hai, jaise galat format string par TypeError. Logging module aisa nahi karta — agar message banane me fail ho jaye, to wo problem ko advertise karke continue karta hai, application ko break nahi karta.

Book kehta hai — Python me print() use karna bilkul shell scripts me echo use karne jaisa hai. Na control hai, na verbosity par kabu, aur production application ko break karna aasan hai. Logging me verbosity control hoti hai — aap chun sakte ho ki kitni detail chahiye.

Ek brittle script ko logging se sudharna

Book me describe.py naam ki ek chhoti script hai jo CSV file ko read karke describe karti hai. Bina arguments ke chalao to wo khud apne aap ko describe karne lagti hai, kyunki last argument script ka naam hi hota hai. Galat path do to FileNotFoundError ka bada traceback aata hai. Aur agar saare exceptions ko catch karke sirf "Had a problem trying to read the CSV file" print kar do, to production me ye dekh kar bahut gussa aayega — koi context hi nahi milta.

Logging add karna simple hai — kuch lines se shuruaat hoti hai:

import logging
logging.basicConfig()
logger = logging.getLogger("describe")
logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)
argument = sys.argv[-1]
logger.debug("processing input file: %s", argument)

Phir log format ko nicer banao — logger ka naam, level aur message square brackets me, padding ke saath:

log_format = "[%(name)s][%(levelname)-6s] %(message)s"
logging.basicConfig(format=log_format)
logger = logging.getLogger("describe")
logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)

Traceback ke saath error — aur program continue karta hai

Logging ki ek superpower hai — error ke saath traceback capture karna, bina error condition me gaye. except block me logger.exception() use karo:

try:
    df = pd.read_csv(argument)
    print(df.describe())
except Exception:
    logger.exception("Had a problem trying to read the CSV file")
    logger.info("the program continues, without issue")

Traceback error ka string representation hai, khud error nahi — iske baad logger.info() wali line phir bhi chalti hai aur program continue karta hai. Ye print() se bilkul alag hai.

Log levels — sabse verbose se sabse kam

Python logging me levels ka weight hota hai, sabse zyada verbose se sabse kam tak:

  • debug: sabse verbose — har level ke messages dikhte hain.
  • info: general information.
  • warning: chetavni — kuch galat ho sakta hai.
  • error: error hua hai.
  • critical: sabse serious — sirf critical messages dikhte hain.

Level ko ERROR par set karne se sirf error messages dikhte hain. Book recommend karta hai ki naye production code ke liye debug level set karo, taaki potential problems aasani se pakdi jayein. Jab application stable ho jaye aur surprising issues kam hon, to dheere-dheere level ko info ya error par fine-tune karo.

Root logger aur alag-alag loggers

Python me har module aur package ka apna logger ho sakta hai, aur logging facility inhe independently configure karne deti hai. Root logger sab loggers ka parent hai — uski settings sab par lagu hoti hain. http-app.py example me root logger ko DEBUG par set karne se urllib3 package ke debug messages bhi dikhne lage, kyunki requests library internally urllib3 use karti hai.

Aap urllib3 ka level alag se ERROR par set karke uska noise band kar sakte ho, jabki apne app ka logger DEBUG par hi rehta hai:

urllib_logger = logging.getLogger('urllib3')
urllib_logger.setLevel(logging.ERROR)

Ek production application me do loggers bhi banaye ja sakte hain — ek terminal par user-friendly messages dikhaye, dusra logfile me developer-oriented detailed logging likhe. Ye flexibility print() se kabhi nahi mil sakti. Logging monitoring ke saath haath me haath chalti hai, aur dono hi DevOps aur ML lifecycle ki foundation hain.

Yaad rakho: Logging ko kabhi application ko break nahi karna chahiye, aur print() ko production code me logging ki jagah use mat karo. Levels, formatting aur alag-alag loggers se aap exactly wahi information pa sakte ho jo us waqt chahiye — na zyada noise, na kam context.
Book ka poora code — official repo se (code cells/files only, outputs nahi):
describe.py — chapter6/simple-logging/describe.py
from os import path
import sys
import pandas as pd

argument = sys.argv[-1]

try:
    df = pd.read_csv(argument)
    print(df.describe())
except Exception as error:
    print(f"Had a problem trying to read the CSV file: {error}")
logging_describe.py — chapter6/simple-logging/logging_describe.py
from os import path
import sys
import pandas as pd
import logging

log_format = "[%(name)s][%(levelname)-6s] %(message)s"
logging.basicConfig(format=log_format)
logger = logging.getLogger("describe")
logger.setLevel(logging.ERROR)

argument = sys.argv[-1]
logger.debug("processing input file: %s", argument)

try:
    df = pd.read_csv(argument)
    print(df.describe())
except Exception:
    logger.exception("Had a problem trying to read the CSV file")

logger.info("the program continues, without issue")
http-app.py — multiple loggers — chapter6/multiple-loggers/http-app.py
import requests
import logging

logging.basicConfig()
root_logger = logging.getLogger()

# Sets logging level for every single app, the "parent" logger
root_logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)

# new logger for this script
logger = logging.getLogger('http-app')


logger.info("About to send a request to example.com")
requests.get('http://example.com')

# fine tune the urllib logger:
urllib_logger = logging.getLogger('urllib3')
urllib_logger.setLevel(logging.ERROR)
#
logger.info("About to send another request to example.com")
requests.get('http://example.com')

06.3Chapter 6 · Monitoring and Logging

Monitoring Drift — SageMaker and Azure ML

Model production me jaane ke baad data badal sakta hai — naye values, naye types, ya seasonal patterns. Isi ko data drift kehte hain, aur ise pakadna MLOps ka sabse important kaam hai. Is section me AWS SageMaker Model Monitor aur Azure ML drift detection ka practical workflow dekhenge.

Drift kya hai aur kyun dangerous hai

Drift ka matlab hai training data aur serving data ke beech farq aa jana. Iske kai causes ho sakte hain — value types me change (jaise Fahrenheit se Celsius), empty ya null values, ya natural drift jaise seasonal changes. Book me swimsuit sales ka example hai — agar hafte ki sales zero ho jayein, to kya dataset drift kar gaya, ya bas winter hai aur koi khareed hi nahi raha? Data ko gehrai se samajhne par hi ye sawal answer ho sakta hai.

Production me significant accuracy change ke saath model deploy kabhi nahi hona chahiye — ise rokna zaroori hai. Aur jitni jaldi ye problems detect hon, utna sasta unhe fix karna hota hai.

SageMaker — data capture enable karna

SageMaker Model Monitor ke liye pehle deploy karte waqt data capture enable karna hota hai, DataCaptureConfig class se:

from sagemaker.model_monitor import DataCaptureConfig
s3_capture_path = "s3://monitoring/xgb-churn-data"
data_capture_config = DataCaptureConfig(enable_capture=True, sampling_percentage=100, destination_s3_uri=s3_capture_path)
predictor = model.deploy(initial_instance_count=1, instance_type="ml.m4.large", endpoint_name="xgb-churn-monitor", data_capture_config=data_capture_config, deserializer=CSVDeserializer())

Phir endpoint par prediction requests bhejo — test_data.csv ki har row ek prediction banati hai, aur capture configuration data ko S3 bucket me save kar deti hai. Bucket ko list karke confirm karo ki .jsonl files ban rahi hain:

aws s3 ls s3://monitoring/xgb-churn-data/datacapture/AllTraffic/2021/02/03/13/

SageMaker — baseline banana aur schedule chalana

Captured data se baseline banayi jati hai. Baseline dataset aur target dataset shuru me ek hi ho sakte hain — isiliye documentation me dono terms interchangeably use hote hain aur confusion hota hai. Baseline ko gold standard samjho, aur naya data target hai. DefaultModelMonitor se baseline suggest karo:

from sagemaker.model_monitor import DefaultModelMonitor
monitor = DefaultModelMonitor(role=role, instance_count=1, instance_type="ml.m5.xlarge", volume_size_in_gb=20, max_runtime_in_seconds=3600)
monitor.suggest_baseline(baseline_dataset=s3_path + "/training-dataset.csv", dataset_format=DatasetFormat.csv(header=True), output_s3_uri=s3_path + "/baseline/", wait=True)

Run complete hone par S3 me do files banti hain — constraints.json aur statistics.json. Inhe Pandas se visualize kar sakte ho. Phir hourly monitoring schedule banao jo baseline se traffic ko compare kare:

from sagemaker.model_monitor import CronExpressionGenerator
monitor.create_monitoring_schedule(monitor_schedule_name="xgb-churn-monitor-schedule", endpoint_input=predictor.endpoint_name, output_s3_uri=s3_report_path, statistics=monitor.baseline_statistics(), constraints=monitor.suggested_constraints(), schedule_cron_expression=CronExpressionGenerator.hourly(), enable_cloudwatch_metrics=True)

Reports me teen JSON files hoti hain — constraint_violations.json, constraint.json aur statistics.json. Violations me jaise State_MI feature par 99.7% data Integral tha jabki 100% expected tha — ye chhoti violation hai. Lekin Churn feature par 0% Integral milna critical situation hai — yehi wo moment hai jiske liye poora system banaya gaya tha. Ek baat dhyaan rakho — AWS ke paas 20-minute ka buffer hota hai, isliye hourly schedule ke reports hour mark ke 20 minute baad tak aa sakte hain.

Azure ML — data drift detection

Azure bhi drift ko usi tarah handle karta hai — baseline dataset, target dataset aur monitor, teeno milkar metrics banate hain aur drift detect hone par alerts create karte hain. Book likhe jaane ke waqt Azure ML me data drift detection preview me tha, isliye solid code examples dena mushkil tha — lekin workflow aur concepts saaf hain.

Azure me shuruaat target dataset banakar hoti hai, jisme time-series set honi chahiye — timestamp column se ya virtual column se. Virtual column ek nice feature hai — ye dataset ke stored path se timestamp infer karta hai, jise partition format kehte hain. Jaise /2021/10/14/dataset.csv path ka matlab hai 14 October 2021 ka virtual column. Configuration by convention automation ka golden nugget hai — kam configuration matlab kam overhead aur tez workflows.

Baseline dataset ke features target dataset jaise hone chahiye. Monitor ki configuration dono datasets ko jodti hai, schedule banati hai, aur data drift percentage ke liye tolerable threshold set karti hai. Drift results Dataset Monitors tab me milte hain — drift magnitude aur sabse zyada drift wale top features ki sorted list ke saath. Gehre metrics ke liye Application Insights se monitor se judi logs aur metrics query ki ja sakti hain.

Yaad rakho: Baseline banana ek baar ka heavy lifting hai, phir wo rarely badalta hai — isliye use automate kar lo aur thresholds ko fine-tune karo taaki bekar violations na aayein. Drift ko jaldi pakadna hi production model ko catastrophic failure se bachata hai.
Book ka poora code — official repo se (code cells/files only, outputs nahi):
capture.py — SageMaker — chapter6/sagemaker/capture.py
from sagemaker.model_monitor import DataCaptureConfig

s3_capture_path = "s3://monitoring/xgb-churn-data"


data_capture_config = DataCaptureConfig(
    enable_capture=True, sampling_percentage=100, destination_s3_uri=s3_capture_path
)


from sagemaker.deserializers import CSVDeserializer

predictor = model.deploy(
    initial_instance_count=1,
    instance_type="ml.m4.large",
    endpoint_name="xgb-churn-monitor",
    data_capture_config=data_capture_config,
    deserializer=CSVDeserializer(),
)
invoke.py — SageMaker — chapter6/sagemaker/invoke.py
from sagemaker.predictor import Predictor
from sagemaker.serializers import CSVDeserializer, CSVSerializer
import time

endpoint_name="xgb-churn-monitor"

predictor = Predictor(
    endpoint_name=endpoint_name,
    deserializer=CSVDeserializer(),
    serializer=CSVSerializer(),
)

# get a subset of test data for a quick test
#!head -120 test_data/test-dataset-input-cols.csv > test_data/test_sample.csv
print("Sending test traffic to the endpoint {}. \nPlease wait...".format(endpoint_name))

with open("test_data/test_sample.csv", "r") as f:
    for row in f:
        payload = row.rstrip("\n")
        response = predictor.predict(data=payload)
        time.sleep(0.5)

print("Done!")

07Chapter 7 · MLOps for AWS

MLOps for AWS

Kaunsa cloud chunein? Book ka jawab hai — safe choice Amazon hai. AWS ke paas sabse wide selection of technology aur sabse bada market share hai. Ek baar AWS master kar liya, to dusre clouds ko samajhna aasan ho jata hai, kyunki wo bhi maan kar chalte hain ki aapko AWS aata hoga. Ye chapter AWS par MLOps ki foundations aur practical patterns cover karta hai.

AWS ki culture — Day 1 aur customer first

AWS 2005-2006 me launch hua — MTurk, Amazon S3, Amazon EC2 aur Amazon SQS ke saath. Ye core offerings aaj bhi hain aur har quarter behtar hoti ja rahi hain. Iske peeche AWS ki culture hai — Amazon me hamesha "Day 1" hota hai, matlab pehle din wali energy aur enthusiasm har din honi chahiye. Aur customer ko "heart of everything" me rakha jata hai.

Ye culture Google se bahut alag hai — Google research-oriented hai, jahan Kubernetes aur TensorFlow jaise complex engineering marvels bane, lekin customer first na hone ki wajah se cloud market share me use nuksan hua. AWS ke leadership principles "Bias for Action" aur "Deliver Results" hain — speed se kaam karo, critical inputs par focus karo, aur results jaldi deliver karo. SageMaker jaise products me yehi spirit dikhti hai.

Is chapter me kya cover hoga

Chapter AWS ke sheer size ki wajah se har aspect cover nahi kar sakta — exhaustive coverage ke liye Data Science on AWS book refer ki gayi hai. Is chapter ka focus higher-level services par hai — AWS Lambda, AWS App Runner, Fargate, Elastic Beanstalk, aur SageMaker jaise complex systems ke baare me dusre chapters me baat hoti hai.

Aage ke sections me hum dekhenge — AWS se shuruaat kaise karein, Free Tier, AWS Academy aur AWS Educate kya hain, Comprehend jaise no-code/low-code NLP solutions, Hugo static website ko S3 par deploy karna, serverless cookbook, Fargate aur App Runner jaise container services, DeepLens se computer vision, aur MLOps Cookbook ka poora end-to-end workflow.

Accuracy, explainability, operations — kaunse do chunein?

Chapter ek bahut achha sawal uthata hai — jab ML problem me teen constraints hon — prediction accuracy, explainability, aur operations — to success ke liye kaunse do par focus karein, aur kis order me? Academic-focused data scientists turant accuracy ki taraf jate hain — behtar models banana ek fun challenge hai, jaise Tetris khelna.

Lekin dusra approach hai — pehle model ko operationalize karna. Iska fayda hai ki baad me model accuracy software system ke improvements ke saath-saath improve hoti rehti hai. Bilkul waise hi jaise Japanese automobile industry ne Kaizen ya continuous improvement par focus kiya — reasonable initial accuracy se shuru karo aur jaldi improve karo.

Yaad rakho: AWS par MLOps ka matlab sirf SageMaker nahi hai — Lambda, App Runner, Fargate, Elastic Beanstalk aur high-level AI APIs ka poora ecosystem hai. Sahi service chunna is baat par depend karta hai ki aapki team kitni mature hai aur problem kya hai.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 7 — MLOps for AWS
← Previous06.3 · Monitoring Drift — SageMaker and Azure ML→ Next07.1 · Introduction to AWS and Getting Started
07.1Chapter 7 · MLOps for AWS

Introduction to AWS and Getting Started

AWS se shuruaat karna bahut aasan hai — sirf ek Free Tier account chahiye. University me ho to AWS Academy aur AWS Educate bhi use kar sakte ho — Academy hands-on certification material aur labs deta hai, Educate classrooms ke liye sandboxes deta hai. Account milne ke baad agla step hai alag-alag offerings ke saath experiment karna.

Costco analogy — AWS ko samajhne ka tareeka

Book AWS ko Costco bulk wholesale store se compare karta hai. Costco me teen tareeke hain — pehla, customer bulk me sasta ready-made pizza order kare. Dusra, naya customer store me ghoom kar raw ingredients jaise sugar dekhe aur samjhe ki in se kya ban sakta hai. Teesra, customer premade meals aur raw ingredients dono ko jaanta ho, to catering company ya restaurant khol sakta hai.

Bilkul waise hi AWS par bhi alag levels hain. Prepared food zyada mehenga hota hai, raw ingredients saste. Aapki organization ki maturity aur problem ke hisab se aap decide karte ho ki kitna kaam AWS se karwana hai aur kitna khud karna hai. Economics me comparative advantage ka theory kehta hai — cost ko directly compare mat karo, opportunity cost compare karo. Cloud provider ka specialization data center chalana hai — aapka kaam customer ke liye revenue-generating product banana hai, cloud provider ka kaam dobara banana nahi.

No-code/low-code — AWS Comprehend

Shuruaat ke liye best jagah hai Costco pizza wale customer ki tarah behave karna — ready-made service use karo. Jaise ek Fortune 500 company ko customer service products me NLP add karna ho — wo 9 mahine se ek saal team hire karke capability banane me laga sakti hai, ya AWS Comprehend use kar sakti hai. Comprehend se entity detection, key phrase detection, PII detection, language detection aur sentiment analysis jaise NLP operations kiye ja sakte hain.

Aap text ko Amazon Comprehend Console me cut-paste karke Analyze dabao, aur wo entities highlight kar dega. Medical records review karna ya customer service response ka sentiment nikalna bhi boto3 Python SDK se equally straightforward hai.

Hello world — Hugo static website on S3

AWS ke core infrastructure ko samajhne ka achha tareeka hai ek Hugo website ko Amazon S3 static website hosting par deploy karna. S3 low cost aur highly reliable hai — pricing lagbhag ek penny per GB ke aas-paas hai. Poora project GitHub repo me hai — markdown files, Hugo template, aur AWS CodeBuild ke build commands.

Poora kaam buildspec.yml file ke through hota hai — pehle hugo binary install hoti hai, phir hugo command HTML files generate karti hai, aur aakhir me ek command poora deployment kar deti hai:

version: 0.1
phases:
  install:
    commands:
      - cd /tmp
      - wget https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/releases/download/v0.80.0/hugo_extended_0.80.0_Linux-64bit.tar.gz
      - tar -xzf hugo_extended_0.80.0_Linux-64bit.tar.gz
      - mv hugo /usr/bin/hugo
  build:
    commands:
      - rm -rf public
      - hugo
  post_build:
    commands:
      - aws s3 sync --delete public s3://dukefeb1
      - echo Build completed on date

Ye build file ek recipe ki tarah hai — wahi steps AWS Cloud9 development environment me manually bhi kiye ja sakte hain. Cloud9 ka khaas fayda hai ki aap usi jagah develop karte ho jahan saara action hota hai — code checkout karo, cloud me test karo, aur wahi tool se deploy verify karo.

Computer vision — AWS DeepLens

Applied computer vision course me AWS DeepLens use hota hai — ek deep learning-enabled video camera developer kit jisme 1080p camera, operating system aur wireless capabilities hoti hain. Ye computer vision prototyping ki sabse mushkil problem solve karta hai — data capture karna aur use kahin bhejna.

DeepLens video capture karke use do streams me baant deta hai. Project Stream real-time annotation add karke packets ko MQTT (MQ Telemetry Transport) service par bhejta hai — ye ek publish-subscribe network protocol hai. MQTT packets real time me aate hain jaise hi objects stream me detect hote hain. Is "plug and play" technology se zero se one tak pahunchna bahut aasan ho jata hai.

Yaad rakho: AWS par shuruaat hamesha chhote se karo — pehle Free Tier account, phir Comprehend jaise ready-made service, phir S3 par ek hello world website. Core infrastructure samajh lo, to ML deployment baad me bahut aasan lagega.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 7 — MLOps for AWS
← Previous07 · MLOps for AWS→ Next07.2 · MLOps on AWS — Cookbook, CLI Tools, Flask Microservice
07.2Chapter 7 · MLOps for AWS

MLOps on AWS — Cookbook, CLI Tools, Flask Microservice

AWS par MLOps ka matlab hai — model ko ek baar train karke bhool jana nahi, balki use ek repeatable, automated system me dalna. Is section me Elastic Beanstalk par continuous delivery, MLOps Cookbook ka spartan recipe, CLI tools aur Flask microservice ka poora workflow dekhenge.

Serverless cookbook — function hi center hai

Serverless MLOps ki ek crucial methodology hai. Python function ek unit of work hai — input leta hai aur optionally output deta hai. Agar Python function ek toaster hai — bread dalo, garam karo, toast nikalo — to serverless bijli ka source hai. Function ko chalne ke liye kahin to plug hona padega, aur serverless wahi kaam karta hai — code ko cloud me chalata hai, bina servers ke.

AWS Lambda serverless ki sabse low-level service hai. Sabse simple example hai Marco Polo function — event me "Marco" aaye to "Polo" return karo, warna "No!":

def lambda_handler(event, context):
    print(f"This was the raw event: {event}")
    if event["name"] == "Marco":
        print(f"This event was 'Marco'")
        return "Polo"
    print(f"This event was not 'Marco'")
    return "No!"

Lambda kai tareeko se trigger hoti hai — console, AWS CLI ya boto3 SDK se manually invoke karo, S3 par file upload jaise events par respond karo, ya nightly timer se data download karo. Bilkul waise hi jaise garage ki lightbulb switch se, garage door opener se, ya nightly security timer se jal sakti hai.

S3 trigger se computer vision — Rekognition

Ek zyada complex example hai — S3 trigger ke saath computer vision labeling. Jab nayi image folder me drop hoti hai, to Lambda Rekognition se uske labels nikal leti hai, bahut hi kam code me. Aur kai Lambda functions ko AWS Step Functions se chain bhi kiya ja sakta hai — Marco, phir Polo, phir Finish — har step ek Task hota hai jisme Lambda function ka ARN hota hai.

CLI se Lambda invoke karna bhi simple hai:

aws lambda invoke --cli-binary-format raw-in-base64-out --function-name marcopython --payload '{"name": "Marco"}' response.json

Fargate aur App Runner — containers as a service

Fargate ek container as a service (CaaS) offering hai — developer containerized microservices banane par focus karta hai, deployment cloud platform sambhalta hai. Containers ke fayde hain — production service ko locally apne desktop par mimic kar sakte ho, runtime ko Docker Hub, GitHub Container Registry ya Amazon ECR se easily distribute kar sakte ho, GitHub repo ko source of truth bana sakte ho jisme model, code, IaC aur runtime sab ho, aur CaaS services se production deployment aasan ho jata hai.

Flask change-machine microservice ka workflow hai — Cloud9 me develop karo, container build karke ECR me push karo, phir ECS/Fargate me chalao. Steps hain — virtualenv setup aur make all, local test python app.py se, curl se test, ECR repository banao, container build karo, push karo, docker run se local test karo, Fargate par deploy karo, aur public service test karo.

AWS App Runner isse bhi simple karta hai — source code se seedha deploy karo ya container point karo. Wizard me bas teen cheezein batani hoti hain — build command pip install -r requirements.txt, run command python app.py, aur port 8080. App Runner source repo, deploy environment aur secure URL ko ek streamlined workflow me jod deta hai, aur CloudWatch, Load Balancers, Container Services aur API Gateways jaise services ko ek complete offering me connect karta hai.

Elastic Beanstalk par continuous delivery

Continuous delivery (CD) MLOps ka core component hai. Elastic Beanstalk ek platform as a service technology hai jo application deploy karne ka bahut sa kaam streamline kar deti hai. Example stack hai — AWS Cloud9 se development shuru karo, GitHub repo me source code rakho, change events par AWS CodeBuild trigger ho, CodeBuild CI chalakar tests kare, aur continuous delivery se AWS Elastic Beanstalk par deploy kare.

Replicate karne ke steps hain — repo ko Cloud9 ya CloudShell me checkout karo, virtualenv banao aur make all chalao, eb init se naya app initialize karo, eb create se remote environment banao, aur AWS CodeBuild project setup karo jiska buildspec make install, make lint aur make deploy chalata hai. Book ki salah hai — complex ML project me jaane se pehle pehle ek "hello world" type project ko continuous deployment ke saath working kar lo.

MLOps Cookbook — ek spartan recipe

MLOps Cookbook project intentionally spartan hai taaki focus ML deploy karne par rahe. Ye project MLB players ke weight se height predict karta hai. GitHub source of truth hai, build service GitHub Actions hai, container service GitHub Container Registry hai — AWS par inki jagah AWS CodeBuild aur AWS ECR le sakte hain. Ek baar project containerized ho gaya, to deployment targets khul jate hain — AWS Lambda, Elastic Beanstalk aur App Runner.

Project ki files hain — Makefile (recipes ki list aur unhe invoke karne ka tareeka), requirements.txt (pinned versions ke saath Python packages), cli.py (CLI se prediction), utilscli.py (retrain aur alag-alag endpoints query karne ka utility), app.py (Flask web microservice jo /predict par JSON prediction deta hai), mlib.py (model handling library — load, retrain, scale, predict), htwtmlb.csv (input scaling ke liye CSV), model.joblib (sklearn se exported model), Dockerfile (containerization), aur Jupyter notebook (model banane ke peeche ki thinking).

CLI tools — Click se predictions aur retraining

CLI tools ML models ko operationalize karne ka tez tareeka hain. Main cli.py se height predict karo:

./cli.py --weight 180

Asli magic mlib.py library me hai — data scale karo, prediction karo, phir inverse transform se wapas human-readable height banao. utilscli.py se model retrain karo aur deployed API ko query karo:

./utilscli.py retrain --tsize 0.4
./utilscli.py predict --weight 400

CLI ko containerize bhi kiya ja sakta hai — Makefile, cli.py aur Dockerfile hi teen critical files hain. Makefile me hadolint se Dockerfile lint karna bhi hai. Phir docker build aur docker push se container registry me dalo. Ye workflow ML-based CLI tools ke liye ideal hai.

Flask microservice — /predict endpoint

Flask ML microservice ka core simple hai — mlib.py heavy lifting karta hai, Flask route sirf POST request leta hai aur JSON prediction return karta hai:

from flask import Flask, request, jsonify
import mlib
app = Flask(__name__)
@app.route("/predict", methods=['POST'])
def predict():
    json_payload = request.json
    prediction = mlib.predict(json_payload['Weight'])
    return jsonify({'prediction': prediction})
if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=8080, debug=True)

Test karne ke liye predict.sh naam ki chhoti bash script curl ki jargon se bachati hai — Weight 200 bhejkar prediction milti hai, jaise 73.61 inches, matlab 6 foot, 2 inches. Containerized version me docker build karke docker run -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 se local chalao. GitHub Actions se container automatically build karke GitHub Container Registry me push bhi kiya ja sakta hai — docker/login-action aur docker/build-push-action se.

Yaad rakho: MLOps Cookbook ka mantra hai — ek hi recipe, kai deployment targets. Pehle CLI aur Flask se model ko locally working kar lo, phir use containerize karo — uske baad Lambda, Beanstalk, Fargate ya App Runner me se koi bhi target chunna aasan ho jata hai.
Book ka poora code — official repo se (code cells/files only, outputs nahi):
batch.py — chapter7/batch.py
@cli.group()
def run():
    """AWS Batch CLI"""

@run.command("submit")
@click.option("--queue", default="queue", help="Batch Queue")
@click.option("--jobname", default="1", help="Name of Job")
@click.option("--jobdef", default="test", help="Job Definition")
@click.option("--cmd", default=["whoami"], help="Container Override Commands")
def submit(queue, jobname, jobdef, cmd):
    """Submit a job to AWS Batch SErvice"""

    result = submit_job(
        job_name=jobname,
        job_queue=queue,
        job_definition=jobdef,
        command=cmd
    )
    click.echo(f"CLI:  Run Job Called {jobname}")
    return result
dyno.py — chapter7/dyno.py
def query_police_department_record_by_guid(guid):
    """Gets one record in the PD table by guid
    
    In [5]: rec = query_police_department_record_by_guid(
        "7e607b82-9e18-49dc-a9d7-e9628a9147ad"
        )
    
    In [7]: rec
    Out[7]: 
    {'PoliceDepartmentName': 'Hollister',
     'UpdateTime': 'Fri Mar  2 12:43:43 2018',
     'guid': '7e607b82-9e18-49dc-a9d7-e9628a9147ad'}
    """
    
    db = dynamodb_resource()
    extra_msg = {"region_name": REGION, "aws_service": "dynamodb", 
        "police_department_table":POLICE_DEPARTMENTS_TABLE,
        "guid":guid}
    log.info(f"Get PD record by GUID", extra=extra_msg)
    pd_table = db.Table(POLICE_DEPARTMENTS_TABLE)
    response = pd_table.get_item(
        Key={
            'guid': guid
            }
    )
    return response['Item']
