07.3Chapter 7 · MLOps for AWS

AWS Lambda Recipes — SAM Local and Containerized Deploy

AWS Lambda shayad ML predictions serve karne ya MLOps process me events handle karne ke liye sabse valuable aur flexible compute option hai — kyunki development aur testing ki speed bahut tez hai. Is section me SAM (Serverless Application Model) se Lambda deploy karne ke do tareeke dekhenge — SAM Local aur containerized deploy.

SAM kya hai aur kyun use karein

SAM ek deployment process aur development toolkit hai jo Lambda functions, event sources aur dusre resources ko ek saath jodta hai. AWS ke hisab se SAM ke key benefits hain — single-deployment configuration, AWS CloudFormation ka extension, built-in best practices, local debugging aur testing, aur development tools jaise Cloud9 ke saath deep integration.

Shuruaat ke liye AWS SAM CLI install karo — AWS Cloud9 me ye pehle se installed hota hai. Phir official guide ko follow karo, kyunki CLI actively change hota rehta hai aur book likhe jaane ke waqt current CLI version V2 thi.

SAM Local — local par test karo, phir deploy karo

SAM Local ka workflow hai — SAM install karo, sam init chalao, aur sam local invoke se locally test karo. Cloud9 par build kar rahe ho to utils/resize.sh se disk size badhana achha idea hai, taaki kai containers build kar sako:

sam init
sam local invoke
utils/resize.sh 30

Typical SAM init layout me sam-app folder hota hai jisme app.py, requirements.txt, template.yaml aur tests folder hota hai. Local testing ka fayda ye hai ki deploy se pehle hi pata chal jata hai ki function sahi chal raha hai ya nahi.

Containerized deploy — app.py, Dockerfile, template.yaml

SAM containerized workflow support karta hai — ek container register karo jise AWS Lambda use kare. Critical steps me teen files hoti hain — app.py (Lambda entry point), Dockerfile (jo build hokar Amazon ECR me jata hai), aur template.yaml (jisse SAM app deploy karta hai).

Lambda handler bahut kam kaam karta hai kyunki heavy lifting abhi bhi mlib.py library me hai. Ek "gotcha" hai — Lambda ko invoke karne ke tareeke ke hisab se alag logic chahiye. Console ya Python se invoke ho to event me seedha payload hota hai, lekin API Gateway integration me payload event ke body se extract karna padta hai:

import json
import mlib
def lambda_handler(event, context):
    print(f"RAW LAMBDA EVENT BODY: {event}")
    if 'body' in event:
        event = json.loads(event["body"])
        print("API Gateway Request event")
    else:
        print("Function Request")
    if event and "Weight" in event:
        weight = event["Weight"]
        prediction = mlib.predict(weight)
        print(f"Prediction: {prediction}")
        return {"statusCode": 200, "body": json.dumps(prediction)}
    else:
        payload = {"Message": "Incorrect or Empty Payload"}
        return {"statusCode": 200, "body": json.dumps(payload)}

Dockerfile Lambda ke base image se model aur code ko pack karta hai — chhota ML model container ke andar pack ho sakta hai, aur AWS CodeBuild se programmatically retrain karke bhi pack kiya ja sakta hai:

FROM public.ecr.aws/lambda/python:3.8
COPY model.joblib mlib.py htwtmlb.csv app.py requirements.txt ./
RUN python3.8 -m pip install -r requirements.txt -t .
CMD ["app.lambda_handler"]

SAM template — Infrastructure as Code

SAM template IaC (Infrastructure as Code) layer control karta hai, jisse deployment process aasan ho jata hai. Template me HelloWorldMLFunction define hoti hai — PackageType Image, aur ek Api event jo /predict path par POST method se trigger hota hai. Outputs me API Gateway endpoint URL aur Lambda function ka ARN milta hai.

Aakhir me sirf do commands chalani hoti hain — sam build aur sam deploy --guided. Guided deploy me prompts har step par guide karte hain. Local test ke liye sam local invoke -e payload.json use karo, jisme payload hoti hai:

{"Weight": 200}

Local test me container spin up hota hai, payload jati hai aur prediction wapas aati hai — jaise height 73.61 inches, 6 foot 2 inches. Deploy ke baad Lambda ko test karne ke kai tareeke hain — AWS Lambda Console se image verify karo, Cloud9 console se invoke karo, ya Postman tool se API test karo.

Real-world patterns — kaunsi service kab

Book recommended ML engineering patterns ki partial list deta hai. Container as a service (CaaS) — jahan organization ko shuruaat karni ho, wahan App Runner achha starting point hai. SageMaker — badi organizations, alag teams aur bade data ke liye, kyunki fine-grained security aur enterprise-level deployment aur training milti hai. Serverless with AI APIs — chhote startups jo bahut tez move karna chahte hain, unke liye pretrained models via API aur Lambda jaise serverless technology best hai.

Case studies me bhi yehi lessons repeat hote hain — machine learning software engineering hai, isliye traceability, versioning, testing, automation aur documentation optional nahi hain. Code aur datasets versioned aur traced hone chahiye, models safely deploy hone chahiye quality gates aur canary ya blue-green strategies ke saath, monitoring critical hai — infrastructure (throughput, latency) aur ML (prediction quality, data drift) dono taraf se — aur models ko incoming traffic ke hisab se scale up aur down hona chahiye. Aur haan, ye sab processes jitna ho sake automated hone chahiye.

Yaad rakho: SAM ka sabse bada fayda hai local testing — sam local invoke se pehle locally verify karo, phir sam deploy --guided se production me jao. Aur API Gateway wale Lambda me hamesha event ke body ko handle karna mat bhoolo, warna payload kabhi milega hi nahi.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 7 — MLOps for AWS
← Previous07.2 · MLOps on AWS — Cookbook, CLI Tools, Flask Microservice→ Next08 · MLOps for Azure
08Chapter 8 · MLOps for Azure

MLOps for Azure

Azure machine learning ko operationalize karne ki mushkil problems ko solve kar raha hai — datasets aur models ko register aur version karna, live inferencing models ko scalable clusters par deploy karna, aur monitoring ko aasan banana. Ye chapter Azure ML ke practical workflow ko end-to-end cover karta hai.

Azure par MLOps ka overall flow

Azure par kaam ka flow hai — pehle Azure CLI aur SDK se authenticate karo aur workspace setup karo, phir compute instances ya clusters par models train karo, models aur datasets ko register aur version karo, phir ACI ya AKS par deploy karo, aur aakhir me pipelines, Designer aur Application Insights se poori lifecycle ko manage karo.

Book ka point hai — platform chahe koi bhi ho, use aapke workflows ko aasan banana chahiye. Azure abhi functionality me dusre cloud providers se peeche ho sakta hai, lekin ye matter nahi karta — jo available hai use leverage karo, aur cloud features ko dobara invent karne me time waste mat karo. MLOps engineer ka sabse important kaam hai models ko production me ship karna.

ML lifecycle — linear nahi, feedback loop hai

Azure ki saari tooling aur services model lifecycle me madad ke liye hain. Shuruaat training se hoti hai — Notebook, AutoML ya SDK se. Phir validation hoti hai — Azure Designer ya Azure ML Studio se. Phir production deployments Kubernetes ke saath scale karte hain, aur Application Insights se problems par nazar rakhi jati hai.

Ye linear process nahi hai — production me ship karne ke dauraan constant feedback loop chalta hai, aur data issues ya model me dikhi problems ko fix karne ke liye pehle steps par wapas jana pad sakta hai. Ye feedback loop aur constant adjusting healthy environment ke liye zaroori hai — sirf monitoring enable karne wala checkbox click karna ya Kubernetes se scaling karwana kaafi nahi hai. Bina consistent evaluation ke success impossible hai, chahe cloud provider koi bhi ho.

Is chapter me aage kya hai

Aage ke sections me hum dekhenge — Azure CLI, SDK aur authentication kaise kaam karte hain, service principal kya hota hai aur key-based aur token-based auth me kya farq hai, compute instances aur clusters kaise banate hain, models aur datasets ko register aur version kaise karte hain, ACI aur AKS par deploy kaise karte hain, aur Azure ML Pipelines, Designer aur troubleshooting — logs, Application Insights aur local debugging — kaise karte hain.

Yaad rakho: Azure par sabse important baat hai reuse — jo service available hai use karo, apna half-baked solution mat banao. Register karo, version karo, authenticate karo, aur deploy karo — phir feedback loop se lagatar improve karo.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — MLOps for Azure
← Previous07.3 · AWS Lambda Recipes — SAM Local and Containerized Deploy→ Next08.1 · Azure CLI, SDK and Authentication
08.1Chapter 8 · MLOps for Azure

Azure CLI, SDK and Authentication

Azure par kaam shuru karne se pehle authentication samajhna zaroori hai — kyunki automation ka matlab hai bina baar-baar prompt ke kaam hona. Is section me service principal banana, use workspace se jodna, aur API services ke liye key-based aur token-based authentication dekhenge.

Service principal kya hai aur kyun chahiye

Service principal ek aisa account hai jo automation ke liye banaya jata hai — isse aap bina baar-baar login prompt ke Azure se interact kar sakte ho. Azure CLI se service principal banane par output me clientId milta hai, saath me management aur gallery endpoint URLs bhi. Is clientId se aap service principal ka metadata retrieve kar sakte ho:

az ad sp show --id xxxxxxxx-3af0-4065-8e14-xxxxxxxxxxxx

Isse objectId milta hai — jaise 4386304e-3af1-4066-8e14-475091b01502 — aur appDisplayName se confirm hota hai ki service principal ka naam kya hai, jaise "ml-auth". Service principal ka naam valid URI format me hona chahiye, jaise "http://ml-auth".

Service principal ko workspace se jodna

Service principal banane ke baad use Azure Machine Learning workspace aur resource group se associate karna hota hai:

az ml workspace share -w example-workspace -g alfredodeza_rg_linux_centralus --user 4386304e-3af1-4066-8e14-475091b01502 --role owner

Ye command service principal ko workspace se jodne ka aakhri step hai. Ek baat dhyaan rakho — successful call ke baad is command ka koi output nahi aata, isliye ghabrana mat. Account banne ke baad aap ise automation ke saath authentication enable karne ke liye use kar sakte ho, jisse prompts aur constant authenticating se chhutkara milta hai.

Roles — owner versus contributor, least privilege

Examples me role value "owner" use hui hai, jiske paas widespread permissions hote hain. Lekin -role flag ki default value "contributor" hai, jo zyada restricted hai. Apne environment aur usage ke hisab se is value ko adapt karo — aur hamesha access aur role ko least number of permissions tak restrict karo, jitna kaam ke liye zaroori ho.

Ye best practice hai — automation account ko poori duniya ki chabiyan mat do. Sirf wahi permissions do jo use chahiye, aur kuch nahi.

API services ko authenticate karna — keys aur tokens

Kuch environments me service principal account fayda nahi deta — jaise jab services internet par expose hoti hain aur deployed models se HTTP requests ke through interact karna hota hai. Aise cases me deploy karne se pehle ye decide karna hota hai ki kaunsi authentication enable karni hai. Azure do types support karta hai — keys aur tokens — aur inke defaults deployment type ke hisab se badalte hain.

  • Key-based authentication: AKS me by default enabled hoti hai. ACI me by default disabled hoti hai (lekin enable ki ja sakti hai) — ACI me by default koi authentication enabled nahi hoti.
  • Token-based authentication: AKS me by default disabled hoti hai. ACI token-based auth support hi nahi karta.

Deploy karne se pehle in cluster types ko samajhna bahut important hai. Test environments me bhi hamesha authentication enable karo, taaki development aur production ke beech mismatch na ho.

Yaad rakho: Automation ke liye service principal banao, use workspace se jodo, aur role ko least privilege tak restrict karo. Aur API services par hamesha authentication enable karo — test me bhi, production me bhi — taaki dono environments ek jaise rahein.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — MLOps for Azure
← Previous08 · MLOps for Azure→ Next08.2 · Compute, Deploying, Registering Models and Datasets
08.2Chapter 8 · MLOps for Azure

Compute, Deploying, Registering Models and Datasets

Azure ML par model ko production me le jane ke chaar bade steps hain — compute setup karna, model deploy karna, model register karna, aur dataset version karna. Ye section in chaaro ko practical examples ke saath cover karta hai.

Compute Instances — managed workstation for data scientists

Azure compute instances ko managed cloud-based workstation kaha jata hai. Ye Jupyter Notebooks ke liye ready-to-use environment deta hai, jisme bahut saari dependencies preinstalled hoti hain. Proof of concepts banane ya tutorials try karne ke liye ye perfect hai — environment setup ki sabse annoying problem hi khatm ho jati hai.

Compute instance Azure ML Studio se banaya ja sakta hai — Manage section me Compute link se. Rule of thumb hai — shuruaat ke liye low-cost virtual machine chuno, jaise Standard_D2_v3, taaki baad me zyada cost na aaye. Machine ke naam badalte rehte hain, isliye aapke options thode alag ho sakte hain.

Compute instance ko training cluster ki tarah bhi use kar sakte ho, kyunki ye job queue, parallel me multiple jobs, aur multi-GPU distributed training support karta hai. Reproducible environments DevOps ka instrumental hissa hain — "But it works on my machine!" wali problem se bachne ke liye consistency aur normalization bahut zaroori hai.

Deploying — batch ya online inference

Azure par deploy karne ke kai tareeke hain. Agar massive amounts of data hai jo memory me reasonably handle nahi ho sakta, to batch inferencing better fit hai — Azure terabytes ke structured aur unstructured data se inferences nikalne me madad karta hai. Chhote datasets ke liye online (instant) inference useful hai — trained model ke liye Azure programmatically ek HTTP API bana deta hai.

HTTP APIs banana zyada kaam nahi hai, lekin ye kaam service ko offload karne se aap aur aapki team zyada substantial cheezon par focus kar sakte ho — jaise data ki quality ya deployment process ki robustness.

Models register karna — optional, lekin highly recommended

Azure documentation kehti hai ki registration optional hai — bina register kiye bhi model deploy ho sakta hai. Lekin jaise-jaise aap models deploy karne aur production me release karne ke process ke aadi hote jao, waise-waise pata chalega ki authentication ya registration jaise features ko skip karna shuru me aasan lagta hai, lekin baad me problems create karta hai.

Model versioning ke key fayde hain — aap identify kar sakte ho ki kaunsa model version use ho raha hai, descriptions ke saath kai versions me se jaldi select kar sakte ho, aur bina effort ke rollback karke dusra model select kar sakte ho. Ye Git ki tarah hai — production-level models ke changes ko samajhna versioning se natural ho jata hai.

Azure me train kiye model ko Run object se register karo:

description = "AutoML trained model"
model = run.register_model(description=description)
print(run.model_id)

Azure ke bahar train kiya hua model bhi register kar sakte ho — jaise local ONNX model:

import os
from azureml.core.model import Model
model = Model.register(workspace=ws, model_path="models/world_wines.onnx", model_name="world_wines", tags={"onnx": "world-wines"}, description="Image classification of world-wide wine labels")

Python SDK hi ek tareeka nahi hai — Azure CLI se bhi register kar sakte ho, aur Azure ML Studio se seedha upload karke register kar sakte ho:

az ml model register --name world_wines --model-path mnist/model.onnx

Datasets version karna — Git data ke liye fit nahi hai

Models ki tarah datasets ko version karna bhi ML ki sabse badi problems me se ek solve karta hai — enormous datasets jo thode-thode alag hote hain, unhe version karna mushkil tha. Git source code changes ke liye hai, bade datasets ke liye fit nahi hai. Data ML pipeline ka sabse important piece hai, aur data raw se clean tak kai rounds se guzarta hai, isliye har step par version karna instrumental hai.

Dataset retrieve karo, phir register karo — create_new_version=True se naya version banta hai, versions 1 se shuru hote hain:

from azureml.core import Dataset
csv_url = "https://automlsamplenotebookdata.blob.core.windows.net/automl-sample-notebook-data/bankmarketing_train.csv"
dataset = Dataset.Tabular.from_delimited_files(path=csv_url)
dataset = dataset.register(workspace=workspace, name="bankmarketing_dataset", description="Bankmarketing training data", create_new_version=True)
bankmarketing_dataset = Dataset.get_by_name(workspace=workspace, name="bankmarketing_dataset", version=1)

Ek important baat — naya dataset version banane ka matlab ye nahi hai ki Azure poora dataset copy kar leta hai. Datasets storage service me data ke references use karte hain.

Cluster par deploy — ACI versus AKS

Model deploy karne ke liye pehle cluster configure karna hota hai. Automated ML run banate waqt dataset select karo, meaningful name aur description do, aur "Create a new compute" se naya cluster banao. Do significant cluster types hain — Inference Cluster (peeche Kubernetes) aur Compute Cluster (virtual machines). Training ke liye Compute Cluster use karna aam hai, aur inference ke liye Inference Cluster.

Compute Cluster me minimum aur maximum nodes decide karne hote hain — parallel runs ki sankhya maximum nodes se zyada nahi ho sakti. Minimum nodes 0 rakhne se idle nodes ka charge nahi lagta, kyunki cluster unused hone par 0 par scale down ho jata hai. Nodes, RAM aur CPU cores ki sahi sankhya trial-and-error se nikalti hai — test run ke liye kam se shuru karo, aur zaroorat padne par zyada powerful cluster banao.

Deploy ke liye do key tareeke hain — Azure Container Instance (ACI), jo testing aur test environments ke liye best hai, khaas taur par jab models 1 GB se chhote hon; aur Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), jo Kubernetes ke saare benefits deta hai, khaas taur par scaling, aur 1 GB se bade models ke liye hai. Azure ML Studio me Models section se model select karo, compute type chuno, authentication enable karo — kyunki deploy complete hone ke baad keys ke bina container se interact nahi kar paoge.

Deploy hone ke baad Endpoints section me deployment ka dashboard milta hai — Details, Consume aur Deployment Logs tabs ke saath. Details tab me REST endpoint dikhta hai, aur authentication enable hone par "Key-based authentication" true dikhta hai. Phir Python requests library se HTTP par interact karo — JSON input bhejo aur Bearer key header me bhejo:

import requests
import json
scoring_uri = 'http://676fac5d-5232-adc2-3032c3.eastus.azurecontainer.io/score'
key = 'q8szMDoNlxCpiGI8tnqax1yDiy'
data = {"data": [{"age": 47, "campaign": 3, "contact": "home", "day_of_week": "fri", "default": "yes", "duration": 95, "education": "high.school", "nr.employed": 4.967, "poutcome": "failure", "previous": 1}]}
input_data = json.dumps(data)
headers = {'Content-Type': 'application/json'}
headers['Authorization'] = f'Bearer {key}'
resp = requests.post(scoring_uri, input_data, headers=headers)
print(resp.json())

Galat input par HTTP 500 error aata hai — jaise ONNX model ko galat keys milne par. Common errors hain — missing Content-Type header, GET ki jagah POST use karna, aur malformed Authorization header. Inhe fix karna aasan hai — sahi content type declare karo, POST request bhejo, aur header ko "Authorization: Bearer <token>" format me banao.

Yaad rakho: Models aur datasets dono ko register aur version karo — shuru me optional lagta hai, lekin production me yehi aapko rollback, traceability aur reproducibility deta hai. Aur deploy karte waqt authentication enable karna mat bhoolo.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — MLOps for Azure
← Previous08.1 · Azure CLI, SDK and Authentication→ Next08.3 · Azure ML Pipelines, Designer and Troubleshooting
08.3Chapter 8 · MLOps for Azure

Azure ML Pipelines, Designer and Troubleshooting

Pipeline ka matlab hai — desired goal achieve karne ke liye kai steps ka coordinated flow. Azure ML Pipelines, Designer aur troubleshooting tools milkar poori ML lifecycle ko manageable banate hain. Is section me pipelines banana, publish karna, Designer use karna, aur deployment issues debug karna dekhenge.

Azure ML Pipelines — steps towards an objective

Azure ML pipelines teen scenarios ke liye achhe hain — machine learning, data preparation, aur application orchestration. Inka setup similar hota hai, bas information ke sources aur completion ke targets alag hote hain. Pipelines ko Python SDK ya Azure ML Studio se banaya ja sakta hai.

Ek pipeline step ka example hai — pehle se retrieved dataset ko Python script ka input banana. Dataset ko as_named_input se input banao, PipelineData se output define karo, aur PythonScriptStep se step banao:

from azureml.pipeline.steps import PythonScriptStep
from azureml.pipeline.core import PipelineData
from azureml.core import Datastore
dataset_input = bankmarketing_dataset.as_named_input("input")
output = PipelineData("output", datastore=Datastore(ws, "workspaceblobstore"), output_name="output")
prep_step = PythonScriptStep(script_name="prep.py", source_directory="./src", arguments=["--input", dataset_input.as_download(), "--output", output], inputs=[dataset_input], outputs=[output], allow_reuse=True)

Is step me ek key part missing hai — compute target. Pehle se bana hua compute target retrieve karo:

from azureml.core.compute import ComputeTarget, AmlCompute
from azureml.core import Workspace
ws = Workspace.from_config()
compute_target = ws.compute_targets["mlops-target"]

Optionally RunConfiguration bhi de sakte ho — environment variables set karo, ya managed dependencies disable karo. Azure SDK frequently change hota hai, isliye official Microsoft AzureML documentation check karte raho.

Pipelines publish karna — HTTP par trigger karo

Jenkins jaise CI/CD systems se pipelines ka comparison hai — kai steps coordinated tareeke se objective accomplish karte hain. Lekin Azure ka ek straightforward tareeka hai pipeline ko environment ke bahar expose karne ka — pipeline ko publish karke use HTTP par available banao, taaki duniya me kahin se bhi koi system use trigger kar sake.

Isse possibilities endless ho jati hain — aap Azure ke andar ki services, pipelines aur triggers se tied nahi rehte. Pipeline steps kahin aur se bhi start ho sakte hain — jaise company ke closed on-premise environment se ya GitHub jaise public source code service se. Publish karne ke liye pehle ka experiment aur run retrieve karo, phir publish_pipeline call karo:

from azureml.core.experiment import Experiment
from azureml.pipeline.core import PipelineRun
experiment = Experiment(ws, "practical-ml-experiment-1")
run_id = "78e729c3-4746-417f-ad9a-abe970f4966f"
pipeline_run = PipelineRun(experiment, run_id)
published_pipeline = pipeline_run.publish_pipeline(name="ONNX example Pipeline", description="ONNX Public pipeline", version="1.0")

Phir InteractiveLoginAuthentication se auth header lekar REST endpoint par POST karo, aur response se run Id nikalo:

from azureml.core.authentication import InteractiveLoginAuthentication
import requests
interactive_auth = InteractiveLoginAuthentication()
auth_header = interactive_auth.get_authentication_header()
rest_endpoint = published_pipeline.endpoint
response = requests.post(rest_endpoint, headers=auth_header, json={"ExperimentName": "practical-ml-experiment-1"})
run_id = response.json().get('Id')
print(f"Pipeline run submitted with ID: {run_id}")

Azure ML Designer — graphical tareeka

Graphically inclined logo ke liye Azure ML Designer ek achha choice hai — ye ML projects banane ki complexity ko abstract kar deta hai. Process hai — Azure ML Studio me sign in karo, Designer interface select karo, sample project explore karo jaise Automobile Regression project, ya scratch se apna project banao, aur phir pipeline job submit karke run karo.

Designer fancy lag sakta hai, lekin ye Azure ML Studio ecosystem ko samajhne me important role nibhata hai. Sample project par "kicking the tires" karne se aap AutoML, storage, compute clusters aur reporting — sab essential aspects se expose ho jate ho.

Troubleshooting — kabhi assume mat karo

Troubleshooting ek aisi skill hai jo janm se nahi milti — practice aur perseverance se aati hai. Book iski comparison naye sheher me rasta dhundhne se karta hai — suraj ki position ya samundar ko dekho, landmarks ke mental notes lo, aur har step ko mentally review karo. Dost bolein left, to bhi assume mat karo — trust karo, lekin validate karo. Agar park na mile, to backtrack karke dusri taraf jao. Question everything, pay attention to details, trust but verify.

Container deploy karne ke baad logs retrieve karne ke kai tareeke hain — Azure ML Studio, command line, ya Python SDK:

from azureml.core import Workspace
from azureml.core.webservice import Webservice
ws = Workspace.from_config()
service = Webservice(ws, "mobelinetv-deploy")
logs = service.get_logs()
for line in logs.split('
'):
    print(line)

Successful deployment me logs zyada interesting nahi hote — model path, ONNX runtime session initialize, aur listening addresses dikhte hain. Logs me noise ke beech se useful highlights nikalni padti hain.

Application Insights — observability out-of-the-box

Observability ka matlab hai kisi bhi point par system ki state capture karna — dashboards, log aggregation, graphs aur alerting mechanisms se poori system ko visualize karna. Ye sirf application logs ke baare me nahi hai — ye problems aane par applications ki kahani batane ke baare me hai. Jaise Python traceback milna ka matlab ye nahi ki Python code fix karna hai — ho sakta hai external system ne JSON payload ki jagah empty file bhej di ho.

Azure Application Insights ko ek simple SDK call se enable kiya ja sakta hai:

from azureml.core.webservice import Webservice
service = Webservice(ws, "mobelinetv-deploy")
service.update(enable_app_insights=True)

Enable hone ke baad ML Studio me API endpoint section me ye dikhta hai, aur dashboard me response times, failure rates aur exceptions — sab aggregated, timestamped aur graphed milte hain.

Local debugging — production container ko locally chalao

Production web server me login karke dekhna dangerous aur problematic hai. Behtar tareeka hai problem ko reproduce karna — wahi production-grade model, wahi container, locally chalao. Azure Python SDK LocalWebservice class se model ko local container me deploy karne ki facility deta hai — iske liye Docker installed aur running hona zaroori hai.

Steps hain — model register karo, environment banao (jaise onnx pip package ke saath), score.py scoring file banao jisme init() aur run() functions hon, InferenceConfig banao, aur LocalWebservice se port 9000 par deploy karo:

from azureml.core.model import InferenceConfig, Model
from azureml.core.webservice import LocalWebservice
inference_config = InferenceConfig(entry_script="score.py", environment=myenv)
deployment_config = LocalWebservice.deploy_configuration(port=9000)
service = Model.deploy(ws, "roberta-base", [model], inference_config, deployment_config)
service.wait_for_deployment(True)

Deploy hone ke baad docker ps se container dikhta hai, aur container ke andar jaakar score.py aur model files verify ki ja sakti hain. Agar score.py me init() function me argument missing ho, to deployment turant errors deti hai — jaise "module 'main' has no attribute 'init'" aur "Did your init method fail?" — local debugging se aise issues Azure me try karne se pehle hi jaldi iterate karke fix kiye ja sakte hain.

Yaad rakho: Debugging me kabhi assume mat karo — reproduce karo, alag-alag environments me deploy karke try karo, aur locally debug karo. Aur Application Insights enable karna mat bhoolo — logs se zyada important hai poori system ki kahani samajhna.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — MLOps for Azure
← Previous08.2 · Compute, Deploying, Registering Models and Datasets→ Next09 · MLOps for GCP
09Chapter 9 · MLOps for GCP

MLOps for GCP

Is chapter me hum Google Cloud Platform (GCP) par MLOps karna seekhte hain — matlab apne machine learning models ko Google ke cloud par train karna, deploy karna aur chalana. GCP ki sabse badi taakat ye hai ki uski core technologies jaise Kubernetes aur TensorFlow kisi bhi cloud par chalti hain, isliye GCP ek multicloud strategy ke liye bahut accha hedge hai. Agar tum ek cloud vendor par zyada dependent nahi rehna chahte, to GCP ki open technologies tumhe flexibility deti hain, aur in technologies ko jaanne wale logon ko hire karna bhi relatively easy hai kyunki inki adoption bahut wide hai.

GCP ki chaar badi categories

Google Cloud ki services ko chaar clean categories me baanta ja sakta hai: Compute, Storage, Big Data aur Machine Learning. Compute me Compute Engine aata hai — Google ke infrastructure par virtual machines chalane ki service. Isme alag-alag machine types hain: Compute Intensive, Memory Intensive, Accelerator Optimized aur General Purpose. Ek MLOps practitioner ke liye ye samajhna bahut zaroori hai ki kaam ke hisaab se sahi machine chunni hai, kyunki cost asli duniya me matter karti hai. Deep learning ke liye Accelerator Optimized instances best hain kyunki wo NVIDIA GPUs ki massively parallel power use kar sakte hain, lekin agar tumhara training GPU ka fayda hi nahi utha sakta, to aisi costly machine lena pure waste hai.

Preemptible VMs ek aur smart option hain — ye 24 ghante tak available rehti hain, batch jobs ke liye perfect hain, aur cost me 80% tak bacha sakti hain. Matlab agar tum batch ML training ko preemptible VMs ke around design kar lo, to company ka kharcha bahut kam ho jata hai. Storage ki taraf Cloud Storage hai — unlimited storage, worldwide access, low latency, geo-redundancy aur high durability. MLOps workflows me yehi data lake banta hai, jahan unstructured aur structured data rehta hai batch training ke liye.

BigQuery aur Vertex AI — GCP ke crown jewels

Big Data tools me sabse popular hai Google BigQuery — isme SQL interface hai, serverless paradigm hai, aur sabse khaas baat ye hai ki tum BigQuery ke andar hi machine learning kar sakte ho. BigQuery ek bahut acchi starting point hai kyunki tum poori MLOps value chain ko isi ek tool se solve kar sakte ho. Machine learning aur AI capabilities Vertex AI naam ke product me coordinate hoti hain. Google ka approach shuru se hi MLOps solution banne ka hai — Vertex AI ka workflow ek structured approach deta hai: dataset creation aur storage, model training, model ko Vertex AI me store karna, endpoint par deploy karke prediction lena, prediction requests test karna, endpoints ke liye traffic splitting, aur models aur endpoints ka lifecycle manage karna. In saat components ke center me data aur model management hai — jo MLOps ka central element hai.

Light vs heavy MLOps workflow

Chapter me do approaches bataye gaye hain: light aur heavy. Light workflow me tum App Engine, Cloud Build, Cloud Functions aur prediction service jaise standalone components ko chun-chun kar use karte ho — ye ek-do ghante me poora MLOps pipeline set up kar deta hai. Heavy workflow me tum poori Vertex AI platform use karte ho, jisme Feature Store, Explainable AI aur model quality tracking jaise advanced features milte hain. Badi company ya bade project ke liye heavy approach sahi hai, lekin chhote project ya portfolio project ke liye light approach kaafi hai. Dono ka idea ek hi hai: khud se sab kuch behtar banana ki koshish mat karo — comparative advantage samjho, jo cheez trivial cost par khareedi ja sakti hai usko khud se worse version me mat banao.

Final project ka idea

Chapter ke end me ek final ML project ka suggestion hai: ek cloud native ML application banao GCP par. Uski requirements hain — source code GitHub me, continuous deployment CircleCI se, data GCP me (BigQuery, Cloud Storage), ML predictions serve karna (AutoML, BigQuery ya AI Platform se), cloud native monitoring, Google App Engine se REST API ke through JSON payload, aur deployment Google Cloud Build se. Checklist me ye sawal bhi hain: kya app ML inference karta hai, kya alag environments hain, kya comprehensive monitoring aur alerts hain, kya sahi datastore use hua hai, kya least privilege security apply hoti hai, aur kya data transit me encrypted hai. Ye project tumhare portfolio me tumhari ML engineering ability ka proof ban sakta hai.

Yaad rakho: GCP par MLOps ka matlab sirf GPUs khareedna nahi hai — sahi machine type chunna, preemptible VMs se cost bachana, BigQuery se ML karna aur Vertex AI se poora lifecycle manage karna hi asli MLOps hai. Light workflow se shuru karo, heavy features tab lo jab project ko unki zaroorat ho.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 9 — MLOps for GCP
← Previous08.3 · Azure ML Pipelines, Designer and Troubleshooting→ Next09.1 · Google Cloud Platform Overview and CI/CD
09.1Chapter 9 · MLOps for GCP

Google Cloud Platform Overview and CI/CD

GCP ko samajhne ke liye pehle uske core building blocks ko jaan lo. Compute Engine virtual machines deta hai, Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Kubernetes ka managed support deta hai — kyunki Kubernetes ko Google ne hi banaya hai, isliye GKE ka support excellent hai — aur Cloud Run containers ko simple tareeke se deploy karne ka high-level tareeka hai. App Engine ek fully managed PaaS hai jisme tum Node.js, Java, Ruby, C#, Go, Python ya PHP me code likh sakte ho, aur Cloud Functions ek FaaS (functions as a service) hai jo event-driven architecture ke liye perfect hai, jaise kisi event par batch training trigger karna ya prediction dena.

Compute Engine ke machine types

Compute Engine me chaar main machine families hain: Compute Intensive, Memory Intensive, Accelerator Optimized aur General Purpose. Iske alawa preemptible VMs hain jo 24 ghante tak chalti hain aur batch jobs ke liye 80% tak cost bacha sakti hain. MLOps me cost forecasting ek aisi skill hai jo company ko bana ya bigaad sakti hai — isliye har training job se pehle ye socho ki GPU chahiye ya nahi, memory zyada chahiye ya compute zyada. Galat machine chunna seedha-seedha paise ki barbadi hai, aur sahi machine chunna ek professional MLOps engineer ki pehchan hai.

CI/CD — MLOps ki nonoptional foundation

Continuous integration aur continuous delivery MLOps ka sabse important lekin sabse zyada neglected area hai. Testing DevOps aur MLOps dono ka fundamental component hai. GCP par CI ke do main options hain: GitHub Actions jaisa SaaS offering, ya cloud native solution Cloud Build. Cloud Build ka config cloudbuild.yaml me likha jata hai — usme steps hote hain jaise dependencies install karna, pylint se lint karna, aur phir gcloud app deploy se App Engine par deploy karna. Google Cloud Build testing aur linting me thoda clunky hai, lekin App Engine jaisi services ko deploy karna usse bahut easy ho jata hai.

steps:
- name: python:3.7
  id: INSTALL
  entrypoint: python3
  args: ['-m', 'pip', 'install', '-t', '.', '-r', 'requirements.txt']
- name: python:3.7
  entrypoint: ./pylint_runner
  id: LINT
  waitFor:
  - INSTALL
- name: "gcr.io/cloud-builders/gcloud"
  args: ["app", "deploy"]
  timeout: "1600s"

GitHub Actions vs Cloud Build — dono ko saath use karo

GitHub Actions ka config pythonpublish.yml me likha jata hai — push par trigger hota hai, Python 3.8 set up karta hai, make install se dependencies install karta hai, phir pylint se lint, pytest se test aur phir format karta hai. Dono approaches me ek critical difference hai: GitHub developer experience par focus karta hai, jabki GCP cloud experience par. Isliye best strategy ye hai ki GitHub Actions ko developer feedback ke liye use karo — linting aur testing — aur Google Cloud Build ko deployment ke liye use karo. Dono ko saath use karna hi smart approach hai, ek ko dusre se replace karne ki koshish mat karo.

name: Python application test with GitHub Actions
on: [push]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v2
    - name: Set up Python 3.8
      uses: actions/setup-python@v1
      with:
        python-version: 3.8
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        make install
    - name: Lint with pylint
      run: |
        make lint
    - name: Test with pytest
      run: |
        make test

Cloud Shell editor aur workflow

Google Cloud ke saath kaam karne ka recommended tareeka hai built-in editor ko terminal ke saath use karna, jisme Python virtual environment activated ho. Isse tum cloud me hi code likh sakte ho, test kar sakte ho aur deploy kar sakte ho — local machine par heavy setup ki zaroorat nahi. Ek starter project scaffold bhi available hai jo Makefile, linting aur testing ke saath aata hai, jise tum apne projects ke liye base bana sakte ho. CI/CD ko project ke shuru se hi lagana chahiye, baad me add karna hamesha mushkil hota hai.

  • Compute Engine: VMs — sahi machine type chuno, cost bachao, preemptible VMs batch jobs ke liye.
  • GKE aur Cloud Run: GKE Kubernetes ka managed version, Cloud Run containers ka simple tareeka.
  • App Engine: fully managed PaaS, Cloud Build se automated continuous delivery pipeline ka API endpoint.
  • Cloud Functions: event-driven FaaS — event par training trigger karo ya prediction do.
  • Cloud Build: deployment ke liye best; GitHub Actions linting/testing aur developer feedback ke liye best.
Yaad rakho: CI system ke bina MLOps adhura hai. GitHub Actions se lint aur test karo, Cloud Build se deploy karo — ye combination tumhe developer experience aur cloud deployment dono ka best deta hai. Testing ko kabhi optional mat samjho.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 9 — MLOps for GCP
← Previous09 · MLOps for GCP→ Next09.2 · Kubernetes Hello World
09.2Chapter 9 · MLOps for GCP

Kubernetes Hello World

Kubernetes ko ek tareeke se "mini-cloud" ya "cloud-in-a-box" samjho — ye tumhe near-infinite application complexity banane ki power deta hai. MLOps ke liye Kubernetes ideal hai kyunki isme high-availability architecture, autoscaling, rich ecosystem, service discovery, container health management, secrets aur configuration management milta hai, aur uske upar Kubeflow hai — Kubernetes ke liye end-to-end ML platform. TensorFlow se lekar scikit-learn tak ke ML frameworks Kubernetes ke core architecture ke upar coordinate karte hain, aur Kubernetes kisi bhi cloud par ya tumhare apne data center me chal sakta hai.

Kubernetes architecture — cluster, pod, node

Kubernetes ke core operations paanch hain: cluster banana, application ko cluster me deploy karna, application ke ports expose karna, application ko scale karna, aur application ko update karna. Hierarchy me ek control node hota hai jo baaki nodes ko manage karta hai, aur har node ke andar ek ya zyada containers hote hain jo pod ke andar rehte hain. Cluster set up karne ke do main tareeke hain: local cluster (preferably Docker Desktop se) ya cloud cluster — Amazon EKS, Google GKE, ya Azure AKS se. Local cluster se shuru karna learning ke liye best hai, production ke liye managed service lo.

Horizontal Pod Autoscaler — Kubernetes ka killer feature

Kubernetes ki sabse zabardast feature hai autoscaling via Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA). HPA automatically pods ki number ko scale karta hai — replication controller, deployment ya replica set me — CPU utilization, memory ya Kubernetes Metrics Server me defined custom metrics ke basis par. Ye ek control loop se kaam karta hai: metrics monitor karo, aur metrics ke hisaab se action lo. Matlab traffic badhe to pods badh jayenge, traffic kam ho to pods kam ho jayenge — tumhe manually kuch nahi karna padta. ML APIs ke liye ye bahut important hai kyunki prediction traffic kabhi bhi spike kar sakta hai.

Hello World example — Flask app ko Kubernetes par chalana

Chapter me ek simple Flask app ka example hai jo correct change return karta hai, aur use Kubernetes me convert kiya gaya hai. Repository me chaar assets hain: Makefile (project build karta hai), Dockerfile (container configuration), app.py (Flask app) aur kube-hello-change.yaml (Kubernetes YAML config). Shuruat me virtual environment banao, phir make all chalao — ye libraries install karta hai, project ko lint karta hai aur tests chalata hai. Certified containers ka use karo — official Python base image jaise, FROM statement se load hota hai — kyunki official teams ke containers trusted aur maintained hote hain.

python3 -m venv ~/.kube-hello && source ~/.kube-hello/bin/activate
docker build -t flask-change:latest .
docker run -p 8080:8080 flask-change
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/change/1/34

Docker container ko verify karne ke liye docker image ls chalao, aur alag terminal me curl se web service invoke karo — output me quarters, nickels aur pennies ka JSON milega, jaise 1 dollar 34 cents ke liye 5 quarters, 1 nickel aur 4 pennies. Container ko Ctrl+C se roko. Phir Kubernetes locally chalao: pehle kubectl get nodes se verify karo ki docker-desktop context kaam kar raha hai, phir kubectl apply -f kube-hello-change.yaml se load-balanced service aur deployment set up karo.

Deployment YAML aur verification

YAML config me ek Service hai jiska type LoadBalancer hai, port 8080, aur ek Deployment hai jisme replicas: 3 hain — matlab Flask app ke teen copies chalenge. Image flask-change:latest hai aur imagePullPolicy Never hai kyunki image local hai. Verify karne ke liye kubectl get pods chalao — teenon pods Running status me dikhne chahiye. Phir kubectl describe services se load balancer ki details dekho, aur make invoke se endpoint ko curl karo — wahi change wala JSON output milega. Cleanup ke liye kubectl delete deployment hello-python chalao.

kubectl get nodes
kubectl apply -f kube-hello-change.yaml
kubectl get pods
kubectl describe services hello-python-service
kubectl delete deployment hello-python

Is basic tutorial ke baad next step hai GKE, Google Cloud Run ya Vertex AI use karke ML endpoint deploy karna. Kubernetes ML-powered APIs banane ki excellent foundation hai, aur agar tum shuru se Docker format containers use karte ho, to GCP par tumhare paas bahut saare options khul jate hain.

  • Pods: ek ya zyada containers ka group; HPA inki number ko CPU/memory/custom metrics par scale karta hai.
  • Service: LoadBalancer type se app ka port bahar expose hota hai.
  • Deployment: replicas batata hai — kitne copies chalenge, jaise 3.
  • Kubeflow: Kubernetes ke upar end-to-end ML platform.
  • GKE: Google ka managed Kubernetes — Kubernetes Google ne banaya, isliye support best hai.
Yaad rakho: Pehle Docker me app ko locally chalana seekho, phir use hi Kubernetes YAML se deploy karo — Service + Deployment + replicas ka pattern har ML API ke liye same rehta hai. HPA lagana mat bhoolo, warna traffic spike par tumhara model down ho jayega.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 9 — MLOps for GCP
← Previous09.1 · Google Cloud Platform Overview and CI/CD→ Next09.3 · Cloud Native Database, DataOps and Operationalizing Models
09.3Chapter 9 · MLOps for GCP

Cloud Native Database, DataOps and Operationalizing Models

Compute ke baad GCP ki sabse badi taakat uska cloud native database hai — Google BigQuery. BigQuery ko start karna bahut easy hai, uske paas publicly available datasets ki badi list hai, aur MLOps ke nazariye se uski killer feature ye hai ki tum BigQuery platform ke andar hi ML models ko train aur host kar sakte ho. BigQuery ek MLOps pipeline ka center ban sakta hai jo business intelligence aur ML engineering dono ko export karta hai, aur DataOps inputs jaise public datasets, streaming API aur Google Dataflow se feed hota hai. BigQuery me inline ML karne se bade datasets ka processing streamline ho jata hai.

BigQuery MLOps workflow

Workflow aisa hai: DataOps inputs (public datasets, streaming API, Dataflow) BigQuery me aate hain, BigQuery me ML modeling hoti hai, aur results export hote hain — jaise K-means clustering analysis ko Google Data Studio me shareable report ke roop me dikhana. BigQuery se shuru karna GCP par MLOps ke liye optimal choice hai kyunki platform bahut flexible hai. Data ML at scale banane ke liye necessary input hai, isliye DataOps MLOps ka critical aspect hai — data flow ko automate karna hi DataOps hai.

DataOps with Cloud Functions — serverless data engineering

GCP par data flow automate karne ke unlimited tareeke hain, lekin simplicity ke liye chapter me serverless approach use kiya gaya hai — Cloud Functions. Ek simple Cloud Function correct change return karti hai: Google Cloud Console me naya Cloud Function banao, code paste karo, aur "Require authentication" ko "Allow unauthenticated invocations" par set kar sakte ho testing ke liye. Function ko gcloud se invoke karo ya curl se JSON payload bhej kar invoke karo. Yehi pattern ML ke liye bhi kaam karta hai — Cloud Function ek AI API call kar sakti hai ya Pub/Sub se baat karke MLOps pipeline ka hissa ban sakti hai.

gcloud functions call changemachine --data '{"amount":"1.34"}'
curl -d '{"amount":"1.34"}' -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST <trigger>/function-3

Ek aur approach hai endpoint invoke karne ke liye ek command line tool banana — Click aur requests se, jo host ko query karta hai aur result print karta hai. Prototyping ke liye serverless se tez koi tareeka nahi hai — pehle serverless se initial data engineering workflow solve karo, aur complex tools par tab jao jab zaroorat pade. Yehi pragmatic approach MLOps me kaam aata hai: simple se shuru karo, complexity tabhi add karo jab wo justified ho.

Translate API example — ML API ko function se jodna

Ek aur example me Cloud Function Wikipedia se summary lekar Google Translate API se translate karti hai. Iske liye requirements.txt me wikipedia aur google-cloud-translate jaisi libraries add karni padti hain, aur main.py me translate_test function likhni padti hai jo JSON payload se entity, language aur sentences leti hai, Wikipedia summary nikalti hai aur use target language me translate karti hai. Invoke karne ke liye gcloud functions call translate-wikipedia --data '{"entity":"facebook", "sentences": "20", "language":"ru"}' chalao — output me Russian translation milega. Isse ye samajh aata hai ki Cloud Function kisi bhi existing ML/AI API ko wrap karke ek deployable service bana sakta hai.

gcloud functions call translate-wikipedia --data '{"entity":"facebook", "sentences": "20", "language":"ru"}'
gcloud ai-platform local predict --model-dir LOCAL_OR_CLOUD_STORAGE_PATH_TO_MODEL_DIRECTORY/ --json-instances LOCAL_PATH_TO_PREDICTION_INPUT.JSON --framework NAME_OF_FRAMEWORK

Operationalizing models — Vertex AI aur prediction service

GCP par MLOps platform Vertex AI hai — isme AutoML technology bhi integrated hai. Uske essential components hain Feature Store, Explainable AI aur model quality tracking. Badi company me MLOps project shuru karne ki pehli jagah Vertex AI hi honi chahiye — jaise AWS par SageMaker aur Azure par Azure ML Studio. Dusra option hai standalone components use karna: prediction service se models deploy karo aur requests accept karo, phir us endpoint ko Cloud Functions, Cloud Run ya App Engine se call karo. Local sklearn model ko gcloud ai-platform local predict se test kar sakte ho, phir endpoint banao.

Light workflow ka example hai Google App Engine project: cloudbuild.yml me sirf ek deploy command hoti hai, aur app.yaml, requirements.txt aur main.py se kaam ho jata hai. Cloud Build API enable karo, phir deploy karo — poora MLOps pipeline ek-do ghante me set up ho jata hai. Final step me application ko ML karne ke liye ya to kisi ML/AI API ko call karo ya AI Platform endpoint hosting use karo. Light approach easy hai, heavy approach (Vertex AI) me Explainable AI jaise advanced features milte hain jo enterprises ko chahiye hote hain.

  • BigQuery: SQL interface, serverless, platform ke andar ML training aur hosting, public datasets.
  • Dataflow aur Pub/Sub: DataOps inputs — streaming aur batch data flow automate karte hain.
  • Cloud Functions: serverless data engineering aur ML API wrapping ke liye sabse tez prototyping tool.
  • Vertex AI: Feature Store, Explainable AI, model quality tracking — bade projects ke liye poora MLOps platform.
  • Prediction service: standalone deployment option — model deploy karo, endpoint se requests lo.
Yaad rakho: DataOps ke bina MLOps nahi hota — data flow pehle automate karo, phir model ko operationalize karo. Serverless se prototype banao, aur jab project bada ho jaye to Vertex AI ke Feature Store aur Explainable AI jaise heavy features par move karo. Khud se platform banana mat — jo platform de raha hai use lo.

10Chapter 10 · Machine Learning Interoperability

Machine Learning Interoperability

Trained ML models bhi alag-alag constraints ke saath aate hain — zyada tar models us environment me kaam hi nahi karte jo unke liye specially tailored nahi hai. Model interoperability ka main concept ye hai ki ek model ko ek platform se dusre platform par transform kar sako, jisse tumhe choices milti hain. Ye chapter kehta hai ki cloud provider ke out-of-the-box models use karna aur vendor lock-in ki chinta na karna bhi ek valid argument hai, lekin models ko dusre formats me export karna seekhna essential hai taaki wo dusre platforms par bhi chal saken jahan constraints alag hain. Jaise containers kisi bhi system par chal jate hain bas ek container runtime chahiye, waise hi model ko alag formats me export karna flexibility aur empowerment deta hai.

Aalu wali kahani — variety me hi power hai

Chapter ki shuruat ek interesting example se hoti hai: Peru me aalu ki kayi hazaar varieties hoti hain, aur har dish ke liye alag variety chahiye hoti hai. Common baking potato se har dish ka taste same nahi aata. Variety aur pick-and-choose karne ki ability me empowerment hai — aur yehi baat machine learning me bhi sach hai. Train ek baar karo apne pasandeeda framework me, phir model ko transform karke use lagbhag kahin bhi deploy karo — edge devices se lekar mobile phones aur dusre operating systems tak. Ye screws wali analogy jaisa hai: aise screws banao jo kisi bhi screwdriver se khul jayen, na ki sirf ek hi store ke screwdriver se.

Interoperability kyun critical hai — ek real Azure kahani

Ek real example me Azure AutoML par train kiye gaye model ko locally inference ke liye chalana tha, aur bahut problems aayi: no-code deployment me scoring script kahin nahi mili, model ka suffix pickle module ki taraf ishara karta tha lekin load karke inference nahi ho rahi thi, dependencies ka pata nahi tha, Azure SDK sirf Python 3.7 support karta tha jabki system par 3.8 tha, ek library ka version guess karna pada (2019 wala 0.90), aur model train hone ke time ka latest SDK version use karna pada — ye sab advertise hi nahi kiya gaya tha. Ye Azure ki burai nahi hai — platform excellent hai — lekin low-code ya no-code speed ke liye accha hai, portability ke liye complicated ho sakta hai. Control ki granularity kho jati hai. Aisi hi problem tab hoti hai jab ek model AWS par accha perform karta hai lekin use edge TPU device par deploy karna ho jo bilkul incompatible hai — ya model 5 GB ka ho aur accelerator ki max storage se zyada ho.

Simple aur flexible ka tension

Software engineering me abstraction ek typical pattern hai, lekin kabhi-kabhi abstraction utna hi complex ho jata hai jitna underlying software tha. System design ka ek open question hai: system bahut simple aur opinionated ho, ya flexible aur complex? Sabko simple aur flexible chahiye hota hai, lekin aisa system banana bahut challenging hai. ML me alag platforms aur cloud providers models ko alag tareeke se train karte hain — agar tum usi platform ke andar rehte ho to koi problem nahi, lekin jaise hi model ko bahar le jana ho, frustration shuru ho jati hai. Interoperability is problem ko solve karti hai — constraints ko openly describe karke, models ko ek format se dusre me transform karna easy bana kar, aur saare prominent cloud providers ka support lekar.

ONNX — train once, run anywhere

Is chapter ka hero hai ONNX (Open Neural Network Exchange) — 2017 me Facebook aur Microsoft ne jointly present kiya tha, ek open ecosystem ke roop me AI model interoperability ke liye. Aaj ye ek bada open source project hai jisme SIGs aur working groups hain. ONNX ka idea hai: apne pasandeeda framework me train karo, ek baar ONNX me transform karo, aur phir kahin bhi deploy karo — cloud se edge tak, alag operating systems par bhi. Hardware vendors bhi ONNX ko target kar sakte hain aur ek saath multiple frameworks ko impact kar sakte hain — optimizations ko har framework me alag se integrate nahi karna padta. Azure to apne ML SDK me ONNX models ke liye native support bhi deta hai.

  • Vendor lock-in se bachao: model ek platform ka bandi nahi rehta, use kahin bhi le ja sakte ho.
  • Edge deployment: edge devices aur mobile phones par models chalane ke liye conversion zaroori hai.
  • Framework choice: jis framework ki features pasand hain usme train karo, phir ONNX me convert karo.
  • Provenance: model ka source of truth hamesha pata hona chahiye — kahan se aaya, kis se bana.
Yaad rakho: Model train karna sirf aadha kaam hai — use dusre platform par chalana hi asli MLOps challenge hai. Interoperability ka matlab hai choices: ek format me band mat raho, ONNX jaise open standard se model ko kahin bhi le jane ki freedom rakho.
SOURCESource: Practical MLOps, O'Reilly, Chapter 10 — Machine Learning Interoperability
← Previous09.3 · Cloud Native Database, DataOps and Operationalizing Models→ Next10.1 · ONNX — Model Zoo, Conversion, Deployment
10.1Chapter 10 · Machine Learning Interoperability

ONNX — Model Zoo, Conversion, Deployment

ONNX ka full form hai Open Neural Network Exchange — ek open standard jo models ko ek framework se dusre framework ya platform par le jane deta hai. Iska sabse bada promise hai "train once, run anywhere": tum apne pasandeeda framework me train karo, ek baar ONNX me convert karo, aur phir us model ko cloud, edge devices, mobile phones aur alag operating systems par deploy karo. Conversions free nahi hote — kabhi naye features supported nahi hote kyunki ONNX converters hamesha catch-up kar rahe hote hain, aur kabhi purane models naye versions ke saath supported nahi hote — lekin commonality aur run-anywhere ka idea phir bhi solid hai.

ONNX Model Zoo — ready-to-use models ka registry

Model Zoo ONNX models ka ek informational repository hai GitHub par — isme community ke contribute kiye hue aur curated pretrained models ke links hain. Models teen categories me divided hain: vision, language aur everything else. Agar tum ONNX se shuru karna chahte ho aur inference try karna chahte ho, to Model Zoo hi wo jagah hai. Har model page par version aur size ki information ke saath-saath examples bhi hote hain ki model ke saath kaise interact karna hai — proof of concept jaldi banane ke liye ye crucial hai. Jaise RoBERTa-SequenceClassification model — ye PyTorch RoBERTa se aaya, phir ONNX me convert hua, aur phir Model Zoo me available hua. Yehi uski provenance hai, matlab source of truth.

Provenance kyun matter karta hai

Model ka origin jaanna isliye zaroori hai kyunki jab changes ya problems aayen, to tumhe confidently pinpoint karna hota hai ki kya modify karna hai. Ek real kahani me ek production repository corrupt ho gayi, aur ek package ko rebuild karte time pata chala ki wo ek developer ki home directory se download ho raha tha — wo developer company chhod chuka tha, aur wo server ka build system se koi lena-dena hi nahi tha. Aise situations common hain. Isliye jab tum Model Zoo jaise jagah se models lete ho, to jitni information capture kar sako karo — meaningful names use karo aur metadata bharo. "productionmodel-1" jaisa naam kuch nahi batata; meaningful naam aur metadata debugging ka time bahut kam kar dete hain aur onboarding easy bana dete hain.

PyTorch se ONNX — ResNet18 conversion

PyTorch me pretrained models easily milte hain, isliye learning jumpstart karne ka ye accha tareeka hai. ResNet18 ko ONNX me export karne ke liye pehle virtual environment banao aur requirements.txt me numpy, onnx, Pillow, protobuf, six, torch, torchvision aur typing-extensions ke pinned versions likho. Phir convert.py me dummy tensor banao, torchvision se pretrained resnet18 lo, input/output names define karo, aur torch.onnx.export se export karo. Isme opset_version argument critical hai — PyTorch ki tensor indexing me unsupported ONNX opset version se problems aati hain, kuch indexer types sirf version 12 support karte hain — hamesha double-check karo ki versions tumhare required features ko support karte hain.

import torch
import torchvision
dummy_tensor = torch.randn(8, 3, 200, 200)
model = torchvision.models.resnet18(pretrained=True)
input_names = ["input_%d" % i for i in range(12)]
output_names = ["output_1"]
torch.onnx.export(
    model, dummy_tensor, "resnet18.onnx",
    input_names=input_names, output_names=output_names,
    opset_version=7, verbose=True,
)

Ye example intentionally overly simplistic hai — exported model dummy values se bhara hai aur robust nahi hai — lekin ye prove karta hai ki PyTorch me export kitna straightforward hai, aur converter framework ka hissa hai to uske flawlessly kaam karne ki responsibility framework ki hai. Conversion ke baad model ko verify karo: check.py me onnx.load karo, onnx.checker.check_model se check karo, aur onnx.helper.printable_graph se graph print karo. Check se koi error nahi aana chahiye — lekin poori correctness ke liye inference ko evaluate karna hoga aur kisi bhi drift ko capture karna hoga.

Generic ONNX checker — chhota CLI tool

Isi checking pattern ko ek generic command line tool me badla ja sakta hai — onnx-checker.py. Pehle sirf main() function se help menu print karo, phir sys.argv se arguments handle karo: agar --help ho to help menu dikhao aur sys.exit(0) karo, warna last argument ko model ka path maan kar onnx.load karo aur check_model chalao. Isme koi input sanitation nahi hai — ye brittle script hai — lekin ye ek building brick hai jise CI/CD system ya cloud provider workflow me leverage kar sakte ho. Automation hamesha sabse simple problem se shuru karo.

import sys
import onnx
def main(arguments):
    if "--help" in arguments:
        print("A command line tool to quickly verify ONNX models")
        sys.exit(0)
    model = onnx.load(arguments[-1])
    onnx.checker.check_model(model)
    print(onnx.helper.printable_graph(model.graph))

TensorFlow se ONNX — tf2onnx

TensorFlow ke liye tensorflow-onnx project hai (tf2onnx) — isse TensorFlow 1 aur 2, tflite aur tf.keras models convert kar sakte ho, aur ONNX opset 7 se 13 tak support hai. Dhyaan rakho: tf2onnx install karne par tensorflow requirement ke roop me list nahi hota, isliye tensorflow 2.4.1 alag se install karna zaroori hai warna tool kaam nahi karega. Invocation thoda unconventional hai — Python executable ke saath -m flag use hota hai: python -m tf2onnx.convert --help. Saved model ke liye --saved-model flag, frozen graph ke liye --input, checkpoint ke liye --checkpoint use karo, aur --opset se version set karo.

pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m tf2onnx.convert --help
python -m tf2onnx.convert --opset 13 --saved-model /path/to/ssd --output ssd.onnx
python -m tf2onnx.convert --opset 13 --tflite ~/Downloads/mobilenet_v2_1.0_224_quant.tflite --output mobilenet_v2_1.0_224_quant.onnx

Chapter me errors aur tracebacks intentionally dikhaye gaye hain — jaise galat opset par "must be Const" error, ya quantized model par "Opset 10 is required for quantization" error jisme --dequantize flag ya --opset 10 suggest kiya gaya tha. Inse ye seekh milti hai ki model ke inputs, outputs aur internals ko samajhna conversion ke liye crucial hai, aur tf2onnx Support Status page se sahi version determine karna chahiye. Jo demo hamesha perfect dikhata hai us par shak karo — errors se hi asli understanding aati hai.

ONNX ko Azure par deploy karna

Azure ke Python SDK me ONNX ka direct support hai. Scoring file score.py me init() function model ko load karti hai — onnxruntime.InferenceSession se, AZUREML_MODEL_DIR environment variable se path lekar. Phir run() function input JSON ko tokenizer se encode karti hai, session.run se inference karti hai, aur np.argmax se result return karti hai. Environment ke liye CondaDependencies se environ.yml banao (numpy, onnxruntime, azureml-core, torch, transformers), InferenceConfig banao entry_script score.py ke saath, phir ACI (Azure Container Instance) config banao cpu_cores=1, memory_gb=1 ke saath, aur Model.deploy se deploy karo. Training ki details yahan cover nahi hain — koi bhi model train karo, ONNX me export karo, register karo, aur yahin se deployment continue karo.

  • Model Zoo: vision, language aur baaki categories — pretrained ONNX models try karne ki jagah.
  • opset_version: conversion me sabse critical argument — galat version par conversion fail hota hai.
  • check_model: conversion ke baad verification ka pehla step; poori correctness ke liye inference evaluate karo.
  • tf2onnx: TensorFlow, tflite aur tf.keras ke liye converter — tensorflow alag se install karna mat bhoolo.
  • Azure deploy: score.py (init + run), environ.yml, InferenceConfig, ACI config, Model.deploy.
Yaad rakho: Conversion ke time model ke inputs, outputs aur opset version ko achhi tarah samjho — bina iske conversion guesswork ban jata hai. Har conversion ke baad check_model chalao, meaningful naam aur metadata hamesha rakho, aur errors ko chhupao mat — unhi se tum conversion ki asli samajh banate ho.
Book ka poora code — official repo se (code cells/files only, outputs nahi):
onnx-checker.py — chapter10/onnx-checker.py
import sys
import onnx

def main(arguments):
    help_menu = """
    A command-line tool to quickly verify ONNX models using
    check_model()
    """

    if "--help" in arguments:
        print(help_menu)
        sys.exit(0)

    model = onnx.load(arguments[-1])
    onnx.checker.check_model(model)
    print(onnx.helper.printable_graph(model.graph))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main(sys.argv)

azure/scoring.py — chapter10/azure/scoring.py
import torch
import os
import numpy as np
from transformers import RobertaTokenizer
import onnxruntime


def init():
    global session
    model = os.path.join(
        os.getenv("AZUREML_MODEL_DIR"), "roberta-sequence-classification-9.onnx"
    )
    session = onnxruntime.InferenceSession(model)


def run(input_data_json):
    try:
        tokenizer = RobertaTokenizer.from_pretrained("roberta-base")
        input_ids = torch.tensor(
            tokenizer.encode(input_data_json[0], add_special_tokens=True)
        ).unsqueeze(0)

        if input_ids.requires_grad:
            numpy_func = input_ids.detach().cpu().numpy()
        else:
            numpy_func = input_ids.cpu().numpy()

        inputs = {session.get_inputs()[0].name: numpy_func(input_ids)}
        out = session.run(None, inputs)

        return {"result": np.argmax(out)}
    except Exception as err:
        result = str(err)
        return {"error": result}

10.2Chapter 10 · Machine Learning Interoperability

Apple Core ML and Edge Integration

Apple ka ML framework Core ML is mamle me unique hai ki isme Core ML models ko ONNX me convert karne ka bhi support hai aur ONNX se Core ML me convert karne ka bhi. Lekin careful rehna zaroori hai — conversion ka support aur versions sahi hone chahiye, warna breakage ho jata hai. Aaj coremltools ONNX opset version 10 aur usse naye ko support karta hai, aur target environment ko bhi dhyaan me rakhna hota hai — kaunsa iOS ya macOS release supported hai. Is section me hum ONNX model ko Core ML me convert karenge, aur phir edge devices ke liye ORT format dekhenge.

ONNX se Core ML — MNIST conversion

Model Zoo se MNIST model download karo (example me version 1.3), phir naya virtual environment banao aur requirements.txt me coremltools 4.1, onnx 1.8.1, numpy, scipy aur baaki pinned libraries likho. Phir ek simple converter script banao — bilkul ONNX checker jaisi, bina argument parser ya fancy help menu ke, lekin hamesha help menu include karna chahiye taaki dusre log samajh saken ki script ke inputs aur outputs kya hain. Script last argument ko ONNX model ka path maanti hai, basename nikalti hai, convert() chalati hai minimum_ios_deployment_target='13' ke saath, short description add karti hai, aur .mlmodel file save karti hai.

import sys
from coremltools.converters.onnx import convert
def main(arguments):
    model_path = arguments[-1]
    basename = model_path.split('.onnx')[0]
    model = convert(model_path, minimum_ios_deployment_target='13')
    model.short_description = "ONNX Model converted with coremltools"
    model.save(f"{basename}.mlmodel")

Script chalane par output me 11 nodes ka conversion dikhta hai — Conv, Add, Relu, MaxPool, Reshape, MatMul — phir "Translation to CoreML spec completed" aur "Model Compilation done" aata hai. Result ek mnist-8.mlmodel file hoti hai jise macOS computer par Xcode ke saath load kar sakte ho — Finder me double-click karo aur model turant load ho jata hai, description ke saath. Availability section me minimum iOS target 13 dikhna chahiye, Predictions section me inputs aur outputs ki useful information hoti hai, aur Utilities section me CloudKit ke saath integrate hone wala model archive deploy karne ke helpers milte hain.

Core ML kyun compelling hai

Ye process ONNX use karne ki compelling wajah dikhata hai: tum apne well-established frameworks use kar sakte ho jinke tum aadi ho, phir conversion karke targeted iOS environment me deploy kar sakte ho. Tumhe iOS development ke liye apna pura workflow badalne ki zaroorat nahi — train wahi karo jahan tum comfortable ho, deploy wahan karo jahan users hain. Lekin hamesha tested models ki list check karo — Model Zoo aur Core ML docs me bataya gaya hai ki kaunse models achhi tarah kaam karte hain — aur minimum target support ko verify karo.

Edge integration — ORT format

Edge devices ke liye ONNX ne ek naya internal model format announce kiya hai — ORT format — jo model ka build size minimize karta hai taaki embedded ya edge devices par optimal deployment ho sake. Edge devices ki storage limited hoti hai aur aksar slow bhi hoti hai; chhota footprint padhna aur likhna dono easy bana deta hai. ORT me convert karne ke liye onnxruntime repository ko clone karna padta hai — abhi ke liye koi separate tooling install karne ko available nahi hai — aur tools/python directory me convert_onnx_models_to_ort.py script use hoti hai.

git clone https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime.git
python onnxruntime/tools/python/convert_onnx_models_to_ort.py --help
python onnxruntime/tools/python/convert_onnx_models_to_ort.py models/mobilenetv2-7.onnx

Converter ONNX model ko ORT model me convert karta hai aur ek configuration file bhi banata hai — required_operators.config — jisme model ke liye required operators ki list hoti hai. Jaise mobilenet model ke liye config me ai.onnx;1;Conv,GlobalAveragePool, ai.onnx;5;Reshape, ai.onnx;7;Add aur com.microsoft;1;FusedConv hote hain. Ye config crucial hai kyunki isse tum sirf unhi operators ke saath ek unique ONNX runtime build kar sakte ho — binary size reduction ho jata hai. Runtime build karte time --include_ops_by_config flag se config ka path do, --minimal_build se sirf ORT models load karne wala build banao (normal ONNX format ka support drop karke), aur Android target ke liye --android_cpp_shared flag se shared libc++ use karke aur chhota binary banao.

Edge ka bada picture

ONNX alag-alag hardware configurations — varying CPUs aur GPUs — ko support karne ki koshish karta rehta hai; ye easy problem nahi hai, lekin welcomed effort hai. Support jitna broad hoga, ML models ko un environments me deploy karna utna easy hoga jahan pehle possible hi nahi tha — khaas karke remote environments jahan internet ya network connectivity hi nahi hai. ONNX deployment ka friction kam kar raha hai, aur collective knowledge aur contributions se tooling aur support aur behtar hota rahega.

  • coremltools: ONNX opset 10+ support karta hai; minimum iOS deployment target hamesha set karo.
  • .mlmodel: Xcode me double-click karke load karo — Availability, Predictions aur Utilities sections check karo.
  • ORT format: edge ke liye chhota footprint — model ke saath required_operators.config banta hai.
  • Minimal build: sirf required operators ke saath runtime build karo taaki binary size kam ho.
Yaad rakho: Edge par har MB matter karta hai — model ko ORT me convert karo aur sirf required operators wala minimal runtime build karo. Aur iOS par deploy karte time target version ko kabhi assume mat karo — docs me minimum supported target hamesha verify karo.
Book ka poora code — official repo se (code cells/files only, outputs nahi):
coreml/cli.py — chapter10/coreml/cli.py
import sys
from coremltools.converters.onnx import convert

def main(model_path):
    basename = model_path.split('.onnx')[0]
    model = convert(model_path,  minimum_ios_deployment_target='13')
    model.short_description = "ONNX Model converted with coremltools"
    model.save(f"{basename}.mlmodel")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main(sys.argv[-1])

11Chapter 11 · Building MLOps Command Line Tools and Microservices

Building MLOps Command Line Tools and Microservices

Command line tools banana Python seekhne ka perfect intersection hai software development aur machine learning ke beech. Ek Systems Administrator ke roop me Bash scripting se shuru kar ke Python tak ka safar batata hai ki shell scripting me error handling, logging aur debugging mushkil hai, jabki Python, Go ya Rust jaisi languages me ye features easily milte hain. Rule simple hai: agar kaam kuch lines me ho jaye to shell script theek hai — jaise SSH key copy karne wala chhota function — lekin jab solution ek dozen lines se zyada ho jaye, to shell se aage badho aur ek proper language use karo.

Seekhne ka sahi tareeka — apni problem solve karo

Python seekhne ka best tareeka hai tedious, repetitive tasks ko automate karna — client websites banana, servers se users add ya remove karna, aise kaam jo tumhe direct benefit dein. School wali learning se ye bilkul alag hai: ek interesting problem dhoondho jiska direct fayda tumhe ho, aur use solve karte-karte language seekho. Command line tools iske liye perfect hain kyunki wo install karne me straightforward hote hain — bilkul containers aur microservices ki tarah, jo dependencies ko bundle karke kisi bhi system par chal jate hain jahan proper runtime ho.

Microservices — monolith ka ulta

Microservices ek naya application paradigm hai, purane monolithic applications ke bilkul opposite. ML operations ke liye responsibilities ko isolate karna critical hai — taaki components reusable ban saken, sirf ek model ke ek process se tied na rahen. Ise Jenga puzzle jaisa samjho: monolithic application ek bahut uncha Jenga tower hai — bahut saare pieces mil kar use khada karte hain, lekin ek piece chhedo to poora gir jata hai. Dusri taraf, agar pieces robustly jode gaye hain, to unhe nikal kar dusri jagah repurpose karna straightforward hai. Isi liye utility modules banao — common utilities ek jagah rakho taaki application ke dusre hisse unhe import karke reuse kar saken.

Serverless — microservices ka sabse easy roop

Serverless technologies — jaise Lambda aur Cloud Functions — microservices banane ka excellent solution hain: ek file me code likho aur instantly cloud par deploy karo, underlying operating system ya dependencies ki chinta kiye bina. Runtime drop-down se select karo, jaise Python 3.8, aur button click karo. Isse tum poori HTTP APIs ya pipeline-like workflows bana sakte ho. Serverless ka ek aur fayda hai ki tum cloud provider ki offerings ko bina zyada effort ke access kar sakte ho — computer vision chahiye? Ek dozen lines se kam me serverless deployment kar lo. Speed, robustness aur reproducibility — ye teeno DevOps ke significant components hain.

Khud mat banao jo khareed sakte ho

Ek purani kahani yaad rakho: ek digital media agency me ek dozen IT logon ki team ne apne email servers in-house chalane ka faisla kiya — email sahi tareeke se chalana bahut knowledge aur ongoing effort mangta hai, aur email lagbhag har mahine band ho jata tha. Tumhari company ki core competency kya hai? Agar wo state-of-the-art computer vision models banana nahi hai, to unhe khud mat banao. High-level systems jaise AWS App Runner ya Google Cloud Run par build karo, aur reinvent karne ki urge ko resist karo. Cloud ML microservices ke options IaaS se PaaS tak range karte hain — Kubernetes lower-level aur complex hai, App Runner me GitHub repo point karo aur kuch clicks me fully deployed continuous delivery platform mil jata hai, aur beech me Cloud Functions hain.

  • Shell vs Python: kuch lines ka kaam ho to Bash, usse zyada ho to Python/Go/Rust.
  • Automation: repetitive task dikhe to uska CLI tool banao — ye DevOps ka core principle hai.
  • Microservices: responsibilities isolate karo taaki components reusable banen.
  • Serverless: code par focus karo, OS aur dependencies par nahi — ML APIs minutes me deploy karo.
  • Core competency: jo tumhara kaam nahi hai use cloud se lo — email server khud chalane ki galti mat karo.
Yaad rakho: CLI tools aur microservices ka mix-and-match hi MLOps superpower hai — HTTP, command line tools aur cloud offerings ke SDKs ko jod kar tum tricky problems ke creative solutions bahut kam code me bana sakte ho. Pehle apni repetitive problem dhoondho, phir uska tool banao.

11.1Chapter 11 · Building MLOps Command Line Tools and Microservices

Python Packaging and the Requirements File

Bahut se useful Python command line tools ek single script file se shuru hote hain, phir dheere-dheere complex ho jate hain — aur files, aur dependencies. Jab tak script ko extra libraries ki zaroorat nahi hai, single script bina packaging ke theek hai. Lekin jaise hi tumhara script kisi dependency par depend karne lage ya ek se zyada files ka ho jaye, to packaging consider karna hi chahiye. Properly packaged Python application ko Python Package Index (PyPI) par publish bhi kar sakte ho, taaki dusre log use pip se install kar saken. Python packaging perfect nahi hai — ek decade se zyada experience ke baad bhi ye ecosystem ka tricky hissa hai — lekin isse bachna nahi, seekhna hai.

Virtual environments — pehle ye seekho

Pehle ke time me Python packages install karne ke baad unhe remove karna impossible tha — isiliye virtual environments popular hue. Virtual environment me dependencies fix karna ek directory delete karne jitna easy tha, aur system packages intact rehte the. Aaj uninstall karna possible hai, lekin dependency resolution abhi bhi robust nahi hai — isliye virtual environments hi suggested tareeka hain. Python 3 se virtual environment banane ka common tareeka hai python -m venv, aur activate karne ke baad which python se verify karo ki Python executable system wale se alag hai — virtual environment ke andar ka hai.

python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
which python

Jaise hi tumhara command line tool kisi dependency ko need kare, wo requirement ke roop me declare karne ke liye ready hona chahiye — tumhare tool ke consumers bhi un dependencies ko resolve kar payenge, aur dusron ke liye tumhare tool ke saath kaam karna easy ho jayega.

requirements.txt — dependencies declare karne ka tareeka

Dependencies define karne ke do popular tareeke hain — ek hai requirements.txt file. Is file me har dependency alag line par likhi jati hai, optionally version constraint ke saath. Example me Click framework ka koi constraint nahi hai — pip latest version use karega — aur Pytest ek specific version par pinned hai, to pip hamesha wahi specific version dhoondhega. Install karne ke liye pip install -r requirements.txt chalao. Kai projects alag-alag requirements files rakhte hain — jaise development dependencies production se alag hon — ye common practice hai.

# requirements.txt
click
pytest==5.1.0
pip install -r requirements.txt

setup.py vs requirements.txt — confusion mat karo

Dusra tareeka hai setup.py file — ye dependencies install bhi kar sakti hai, lekin sirf setup.py hi Python project ko distribution ke liye package kar sakti hai. Ye Python packaging ki unfortunate side-effect hai ki dono files dependencies install kar sakti hain. Ek important baat: setup.py install time par Python se execute hoti hai, isliye wo installation ke alawa kuch bhi kar sakti hai — lekin recommend nahi kiya jata ki setup.py ko packaging ke alawa kisi aur kaam ke liye extend karo, warna distribution me issues aayenge. Kai projects requirements.txt me dependencies define karte hain aur phir usi file ko setup.py me read karke reuse karte hain.

with open("requirements.txt", "r") as _f:
    dependencies = _f.readlines()

Ye distinction samajhna useful hai taaki confusion aur misuse na ho: agar project distribution ke liye hai to setup.py chahiye, aur agar wo ek service ya project hai jise install karne ki zaroorat nahi hai, to requirements.txt kaafi hai. Packaging seekhna mushkil lag sakta hai, lekin shuru karna itna hard nahi hai — aur proper packaging karke tum kisi bhi team me invaluable ban jate ho.

  • Single script: no external dependencies ho to packaging ki zaroorat nahi.
  • Virtual environment: hamesha use karo — dependencies isolate rehti hain, problems solve karna easy hota hai.
  • requirements.txt: dependencies list karo, version pin karo jahan zaroori ho.
  • setup.py: distribution ke liye — PyPI par publish karne ke liye zaroori; sirf packaging ke liye use karo.
Yaad rakho: Virtual environment ke bina kaam mat karo — ye tumhari safety net hai. Dependencies ko requirements.txt me declare karo aur setup.py ko sirf packaging tak rakho — setup.py me extra kaam karna distribution me problems lata hai.
